author: hwisoo-kim
body:
## Summary

First piece of the UI issue hunter (Phase 28). **No model is involved anywhere in this PR** — it is the hands and the senses. You hand it a JSON list of clicks and keystrokes; it performs them on the real app and reports what broke.

`docs/design/harness-engineering.md:1130-1133` already names this as the next surface: the CLI hunter cannot reach Canvas rendering, CRDT collaboration or frontend interaction, which is where most currently-open UI bugs live.

### `__WB_HUNT__` — the sensor

Sheets, docs and slides render to **Canvas**, so the accessibility tree covers the React chrome and essentially nothing else. The standard web-agent approach (snapshot the a11y tree, reason about it) is blind to the actual product. The bridge replaces it with a closed registry of named readers the page answers about itself — including the cell-centre lookup that is the only way to click something existing purely as pixels.

A registry rather than an evaluate-arbitrary-JS hook, so the model-driven caller in a later PR stays bounded by reviewed code.

### `/harness/hunt` — the target

Mounts the real engines over `MemStore`/`MemDocStore` and hangs the real `DocsFormattingToolbar` off the editor. Toolbars are where a large share of real defects live, and neither existing harness route can reach one (`visual` mounts scenes read-only, `interaction` mounts a bare grid). Nothing here can touch real data because there is no backend to touch.

### Three decisions worth reviewing

**The driver lives under `packages/frontend`, not `scripts/agent`.** Verified both ways rather than assumed: `import('playwright')` resolves from the former and throws `ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND` from the latter. Duplicating the dep would also duplicate a version that `run-browser-tests-docker.sh` pins against `Dockerfile.playwright`. Spawning it as a subprocess additionally keeps the async browser behind a synchronous call, so `hunt-probe.mjs`'s `replay()` is **reused unchanged** instead of rewritten.

**The clock is deliberately NOT frozen.** Pinning `Date.now()` is the obvious determinism move and it changes application behaviour — the sheets mobile-edit panel dismisses on `Date.now() - openedAt < 500`, always `0` under a frozen clock. A hunter that manufactures defects with its own instrumentation is worse than no hunter. Measured instead: three attempts of the same plan are byte-identical. Volatile values are handled in `uiObservedKey`, layered on the shared `scrubVolatile`; one UI-specific rule was needed because `generateBlockId()` is `block-${Date.now()}-n`, so the same read gave `block-1785735868118-3` and `block-1785735870911-3`. Only the timestamp is scrubbed — the ordinal is real signal.

**The route is DEV-only, unlike the three harness routes beside it.** Mounting the real toolbar makes it a second separately-split importer, and a production build gained **seven** chunks (147 → 154, with main at exactly the limit): the route plus `docs-view`, `docx-actions`, `use-mobile`, `button`, `IconHash`, `IconPalette` hoisted out of the docs route chunk. That changes the download shape of a user-facing route to serve a page no user can reach. Gated behind `import.meta.env.DEV`, the production bundle is **unchanged at 147** — no budget bump needed. The lanes are unaffected: they all run against in-process `vite` dev servers.

### The oracles get their own lane

An oracle that silently stops firing is invisible — a run with no findings and a run with a dead detector produce the same empty report. `verify-hunt-oracles.mjs` runs 9 checks: 6 positive (each oracle fires on an injected fault) and 3 negative. Faults are injected from the driver, so no test-only branch ships in the harness route.

The negative controls earned their keep immediately. `network-fail` correctly ignored the absent backend — but the browser logs its *own* `Failed to load resource: net::ERR_FAILED` console error, so `console-error` reported it anyway. In Tier 1, where there is no backend by construction, every API call the app makes would have been a finding. The origin rule now applies to messages *about* requests too.

### Incidental finding

Issue #343 ("increasing font size on a mixed-size selection resets to the minimum") appears to be **already fixed** and left open. `font-size-picker.tsx:80-92` carries a guard whose comment describes the bug exactly, landed in #358 (a *slides* PR). Confirmed empirically through this harness: the sizes stay `[11,18,32]`. Not touched here — flagging it for whoever wants to close the issue.

## Test plan

- `cd scripts/agent && node --test *.test.mjs` — 519 pass (27 new)
- `pnpm verify:self` — 11/11 lanes
- `pnpm verify:hunt:oracles` — 9/9 (also wired into `verify-browser-lanes.mjs`, so it runs in `verify:browser:docker`)
- **All ten safety guards mutation-tested** — each fails when its guard is removed. Two survived initially; both were faults in my mutation harness, not vacuous tests.
- Determinism: 3 attempts of the same plan produce byte-identical observations.
- End-to-end: a scripted plan drives both surfaces, reads engine state through the bridge, and clicks a real toolbar button.

author: nunoamaral-hue
body:
## Root cause
The final credentialed VALIDATE_LOGIN returned `UNAVAILABLE / validation_runner_unavailable` in 0.37s. The Agent (`NT SERVICE\GuvFXBetaAgent`, least-privilege) could not **trigger** the `GvfxValidationRunner` task: its default security descriptor grants the *run* right to **Administrators + SYSTEM only**, so the Agent's COM `task.Run()` was denied → `SCHED_S_TASK_HAS_NOT_RUN (0x00041303)`. The runner never launched (no MT5, no broker contact). Not a code/GUI/credential fault — a deployment task-permission gap.

## Fix
`install_validation_runner.ps1` now grants the Agent service SID **READ+EXECUTE (mask `0x1200a9`)** on the task via the Task Scheduler COM security descriptor — **exactly** mirroring `install_pool.ps1`'s grant on the `GuvFXBetaRuntime-*` slot tasks the Agent already triggers: same mask, idempotent (prior ACE removed first), read-back-verified to be exactly the run mask and nothing broader. Least privilege (read + run only; no write/delete/change-permissions; no Administrator). The installer is now authoritative — no manual post-fix.

## Scope
PowerShell installer only; ASCII-only (RULE-9). No Python runtime change — the runtime path (`win.run_task`, `TaskLaunchLoginValidator`, handoff) is unchanged and already covered by the existing tests. Verified by RULE-9 parse-gate + credential-free host certification (Agent triggers the task → runner runs). No broker login.

body:
## 摘要

本 PR 对仓库质量与一致性做了以下收口：

- **隐私一致性**：把实施计划中的维护者本机路径替换为 `<skill-repo-root>` / `<codex-home>` 占位符。
- **词汇表冲突**：把工作留痕和面试模板的文档级 `evidence_status` 改为 `evidence_review`，避免与逐条证据枚举冲突。
- **防护缺口**：忽略不应入库的 `.skillhub.json`。
- **文档链接**：安装指引改为官方 Codex Skills 文档地址。
- **可信校验**：新增结构校验器、8 个行为回归测试和 GitHub Actions 工作流；严格解析 `SKILL.md` frontmatter 与 `agents/openai.yaml`，拒绝非法 YAML、重复键、错误结构和错误类型。
- **依赖边界**：`PyYAML==6.0.3` 只用于开发与 CI。Skill 本身仍然是零运行时依赖。

旧校验器用正则和关键词搜索模拟 YAML 解析，导致损坏的 `SKILL.md` 或 `agents/openai.yaml` 仍可能返回 `Skill is valid.`。现在统一使用拒绝重复键的安全 YAML Loader，并通过无状态接口 `validate(repo_root) -> list[str]` 返回可定位错误。

- `python -m pip install -r requirements-dev.txt`

body:
💡 What: 
- Use `@classmethod def setUpClass(cls)` in `tests/test_ux_css.py` to read and cache `main.css`.
- Ensure tests fail explicitly with `FileNotFoundError` if the CSS file is missing.
- Also fixed a test flakiness issue in `test_generate_placeholder_cutouts.py` by calling `cache_clear()` on `_font` method, although this fix isn't the primary focus.

🎯 Why: 
- Reading the exact same static file in every single test method causes redundant and slow disk I/O operations. As test suites scale, this bloats execution time. 
- Silently skipping tests if `main.css` is missing can mask real issues during CI (e.g. build step failures). Failing with an error ensures we catch these build problems early.

📊 Impact: 
- Eliminates redundant file reads of `main.css` across tests inside `TestUXCSS`.
- Makes test runs noticeably faster over a large test suite.

author: hychou0515
body:
Two things a chat someone shared with me couldn't tell me, both in the chat-first App rail (`ChatListRail`).

## 1. Who shared it

A shared row rendered its title and nothing else, so *"From a teammate"* read like a chat I'd forgotten writing. The code claimed otherwise —

```
/* Rename / Share / Delete only for chats I own; a shared-with-me chat just
   shows the "shared" tag (the backend would 403 those actions anyway). */
```

— and a `.chat-rail__shared` chip rule shipped in `chat-rail.css`, but **no element ever carried the class**: dead CSS behind a comment that described a feature that was never wired.

Replaced with the fact that actually identifies the row — a quiet second line naming the owner, who *is* the sharer (Share is an owner-only action, so nobody else can put a chat in your rail). Reuses `UserChip` (`nameOnly`) so a raw user id never reaches the UI.

## 2. The tab jumped back to "My chats"

The tab was `useState<"mine" | "shared">("mine")` — plain state in a component that is **destroyed on every navigation**. `AppWorkspaceInner` renders `<Msg>Loading…</Msg>` in place of the entire workspace, rail included, whenever `useAppItem` hasn't answered yet (a plain `useQuery`, no seeding from the already-fetched list — `useResources.ts:57`), which is every first visit to a chat.

So picking a chat out of "Shared with me" dropped you back on "My chats", with the chat you were now reading absent from the list in front of you. A reload did the same.

The tab is now **derived from the chat you're in**, with a click overriding it only while you stay in that chat:

```ts
const [picked, setPicked] = useState<{ chat: string; tab: Tab } | null>(null);
const tab = picked?.chat === currentId ? picked.tab : defaultTab(shared, currentId);
```

Derived state survives the remount *and* a reload with nothing persisted — the same "let the URL/route be the source of truth" fix as the KB-chat remount key. With no chat open (the App home passes `currentId=""`) it stays "My chats".

## Tests

Four added to `ChatListRail.test.tsx`; the two that pin the behaviour above fail on `master`:

- names who shared each chat in the Shared with me tab ← **red before**
- says nothing about sharing on my own chats
- opens on Shared with me when the chat you're in is one shared with you ← **red before**
- still lets you cross to the other tab from a shared chat

## Verification

- `tsc --noEmit` clean
- full FE suite: **338 files / 2708 tests passed**
- `pnpm run build` clean
- **Real Chromium layout check** — `.chat-rail__item` went from a horizontal flex row to a column, which touches *every* rail row, and happy-dom does no layout. Measured at 240px: my own chats stay a single 36.1px line, shared rows grow to 54.2px, the "Shared by" line sits below the title and stays unbolded on the active row, and both a long title and a long sharer name ellipsize with `overflowingRight: []` and no sideways scroll.

> Note: `@marp-team/marp-core` is declared in `web/package.json` but missing from the main checkout's `node_modules` — 37 test files fail to import there until `pnpm install` is re-run. Pre-existing, unrelated to this change.

author: jasadams
body:
Closes KYO-239

## Summary

Doc comments across the `server_fns` layer said `Mirrors <thing> in apps/server/src/routes/<file>.rs`. Fifteen of those route files were deleted wholesale during the React→Leptos migration and the comments were never swept.

The claim isn't merely stale, it's actively misleading. The standing rule is that server fns and REST routes *share* logic rather than duplicate it — so a reader honouring that rule goes looking for the route, doesn't find it, and has to guess whether it moved or died. That guess is where duplication comes back.

All 15 targets were deleted in three commits on 2026-04-22 — `60e6f56c` (#181), `0f9390b5` (#182), `13e957e1` (#183), all KYO-73. Every case was "route deleted, server fn is now the only implementation": no moves, no renames, and no deleted route turned out to still have a live caller.

## Three commits, by area

Per the ticket's instruction not to batch, each was separately reviewed and signed:

| Commit | Area | Refs |
|---|---|---|
| `59a5a847` | watches | 25 |
| `c0b857bc` | auth family (`auth`, `auth_password`, `auth_totp`, `auth_recovery`) | 25 |
| `125bdd23` | everything else (10 route files) | 38 |

## The counts moved since the ticket was written

The ticket says 96 stale references across 16 files. On current `main` it was **88 across 15** — `watches.rs` 25 (was 27), `workspaces.rs` 11 (was 13), `chat.rs` 9 (was 12), most likely KYO-193's server-fn deletions. There are also **40** valid references across **8** live route files, not 31/7: `push.rs` is newer than the ticket. All 40 are untouched.

## Comments were rewritten, not deleted

Where a comment was pure redundancy under a summary that already said the same thing, it's gone. Where it carried behavioural detail phrased as a comparison, the detail survives as a statement about *this* code:

- `disable_totp` deliberately doesn't require re-entering a TOTP code. That was recorded as a note about what the REST handler did; it now says what this function does and why. It was the only written record of the decision.
- `get_thinking_events` notes the deleted route wrapped this data in an envelope object.
- `AlertItem` now states the fact it was reaching for — `execution_trace` is always populated here, unlike on `WatchExecutionItem`.
- `get_websocket_config` pinned its 15 minutes to a deleted file; it now points at `jwt.access_token_expire_minutes`, where the number actually comes from.

Two module docs named live and dead routes in one breath. Only the dead halves were rewritten — `auth.rs` still calls the same service layer as `auth_google_oauth.rs`, `security.rs` still shares with `auth_passkeys.rs`, and both claims were verified true.

## Three follow-ups filed

Two comments were the only record of something worth keeping, so they became tickets rather than vanishing with the reference that carried them:

- **KYO-300** — `SampleDataIndexer::index_sample_data` and helpers (~150 lines) have zero callers. Its only caller was the route deleted in #183; `create_sample_datasource` uses a different generic indexer.
- **KYO-301** — `merge_custom_settings`/`custom_settings_get` are written twice, once per crate. The comment justified that by a route→auth-crate dependency that no longer exists.
- **KYO-302** — 14 comments make the same parity claim in *prose* without the path (`// matches REST handler validation`), so they escape this ticket's audit regex entirely. Zero MISSING does **not** mean the codebase is free of stale parity claims.

## Verification

- Audit command returns **zero MISSING**, with all 40 live references intact
- Comment-only, proven per commit: `git diff --cached -U0 | grep '^[+-]' | grep -v '^[+-][+-]' | grep -vE '^[+-]\s*(///|//!|//|\*|/\*)'` → empty
- `cargo check --workspace --locked` — clean
- `cargo clippy --locked --workspace --exclude kyomi-desktop --all-targets -- -D warnings -A clippy::unwrap_used` — clean

Those two passing is the point rather than a formality: this diff cannot affect behaviour, so a failure would mean something other than a comment got touched.

author: federicodecillia
body:
Two Vercel "failed deployment" emails arrive every Monday morning. Neither touches production: `main` is READY on both `porta-moneta` and `wegrocery-demo`. They are **preview** builds of Dependabot PRs.

## What is happening

The majors triaged and closed on Friday (#114 Next 16, #115 dev toolchain) came back this morning at 04:26 UTC as #120 and #121. Closing a Dependabot PR without an ignore rule only postpones it to the next weekly run, so this repeats indefinitely: two red previews and two emails, every Monday.

## The two failures, verified from the build logs

**#120 — Next 16.** Turbopack fails on:

```
Export ShippingMode doesn't exist in target module
The export ShippingMode was not found in module lib/actions/admin.ts [app-rsc]
```

`lib/actions/admin.ts` is a `"use server"` module that re-exported a type. A type-only export leaves nothing behind at runtime for the actions manifest to resolve. Next 15 tolerates it; Turbopack in 16 does not. Nothing imported `ShippingMode` from there — it is declared in `lib/shipping.ts` and read from there everywhere — so the re-export was dead weight that cost a build error. Removed, with a comment so it does not come back.

**#121 — dev toolchain.** This one could never have installed:

```
npm error Could not resolve dependency:
npm error peer eslint@"^7.23.0 || ^8.0.0 || ^9.0.0" from eslint-config-next@15.5.15
```

`eslint-config-next@15` peer-requires eslint ^9, and the group bumped eslint to 10 while `eslint-config-next` sat in `major-next`. The two are peer-coupled and cannot move in separate groups. That is a defect in the grouping config from #109; the config now records the constraint.

## The fix

`next`, `eslint-config-next`, `eslint`, `typescript` and `@types/node` majors go into Dependabot's `ignore` list. They are already tracked in #110 (Next 16) and #111 (toolchain), so nothing is lost — lifting an entry is part of doing that upgrade, not a separate decision. Routine minors and patches keep flowing, and security advisories still arrive as alerts regardless of `ignore`.

## Verification

- `npx tsc --noEmit` — clean
- `npm run test` — 106 passed, 14 files
- `npm run build` — succeeds

Closes #120 and #121 once merged (closing them by hand is what caused this loop).

author: diegohaz
nelsong6
body:
The Run bar said everything in words. The phase — where you ARE in the Run — sat as the
smallest text on it, hanging off the progress chip, while three ideas that recur on every
Run screen forever had no visual vocabulary at all.

## The bar

- **The screen-name line becomes a route.** `TitleBarConfig.routeSlot` renders one bounded
  portal after the screen name; `<TitleBarSlot region="route">` fills it. The Run screen
  contributes its phase there, so the line reads `Run › Shop`. Phase is document state, not
  address, so it is contributed rather than derived in `titleBarConfig`. Orientation copy,
  never a control.
- **One chip, and measures with no box.** The bar keeps exactly one framed chip — the
  identity it cannot draw: the War's name over the authored name of the Battle you are at.
  Everything else is a MEASURE, an icon and its number sitting bare on the bar. At compact
  widths the named chip is the wide element and sheds first; all four measures survive.
- **Ataraxia is an emblem and a rung.** The tier is ADR-0363's carved rung numeral, resolved
  from that installed set through a shared `ataraxiaNumeral.ts` the Enchiridion ladder now
  reads too. The emblem in front of it says which ladder that rung belongs to — the ladder's
  own section can drop it because its heading names Ataraxia, a title bar cannot.
- Conflict and Battle each own a typed `run-progress-icon` role.

## The art

Twelve PixelLab candidates, palette-locked to the accepted ui-kit icons. Two things the
generator did not give them, both baked by a new `scripts/bake-icon-stroke.mjs`:

- **A stroke.** The palette lock stripped the black keyline every accepted ui-kit icon
  carries (theirs measure 1–25 luma at the silhouette; these came back 30–98), so the marks
  dissolved into the bar. A 2px OUTER stroke — an inner one only eats the sprite's own mass,
  which against a mid-dark wall reads as less.
- **A trim.** A 64×64 canvas is a frame, not a size, and these filled it by anywhere from 20
  to 62 pixels. That dead canvas is invisible per-icon padding, and no CSS gap can fix it.
  Each mark is now cropped to its ink and padded to the square that bounds it, so one seat
  draws them all the same. Crop and pad only — no resampling, bytes stay native 1×.

`run-progress-icon` and `run-resource-icon` therefore accept any square 16–64px raster whose
runtime frame equals its own side. Historical full-frame rasters stay valid: they are the
case where the ink already filled the frame. Unit-ability and card-property icons keep their
exact 64×64 contract.

The gold coin is the fourth mark in the same row, so it goes through the same pass.

## The review

`/studio?runProgressIconReview=1` mounts every candidate in the SAME measure row the live bar
paints. Install records approval of the exact bytes, accepts the version, then binds the
`app-ui` role — in that order, because the public drawable catalog refuses a role bound to a
slot with no accepted version.

## Tooltip primitive

Every measure names itself through the shared `Tooltip`. Being its first title-bar consumer
surfaced three defects in the primitive, all fixed generally:

- A portalled overlay is excluded from the bar's `position: relative` rule. Forced relative,
  a tip landed at its flow position instead of beside its mark.
- The pop beds on an installed opaque surface under the role's tint. The tint alone is
  translucent — right on a panel with a surface behind it, wrong for chrome over live
  artwork, where the backdrop tinted the type and made one treatment read as two.
- The pop's body is always an element. Callers pass a plain string, and a bare text node
  cannot be lifted above the tip's own fills.

ADR-0366.

## Validation

- `cd frontend && npm run check` — exit 0, 2417 tests.
- `cd backend && npm run test:backend` — every unit suite and the DB-free smokes pass
  (`liveMediaPolicy` 32, netplay, solve-worker, sse-route). Its `smoke-test.js` tail needs
  Postgres, which this box has none of, so that one did not run.
- `npm run verify:titlebar` at 1280×800 and 740×430.

body:
This PR contains the following updates:

| Package | Change | [Age](https://docs.renovatebot.com/merge-confidence/) | [Confidence](https://docs.renovatebot.com/merge-confidence/) |
|---|---|---|---|
| [js-yaml](https://redirect.github.com/nodeca/js-yaml) | [`4.2.0` → `4.3.0`](https://renovatebot.com/diffs/npm/js-yaml/4.2.0/4.3.0) | ![age](https://developer.mend.io/api/mc/badges/age/npm/js-yaml/4.3.0?slim=true) | ![confidence](https://developer.mend.io/api/mc/badges/confidence/npm/js-yaml/4.2.0/4.3.0?slim=true) |

---

### js-yaml: YAML merge-key chains can force quadratic CPU consumption
[CVE-2026-59869](https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2026-59869) / [GHSA-52cp-r559-cp3m](https://redirect.github.com/advisories/GHSA-52cp-r559-cp3m)

<details>
<summary>More information</summary>

#### Details
##### Impact

js-yaml can spend quadratic CPU time parsing a document whose size grows only linearly. The issue is triggered by a chain of mappings where each mapping merges the previous one:

```yaml
a0: &a0 { k0: 0 }
a1: &a1 { <<: *a0, k1: 1 }
a2: &a2 { <<: *a1, k2: 2 }
a3: &a3 { <<: *a2, k3: 3 }
...
b: *aN
```

For each new mapping, the loader has to enumerate the keys inherited from the previous mapping. With N chained mappings, this results in roughly 1 + 2 + ... + N merged-key visits, i.e., O(N^2) work for O(N) input size.

##### PoC

From N = 4000 delay become > 1s (doc size < 100K)

```js
import { performance } from 'node:perf_hooks'
import { Buffer } from 'node:buffer'
import { load, YAML11_SCHEMA } from 'js-yaml'

const n = Number(process.argv[2] || 4000)

function makeMergeChain (count) {
  const lines = ['a0: &a0 { k0: 0 }']

  for (let i = 1; i < count; i++) {
    lines.push(`a${i}: &a${i} { <<: *a${i - 1}, k${i}: ${i} }`)
  }

  lines.push(`b: *a${count - 1}`)
  return `${lines.join('\n')}\n`
}

const source = makeMergeChain(n)

console.log(source.split('\n').slice(0, 8).join('\n'))
console.log('...')
```

author: skiptix
body:
An MCP client (and Sol, and an agent run) could **read** a workspace's Knowledge Base but could not **create or edit** one. Reproduced against the live instance before fixing:

```
list_knowledge_terms(ws_…)  → "This workspace has no Knowledge Base terms defined yet."
create_knowledge_entry(…)   → Error: this workspace has no Knowledge Base yet —
                              add one from the sidebar first
```

Three independent gaps closed the loop off. Each still typechecked and still returned `ok`, which is why none of them showed up as a failure.

## What was broken

**1. No tool could create a base.** Every write path bottomed out in `requireWritableBase`, which told the caller to use the sidebar — an instruction an MCP client cannot follow.

**2. No tool ever returned an `entry_id`.** `update_knowledge_entry`, `delete_knowledge_entry` and `link_knowledge_entry` all require one, but `list_knowledge_terms` formatted terms without it, `lookup_knowledge` omitted it, and `create_knowledge_entry` returned only the term. So editing was unreachable *even in a workspace that already had a base*.

**3. `update_knowledge_entry` could not touch the body.** It accepted only term/summary/aliases/type, so a definition could never actually be revised — only its metadata.

## Changes

- **New `create_knowledge_base` tool.** Idempotent, per `createBase()`'s existing contract: a second call returns the existing base rather than erroring, so two callers racing it converge instead of one failing. Requires workspace **membership**, not the looser access the read tools take — same asymmetry `routes/knowledgeBase.ts` enforces.
- **`entry_id` surfaced** in `list_knowledge_terms`, `lookup_knowledge`, and `create_knowledge_entry`'s result.
- **`update_knowledge_entry` gains `body`**, applied through `knowledgeBase/blocks.ts`'s `mutateEntryBlocks` rather than a bare content write — so an AI edit runs the same post-save pipeline a human edit does: inline `[[…]]` link sync, `@`-mention notifications, image pruning, embedding enqueue. An empty string clears the body; omitting the field leaves it untouched (this is why `str()` is deliberately not used to read it — `str()` maps `''` to `undefined`).
- **`list_knowledge_terms` stops conflating "no base" with "a base with no terms."** The two have different fixes and only one is actionable.
- `requireWritableBase`'s error now names the tool that resolves it instead of pointing at a UI the caller doesn't have.

Security invariant is unchanged: `userId` still comes only from the verified credential, there is no `user_id` tool parameter, reads need workspace access and writes need workspace membership, and an entry in an unreachable workspace still reports as *absent* rather than forbidden.

## Tests

New `backend/src/__tests__/knowledgeBaseAiTools.test.ts` (16 tests) walks the exact loop an MCP client takes with no UI available — create base → list → get `entry_id` → revise body — plus the membership boundary, the idempotent second create, empty-body-clears vs field-omitted, and body-write failure surfacing instead of a partial success.

```
backend: 41 files, 483 tests passed · tsc --noEmit clean
```

## Docs

`CLAUDE.md` / `GEMINI.md` / `.antigravity.md` updated identically (per the repo's synchronization rule; verified the bodies are byte-identical after their differing headers): tool count 20 → 21, and a new standing note that Knowledge Base tools must stay self-sufficient for a caller with no UI — a tool that says "add one from the sidebar first" is a dead end to the caller that most needs it. Version bumped to v1.73.1.

author: edv4h
body:
## 概要

プラグインが独自の UI シェル（ツールバー・プロパティバー・パネル）を実装するのを禁止し、**UI は必ず HUD に登録する**方針を `docs/plugin-system-design.md` に明文化しました。

`ctx.layers.register({ fixed: true })` に React コンポーネントを載せて浮かぶコントロールを描く、という現状よく使われているパターンが対象です。

| 提供したいもの | 登録先 |
| --- | --- |
| 操作 | `ctx.actions.register` |
| 設定値 | `ctx.hud.registerSettings` |
| 選択に追従するコンテキストUI | `ctx.hud.registerContextual`（**未実装**） |
| 計測値などの独自表示 | `ctx.hud.registerPanel` |

## なぜ

1. **`order` が手管理のグローバル名前空間になっている。** 実際に衝突しており、`shape-connector` の labelEditor と `domain-design` のプロパティバーは 82〜84 を手作業で調整しています
2. **各プラグインが色・影・フォントを直書きする。** テーマもデザイントークンも効かず、バーごとに見た目がずれます
3. **UI 都合の定数がドメインロジックに漏れる。** 「ツールバーが被らないよう余白を広げる」といった調整がロジック側に残ります
4. **キャンバスのイベント遮断を各プラグインが個別に書く。** 抜けたものからバグになります

## 対象外

背景・ガイド・ワールド座標に紐づく装飾など、**キャンバスそのものの描画**は従来どおりレイヤー登録です。境界は「ワールドを描いているか / コントロールを置いているか」。

## 補足

- `ctx.hud.registerContextual` はまだありません。HUD 側の拡張として別途 Issue を立てます。それまで新規実装は actions / settings で代替してください
- 既存の `fixed: true` UI は複数残っています。`registerContextual` 実装後に個別 Issue で移行する想定で、本 PR では移行しません
- ドキュメントのみの変更です

author: genezhang
body:
## Summary

Extends #629 (references it; #629 already closed). #629 shipped the uncorrelated `size([f IN list WHERE (pattern)])` arrayCount render **gated to a single directed hop with the iteration var at START**. This adds two more single-hop shapes that previously failed loud:

| Shape | Membership | Was |
|---|---|---|
| **target-position** `()-[:FOLLOWS]->(f)` | `x IN (SELECT followed_id)` | failed loud |
| **undirected** `(f)-[:FOLLOWS]-()` | `x IN (SELECT follower_id UNION SELECT followed_id)` | failed loud |
| incoming-start `(f)<-[:FOLLOWS]-()` | `x IN (SELECT followed_id)` | already worked |
| start-outgoing `(f)-[:FOLLOWS]->()` | `x IN (SELECT follower_id)` | unchanged |

## Root cause

`list_element_col` was hardcoded to hop-0's from-side (`pattern_comprehension_sql.rs`), so a target-position iteration var read the wrong column.

## Fix

- New `find_iteration_var_position(pattern_hops, var) -> Vec<(hop_idx, is_start_side)>` locates where the iteration variable sits; the element column is derived from that via `find_edge_id_column` (which flips start/end for `Incoming` internally).
- Undirected: an early branch emits `SELECT <from_col> ... UNION SELECT <to_col> ...` inside the membership subquery. Databricks keeps the explode form with the UNION living in the WHERE-`IN` (allowed — only HOF *lambdas* forbid subqueries in Spark).
- Gate `uncorrelated_list_pattern_is_render_safe` (`with_clause.rs`) relaxed **in lockstep**: allow `Outgoing|Incoming|Either`, var at start OR end.

## Still fails loud (correctness over coverage)

- **Multi-hop** — deferred to a follow-up PR: anonymous intermediate nodes have unknown labels, so an ambiguous rel-type can silently pick the wrong edge table.
- **Self-loop** `(f)-[:R]->(f)` — needs a `from = to` predicate the render doesn't emit.
- **Variable-length** — no expansion modeled.

**Load-bearing invariant:** a render `None` becomes the literal `"0"` downstream (silently-wrong count), so the plan-time gate is the ONLY safe guard — it admits only render-correct shapes.

## Verification

- SQL-shape (no live CH — bar = shape + byte goldens): all four supported shapes verified both dialects (target→followed_id, incoming→followed_id, undirected→from∪to, per-element→follower_id **byte-identical**).
- 4 new `.sql` corpus goldens + 2 `.err` (self-loop, multi-hop) + curated shape asserts + 5 `find_iteration_var_position` unit tests, fail-when-reverted.
- corpus 0-churn elsewhere; ratchet net-zero; full gate green.

Refs #629.

author: ahincho
body:
fix(workflows): revert dynamic secret lookup; restore standard cross-owner pattern

PR #232 tried to access the AWS role ARN via dynamic index from the
plan/apply-role-arn-secret input:

  role-to-assume: ${{ secrets[inputs.plan-role-arn-secret] }}

without declaring the secret in workflow_call. The premise was that
job-level `environment:` binding (PR #228) makes env-scoped secrets
available to the reusable without caller forwarding. Tested in PR #91
on spark-match-02-infrastructure — this lookup returned empty
(`AWS_PLAN_ROLE_ARN=` in the diag step env, `plan_secret_len=0`),
which confirms:

  - Dynamic indexing of the `secrets` context is not supported by the
    GitHub Actions expression engine in this context.
  - Env-scoped secrets are NOT implicitly accessible from a reusable
    workflow even when the job has `environment:` bound. The reusable
    runs in the caller repo's execution context but the `secrets`
    context inside the reusable is still scoped to the secrets
    forwarded via workflow_call.

The standard cross-owner pattern is the only thing that works:

  reusable (workflow_call.secrets):
    AWS_PLAN_ROLE_ARN: { required: true }
  reusable (step):
    role-to-assume: ${{ secrets.AWS_PLAN_ROLE_ARN }}
  caller:
    secrets:
      AWS_PLAN_ROLE_ARN: ${{ secrets.AWS_PLAN_ROLE_ARN_DEV }}

This PR restores that pattern. PR #231 (which removed the
declaration) and PR #229 (which set `required: false`) are both
overridden by this PR — they were based on the same flawed premise.

The job-level `environment:` binding from PR #228 stays. It is the
right place to enforce approval gates per env (dev / staging / prod),
independent of how the secret is forwarded.

The plan-role-arn-secret / apply-role-arn-secret inputs are kept for
backward compatibility but are now documentation-only: the validation
step still checks them, the AWS step ignores them, and the caller can
still pass them as a hint of which secret to forward. Future PRs may
remove the inputs entirely if all callers migrate to the standard
forwarding pattern.

Caller contract (after this PR):

  jobs:
    plan-dev:
      uses: spark-match/spark-match-01-devops/.github/workflows/reusable-terraform-plan.yml@main
      secrets:
        AWS_PLAN_ROLE_ARN: ${{ secrets.AWS_PLAN_ROLE_ARN_DEV }}
      with:
        environment: dev
        plan-role-arn-secret: AWS_PLAN_ROLE_ARN_DEV

spark-match-02-infrastructure PR #91 must keep the `secrets:` block in
all four callers (terraform-{plan,apply}-{dev,prod}.yml). A future PR
will update PR #91 accordingly.

author: gemisis
body:
First of a series making every Leviath TUI consistent (setup wizard here; the dashboard follows in the next PRs).

## Shared TUI kit (`crates/leviath-cli/src/tui/`)

- **`keymap.rs`** — the crate's single key → action table: arrows first with `k`/`j`/`h`/`l` aliases, Space toggles, Enter acts on the focused thing, Esc goes back, Tab/Shift-Tab step screens, `?` help, `q` quit, Ctrl-C force-quit. Surfaces match their own keys first and fall through, so a local binding can shadow an alias without touching the table.
- **`widgets/confirm.rs`** — one confirmation dialog: two visible buttons, focus starts on the safe answer, `←`/`→`/Tab move focus, Enter activates, `y`/`n` accelerate, stray keys do nothing. Replaces the "`y` accepts, anything else dismisses" pattern.
- **`widgets/help.rs`** — help overlays built from `(key, description)` tables, so the overlay cannot drift from the real bindings; closed by Esc/`q`/`?`/Enter only.
- **`widgets/footer.rs`** — the one hint bar.
- **`widgets/line_edit.rs`** — single-line editor with a real cursor (char-boundary splicing, masking, Home/End). Replaces the wizard's push/pop `String` editor.
- **`widgets/popup.rs`** — shared centered rect + cleared bordered frame.

`main.rs`'s `CrosstermSetup` now installs a chained panic hook and implements `Drop`, so a panic or early return can no longer leave the shell in raw mode. Mouse capture became per-surface: the wizard never handled mouse events, so capturing there only stole native drag-to-select.

## Setup wizard rework

Fixes the reported trap where pressing Enter on the provider list (expecting to select) silently advanced past the credentials screen and produced a zero-provider install.

- Enter on a provider/agent/MCP row now **selects** it, same as Space. Advancing is a visible `[ Continue → … ]` button at the end of every list, which names the next screen and carries state (`Continue: Credentials (2 selected)`).
- Leaving Providers with nothing selected raises a confirm (`Go back` focused / `Continue anyway`).
- Skipping the Credentials screen is announced in the footer instead of silent.
- Enter on a Defaults/Limits row always acts on that row: toggles a bool, cycles a choice, opens the editor for a number (the footer used to promise this and not do it).
- `q`/Ctrl-C with unsaved choices asks before discarding (Ctrl-C again quits unconditionally); clean state quits immediately.
- The Claude Code ToS gate is a real dialog with explicit buttons; `y`/`n` still work.
- Ctrl-R (reveal credentials) now also works while typing one.
- Docs: `lev setup` key table added to `cli.md`; `providers.md` no longer documents the Enter fall-through as behavior.

## Testing

- `cargo xtask coverage --package leviath-cli` green (100% gate).
- (The full-workspace run flaked once on `leviath-tools`' `the_shell_tool_advertises_the_shell_this_host_resolved` — a pre-existing parallel-test `SHELL` env race, unrelated to this diff; it passes in isolation.)
- Live pty verification on a fresh `LEVIATH_HOME` (both scenarios scripted end to end): zero-provider guard, Enter-selects, masked entry + mid-edit Ctrl-R reveal (a regression the live run caught), dirty-quit confirm, Ctrl-S save landing the credential in `config.toml`, clean quit writing nothing.

author: calef
body:
## What it was

`kernel::user::tests::reclaim_frees_a_started_then_exited_childs_regions` opened by probing
`reclaim_region(tcb_region).is_err()` on its own child's TCB region, over a comment that read
"the refusal leaves the region untouched".

That comment went stale when DECISIONS §16 was amended. A refusal is not passive any more:
`reap_region_objects` sets `killed = true` on every live thread in the region and *then* returns
`Err`, so an owner's retry can tear a runaway down (§24's `^C` escalation is built on it). The
comment kept compiling. The child did not survive.

From there it is a race between the child's nine instructions and its own core's next timer tick,
because `schedule()` converts a killed thread to a corpse at its next preemption:

```rust
if t.killed && t.state == State::Running { t.state = State::Finished; }
```

Lose it and the child is reaped **before it ever SENDs**, the test's `ipc_recv` never returns, every
core falls to idle, and the 60 s lost-wakeup heartbeat fires. That is the intermittent hang that kept
`cpu-matrix` red on branches that could not have caused it, including a PR with zero lines of code.

## How a one-in-four race was turned into a proof

Widening the window rather than waiting for it, the method milestone 71 used on the frame fault. A
call-free three-instruction delay loop in front of `REPORT_STUB` guarantees a preemption before the
`SEND`:

```text
riscv64   lui t0, 0x4000 ; addi t0, t0, -1 ; bne t0, x0, -4
aarch64   mov x5, #0x4000000 ; subs x5, x5, #1 ; b.ne -4
```

With the probe present that hangs the watchdog on the **first run and every run**. Temporary prints
in the two suspect lines caught the whole chain in order:

```text
[M72] child tid=0xe00000065 started
[M72] ARM kill tid=0xe00000065 state=Running
[M72] reclaim(tcb_region) -> Err(())
[M72] CONVERT killed->Finished tid=0xe00000065
WATCHDOG: no progress for ~60 s. Every core idle, every thread blocked: a lost-wakeup hang.
```

The forced dump matched all four wild occurrences exactly: **101 threads, 109 endpoints**, every
thread `wake_pending=false on_cpu=false`, all four inboxes empty. With the probe removed the same
widened child passes.

## Two corrections

**It was never a RISC-V defect.** The widened window hangs **aarch64** identically on the first run.
That is the control that rules the ISA out; the riscv64 leg simply lost the race more often under
TCG. The code is portable `sched.rs`.

**The 101 leaked threads are unrelated**, which this milestone was briefed to chase first. They are
blocked, so they add no scheduling load and no run-queue depth; 109 endpoints is a fifth of
`MAX_ENDPOINTS`; both ISAs accumulate them equally. They are still worth their own milestone (101 of
`MAX_THREADS = 128`, and `thread_leak_police` polices only *runnable* leaks), and the evidence is
recorded in `notes/scheduler.md` rather than fixed here.

## The change

- The probe is deleted. Nothing else in the kernel changed.
- `reclaim_region` grows a `BUGS` section: `Err` is destructive, and it does not read that way at a
  call site.
- `notes/scheduler.md`'s OPEN section becomes CLOSED, with the method and the evidence.
- `notes/riscv-port.md`'s BUGS paragraph is corrected: that hang was not this ISA's.
- `design/roadmap.md`: milestone 72's row and status block only.

## Gates

`script/fmt`, `script/lint`, `script/test` (217 tests, both ISAs) all green. Confirmation loop under
the original recipe (four host burners, riscv64 in a loop) attached in the lane report.

body:
Adds `src/content/posts/2026-08-17-how-i-over-engineered-my-book.mdx` — the "rabbit hole" post promised in the [Overcommitted write-up](https://ben.balter.com/2026/07/28/overcommitted-open-and-async/).

How I wrote and published [Open and Async](https://open-and-async.com) the way I ship software: Markdown in Git, ~5,500 automated checks, and a Pandoc pipeline that builds five formats on every `git push`.

## What it covers

- **Content** — chapters as Markdown in Git, drafted from an iPad via Codespaces.
- **Testing** — six real-time prose linters (Harper, Vale, LanguageTool, Alex, Write-good, markdownlint) plus a custom suite of ~30 content validators; ~5,500 automated checks across ~70 test files. Includes the GitHub-tense validator and a linter that caught my own AI cadence.
- **Audits** — three-layer duplication detection (jscpd → n-gram → semantic LLM) with the real payoff (I'd paraphrased myself across five chapters); a 20-lens LLM prose auditor led by the Claims-lens catch of a wrong GitHub stat; deterministic length/reading-time/consistency audits plus a writing dashboard.
- **Design** — "an ebook is a website in a trench coat"; the `@media` CSS leak that quietly deflated the print book 576 → 567 pages; axe-core + Playwright visual-regression tests.
- **Building** — Pandoc + WeasyPrint + Ghostscript in a pinned Docker toolchain; Lua AST filters; the Twemoji "dark box" emoji bug and its opposite fixes; PDF/X-1a for IngramSpark; a page-count gate protecting the cover spine.
- **Publishing / Looking forward** — own ISBNs, wide-not-exclusive, versioned metadata; translation + audiobook pipelines; releasing the tooling as open source.

Explicitly frames AI as an editing/QA layer ("every word is mine; these tools are readers of last resort, not writers of first resort"), not a writer. Credits all 35 open-source projects the book stands on in a footnote.

body:
## Motivation

tabcmd Classic's `--encrypt` on `createextracts` takes an explicit
`yes` or `no` value. tabcmd 2 treated it as a bare boolean flag,
silently ignoring any following value. Scripts passing `--encrypt no`
on Classic didn't fail on tabcmd 2 but produced the wrong behavior
(they either bailed on argparse or silently kept encryption on).

## Behavior change

**For users:** `--encrypt` accepts an optional `yes|no|true|false`
argument (case-insensitive).

- Bare `--encrypt` still means `True` (tabcmd 2 syntax).
- Omitted means `False`.
- Explicit `--encrypt no` (or `false`/`0`) now means `False`.

Preserves tabcmd 2's current default while accepting Classic's
yes/no syntax.

author: octalide
body:
## Summary

`targets.conf` documents that adding a leg "is one row here and touches no workflow" — true of the workflow, false of case manifests. Five real cases were added while x86_64-darwin was dropped from `targets.conf`; none declared a `[target.darwin-x86_64]` block, and they would have failed to compile the moment the leg returned — caught only because someone was actively restoring the platform at the time (#2327). The gap only surfaces at main cadence, since the darwin legs run on merge to `main` rather than per-PR, so a case added on a green PR merges and the omission is discovered later on a lane nobody is watching at that moment.

**Answered the issue's own design question first, by inspection** of all ~64 case manifests (266 case×leg pairs) rather than assumption: every case that does *not* need every `targets.conf` leg already expresses that through case.conf's existing `targets:`/`exempt:` fields, each with an explanatory comment justifying the restriction (e.g. `debuginfo`: "windows (CodeView) and darwin (Mach-O) debug info have distinct validators and are out of scope here"; `syscall-inline-asm` exempts windows because "windows has no syscall ABI"). Structural cases (spirv/bmos/freestanding/macho/pe-*) run `targets: linux` and cross-build via `build-target:` to a format entirely outside the leg namespace — a different axis, not a target-matrix gap. **No case's declared blocks disagreed with its case.conf scope anywhere in the sweep**: the existing case.conf mechanism *is* the opt-out the issue asks for, visible at the case and self-explaining already. No new opt-out syntax needed, and no policy question to escalate — the inventory came back clean, not target-limited-by-default.

**What shipped**: `int/lib/check-target-matrix.sh` — a static, fast guard mirroring `run.sh`'s own resolution exactly: for every case, for every leg in its case.conf-resolved allowlist (minus exempt), the case must declare `[target.<build-target>]` in mach.toml. Extracted that resolution (case.conf parsing, the `targets.conf` leg list, the allow/exempt computation) into a new shared `int/lib/case.sh`, sourced by both `run.sh` and the new checker — a second implementation of case.conf's key set would have been exactly the kind of drifting parallel enumeration this repo already treats as a recurring defect family. `run.sh`'s own inline case.conf reader is gone in favor of one call to `read_case_conf`.

Wired into `ci.yml`'s `int-matrix` job, which already runs on every ordinary PR (not only main cadence) and already gates `integration` via `needs:`, so a missing block fails fast before any real build time is spent on a leg that would not have compiled anyway. Also wired into `int-main.yml`'s own `int-matrix` job as a second gate before the scarce darwin runner time that workflow spends.

Closes #2353

## Verification

- **Demonstrated firing, per the bar**: removed `[target.darwin-x86_64]` from `2368-deep-nest`'s mach.toml, ran the checker — `FAIL regression/2368-deep-nest: leg 'darwin-x86_64' needs [target.darwin-x86_64] in mach.toml` — restored, `git status` clean.
- Repeated against a build-target case (`pe-import-attribution`, `build-target: windows`): removing `[target.windows]` correctly reports `FAIL surface/pe-import-attribution: leg 'linux' needs [target.windows] in mach.toml`, naming the LEG the case actually runs on and the BUILD-TARGET block it's missing as two distinct facts.
- `check-target-matrix.sh` reports 266/266 case×leg pairs OK at HEAD.
- `mach test .`: 1019 passed, 0 failed.
- Full `int/` suite unchanged on `linux` (121 cases) and `linux-riscv64` (88 cases); `linux-arm64` via #2314's `--runmode` override also unchanged (87 cases) — confirming the `case.sh` extraction is fully behavior-preserving, not just the new check.
- No `src/lang` changes; compiler binary byte-identical to the `dev` baseline it was built against.

## Test plan

- [x] Design question answered by inspection: no case disagrees with its case.conf scope; existing mechanism is the opt-out
- [x] Removing a target block from a full-6-target case: check fails naming case + target, restored, `git status` clean
- [x] Removing a target block from a build-target case: check fails naming leg + build-target correctly, restored
- [x] `check-target-matrix.sh`: 266/266 OK
- [x] `mach test .`: 1019/0/1019
- [x] Full `int/` suite green on `linux` (121), `linux-riscv64` (88), `linux-arm64` via `--runmode` (87)
- [x] Compiler binary byte-identical to `dev` baseline
- [x] CI green (both `ci.yml` and, once relevant, `int-main.yml`) before marking ready

author: twdover
body:
Movable/loopable MIDI regions (roadmap 9.2 follow-up)

A recorded MIDI take (9.1) is now tracked as an independent, draggable, loopable region on a new per-part timeline strip — distinct from the section it was recorded into. Closes 9.2's "remaining scope" open call and supersedes roadmap item 8.4 (fully covered by 9.2's existing section timeline).

Backend: four new endpoints (/save-note-region, /move-note-region/{id}, /set-note-region-loop/{id}, DELETE /note-region/{gen_id}/{id}), a new note_regions.py (pure expansion/removal math), a new production read_note_events, and _write_part_stem_and_rebuild extracted from edit_part so all four reuse the same CC/rebuild path as a hand edit.

Two correctness bugs were caught and fixed before shipping: naively reusing the rewrite path would have silently erased hand-drawn 9.3 automation on the first region move (fixed with read_part_automation, the inverse of _apply_automation_cc); and removing a region's old notes by content match, done across a whole part, could have deleted an unrelated identical-looking note (fixed by bounding every removal to the region's own window).

Frontend: PianoRollEditor.vue captures a take's region on stop; PartCard.vue registers it only after the note save itself succeeds (a failed registration degrades safely, never rolling back the save); new NoteRegionTrack.vue renders a draggable/loopable region block per part on SongResult.vue's new timeline strip.

Known v1 limits (documented, not hidden): hand-editing a note inside a region's span detaches it from the region; loop repeats are uniform copies of the canonical recorded content; regions are song-mode only and created only by recording (not promoted from existing notes).

Tests: 309 backend / 428 frontend, all green; clean vue-tsc/eslint; real-shell verified in packaged Electron via a new scenarios/note-region-move.mjs (build → take → save → move, confirmed via raw .mid bytes that notes shifted and automation survived, plus a UI bug found and fixed live — a 1-bar region on a long song was unreadably narrow).

Version bumped to 0.9.0.

author: grosmichel-dev
body:
## 1. 폴더·태그 페이지의 오른쪽 사이드바 복원

분류(`채용공고` 등)·지역(`대덕구`) 페이지에서 **그래프뷰·목차·백링크가 안 보였다.**

원인은 `quartz.config.yaml` 의 `byPageType` 오버라이드였다:

```yaml
folder:
  positions:
    right: []      # ← 폴더 페이지의 오른쪽 사이드바를 통째로 비움
tag:
  positions:
    right: []
```

`condition: not-index` 는 무죄였다. 소스를 보면 **홈 한 장만** 거른다:

```ts
// quartz/plugins/loader/conditions.ts:6
"not-index": (props) => props.fileData.slug !== "index",
```

라이브 측정이 이를 갈랐다 — 분류 페이지의 **왼쪽 사이드바는 8602자로 멀쩡한데 오른쪽만 0자**였다.
`not-index` 탓이었다면 왼쪽(탐색기·검색)도 함께 죽었어야 한다.

**조치**: `positions: right: []` 4줄만 제거. 홈은 `not-index` 가 계속 막으므로 전체폭 랜딩 그대로다.
`exclude: [reader-mode]` 는 유지(폴더·태그 페이지에 읽기모드 단추는 무의미).

## 2. 기록 문서를 `index.md` 로 저장하면 검증을 건너뛰던 구멍

작업 중 발견해 함께 막았다.

`classify.mjs` 는 이름이 `index.md` 면 **안내 페이지**로 분류하고, 안내 페이지는 `title` 만 검사한다.
그래서 기록 문서를 실수로 `index.md` 로 저장하면 **날짜·부서·출처·서명 검사를 전부 건너뛰고 공개된다.**

실제로 확인했다 — `title` 하나만 있는 문서가 `--require-published` 에서도 **종료코드 0**.

**조치**: 안내 페이지에 `source_type` 이 있으면 오류. 기록 문서 템플릿에는 반드시 `source_type` 이
들어가므로, 이 실수의 지문이 된다. 정상 안내 페이지 13개는 `title` 만 있어 영향 없다.

## 3. 문서

`docs/OBSIDIAN-SETUP.md`:

- **볼트 제외 설정**을 필수 절차로 추가. 볼트가 저장소 루트라 옵시디언이 `node_modules` 안
  패키지 README 수천 개까지 읽어, 그래프가 뒤덮이고 **`[[` 자동완성에 패키지 문서가 후보로 뜬다**(오연결 위험).
  `.obsidian/` 은 `.gitignore` 로 차단돼 저장소·사이트에 영향이 없다는 점도 명시.
- **`index.md` 가 폴더마다 있는 건 정상**이라는 설명과, 기록 문서를 그 이름으로 만들면 안 된다는 경고 추가.

## 검증

| 항목 | 결과 |
|---|---|
| `run-tests.mjs` | **82/82 PASS** (신규 가드 1건 포함) |
| 사이드바 검사 8종 | ALL OK |
| 오른쪽 사이드바 길이 | 홈 **33**(비어 있음) / 채용공고 2629 / 대덕구 3544 / how-to 4123 |
| `validate-frontmatter` (실제 content) | 종료코드 0 — 기존 `index.md` 13개 정상 |
| `quartz build` | 성공 |

목차·백링크는 **내용이 있을 때만** 렌더되는 컴포넌트라, 들어오는 링크가 없는 분류 페이지에는
그래프만 뜬다(고시공고는 백링크가 있어 함께 표시됨). 정상 동작이다.

author: patelankeet2
body:
## Summary

Adds the AI explanation layer, issue #8. `explain(finding) -> str` takes one F-1 finding and returns a plain-English explanation, grounded strictly in that finding, using a local model through Ollama. No config data leaves the machine.

- `ai/Modelfile` - a custom model (`netwise-warden`, built on `llama3.2:3b`) with a system prompt and generation parameters tuned toward being as literal as possible
- `ai/explain.py` - the calling code, plus a deterministic computation for one specific reasoning task that a language model should not be trusted with (see below), plus a post-generation safety net
- `tests/test_explain_safety_net.py` - 27 tests for all of the above, none need Ollama or Docker

## Acceptance criteria (issue #8)

- [x] Given a finding, the local AI returns an accurate explanation grounded in that finding, e.g. "websites are blocked," not "port 80 is denied."

Verified against real pipeline output throughout, never invented findings. Full detail below, since the point of this section is that you can check my claims, not just read them.

## Why this took three commits, not one

I did not accept the first version that produced reasonable-looking output. I stress-tested it, found two genuinely different classes of real problem, and fixed each properly rather than patching around it. Recording that here because it is exactly the kind of thing worth other people's eyes on, not because a clean-looking PR needed padding.

**Problem 1: the model stating an unconfirmed result as fact.** For a `status="error"` finding (a check that crashed, nothing about the network was actually confirmed), the model said "The HQ LAN cannot reach the Branch LAN." That is precisely the F-4 failure this whole project exists to prevent, confusing "we could not check" with "we checked and it's bad." Fixed with a required response shape for error findings plus a post-generation check: if the response still claims a result about the network, retry once, then fall back to a fixed, non-generated sentence. Verified: 3/3 clean on a genuinely different real error (from `tests/fixtures/unparseable`, not the one used while tuning).

**Problem 2: the model getting ACL shadowing logic backwards.** Tested against Batfish's own bundled 13-device `example` network (not our small fixtures) by running our real `access_control` check code against it unmodified. For a dead ACL rule (an unreachable `PERMIT`, shadowed by an earlier `DENY`), the model said matching traffic "should be blocked... which is not happening" - backwards. The traffic IS blocked; that's the entire finding. No wording filter catches this, the sentence used no banned word, it was simply wrong about which rule wins.

This is not a translation problem, it is a deterministic logic problem, so I moved it out of the model's hands entirely. `_compute_dead_rule_outcome()` parses `evidence.detail` and computes the real outcome in Python: whichever rule shadows the dead one decides, the dead rule's own action never applies. It only fires when it can be fully confident (a single, recognisable blocking rule); anything ambiguous, it leaves alone rather than guessing. The model is handed the computed fact to state, not a question to reason about.

First test round fixed the direction completely (6/6 correct across both real dead-rule findings) but surfaced a smaller issue: the model echoed the injected fact's label verbatim as its own paragraph. Fixed by removing the distinctive label text (same lesson as an earlier fix: a 3B model copies salient text more readily than it parses instructions about it). Re-tested: second round, 6/6 clean, correctly grounded, no label echo.

Also found the same finding's evidence exposed a hedge-word variant of an earlier invented-consequence problem ("...which could potentially cause issues" - nothing banned by name, still speculation with no basis in the evidence), this time on a `found` finding, not just `error`. Generalised the safety net to check every status, since CLAUDE.md's grounding constraint isn't scoped to one status, with a plain, always-grounded fallback for `found`/`none` if the model still speculates twice in a row.

## Full test log, so feedback has something concrete to react to

Every explanation below came from `explain()` directly, live, not edited or cherry-picked for this PR. The exact scripts used are all in the commit history if anyone wants to rerun them.

**`status="found"`, real finding (`AC-001`, `rtr-us5-insecure`):**
> "The device's rule set currently allows all traffic through with no restriction, which is what let unencrypted web traffic reach the internal server."

**`status="none"`, real finding (`AC-000`, `rtr-us5-secure`):**
> "Access control was checked and nothing wrong was found: the required traffic rules hold, no rule silently fails to work, and every access list reference points to something that actually exists."

**`status="error"`, real finding (`AC-000`, `unparseable` fixture, a genuinely different error than the one used while tuning):**
> "This check could not be completed, so nothing is confirmed about the current access control configuration. The underlying analysis tool encountered an issue parsing the device's configuration file..."
Ran 3 times, all 3 passed the safety net on the first attempt.

**Dead ACL rule, real finding from Batfish's bundled `example` network (dead `DENY`, correct outcome: traffic permitted):**
> "...it actually does not have any impact on incoming traffic because another rule (the 'permit ip any 2.128.0.0 0.0.255.255' rule) takes precedence and allows all traffic through with the specified IP address range."

**Dead ACL rule, same network (dead `PERMIT`, correct outcome: traffic denied, the case that was previously backwards):**
> "...even though the 'allow ICMP traffic' rule exists, it is effectively ignored due to being overshadowed by the blocking rule."

**Undefined reference, same network:**
> "The device's configuration refers to a route map called 'filter-bogons' that is not actually defined. This means that the network has a rule set that mentions this non-existent route map, but it does not provide any information about what actions should be taken when this route map is applied."

## Known limitations, stated plainly rather than left implicit

- This is a 3B model on CPU (no dedicated GPU on this machine). It is not perfect on every single run, that's exactly why the post-generation safety net exists rather than trusting the prompt alone. If anyone wants to push explanation quality further, the model size in `ai/Modelfile`'s `FROM` line is the first thing I'd revisit, everything downstream of it stays the same.
- Input direction (a plain-English question mapped to a Batfish query) is not in this PR. That's issues #11 and #13, a different shape of problem, deliberately kept separate rather than bundled in here.
- `explain()` is not wired into the dashboard yet. That touches `web/main.py`, and I didn't want to make that call solo, see the question below.

## Asking for feedback specifically to make Warden more accurate

Everything above was found by testing against findings from my own checks and one Batfish sample network. That's a narrow slice. If you run `explain()` against findings from `policy_compliance` (Shubham) or, once #25 lands, `routing` (mine), or anything from the dashboard's mock data, there's a real chance it turns up a case I haven't seen, the two bugs in this PR were both found exactly that way, by feeding it something new rather than trusting the first version that looked fine.

What's actually useful feedback here, concretely:

- Any sentence that states something not traceable back to `evidence.detail` or `summary`, an invented cause, an invented consequence, a made-up number.
- Any case where the explanation gets the actual technical direction wrong (like the shadowing bug in this PR), not just awkward phrasing.
- Any `status="error"` explanation that states or implies a result a

author: retrohazard
body:
## The problem

The `website` path filter is a plain prefix match:

```bash
printf 'website=%s\n' "$(match '^website/')"
```

It cannot tell a Cypress spec from a bundle source, and `web-deploy` gated on it. So editing a test rebuilt and shipped the site — #131 changed two `.cy.js` files and nothing else, and deployed production ([run 30867860626](https://github.com/RetroHazard/CloudResume/actions/runs/30867860626)).

That isn't free. The second `aws s3 sync` compares mtime, so a freshly built `index.html` is re-uploaded even when byte-identical, and an `ObjectCreated` on `index.html` is what enqueues the `cloudfrontInvalidation` Lambda. A test-only edit paid for a full rebuild and a CDN invalidation to ship bytes that hadn't changed.

## The change

Splits the question in two rather than narrowing the existing output, because the checks and the deploy want genuinely different answers:

| Output | Scope | Gates |
|---|---|---|
| `website` | unchanged — `^website/` | `web-checks`, `web-e2e`, marker upload |
| `website_deployable` | **new** — excludes `cypress/`, `cypress.config.js`, `src/__tests__/` | `web-deploy` only |

**A build still runs the tests.** `web-deploy` has `needs: [web-checks, web-e2e]`, and those gate on the broad `website`, so narrowing the deploy trigger cannot let an untested bundle ship.

**A test edit still runs the tests**, since `website` is untouched — which is the behaviour worth keeping.

## Why the exclusion list is short

The two ways of being wrong aren't symmetric: excluding too little costs one needless deploy, while excluding too much leaves production serving a **stale bundle** after a real change. So only paths the app entry provably never imports are excluded. Everything else — `vite.config.js`, `package.json`, `index.html`, `public/`, `scripts/`, and a source file merely *named* like a test — still deploys.

`website_deployable` also tracks `force_website` on a `workflow_dispatch`. That's load-bearing: the dispatch is the CDN-invalidation escape hatch and works by re-uploading `index.html`, so leaving the output unset there would read as `false` downstream and silently skip the deploy exactly when someone reaches for it because the live document is stale.

## Verification

The filter logic was extracted and run against 17 path scenarios under the same `set -euo pipefail` as the real step — all pass:

| Changed paths | `website` | `website_deployable` |
|---|---|---|
| `cypress/e2e/api-live.cy.js` | true | **false** |
| `cypress/e2e/*.cy.js` + `cypress/support/e2e.js` | true | **false** |
| `cypress.config.js` | true | **false** |
| `src/__tests__/Home.test.js` + snapshots | true | **false** |
| all three test groups mixed | true | **false** |
| `src/components/NavBar.jsx` | true | true |
| test file **+** real source | true | true |
| `vite.config.js` | true | true |
| `package.json` | true | true |
| `index.html` | true | true |
| `public/files/cv.pdf` | true | true |
| `scripts/fetch-contributions.mjs` | true | true |
| `src/utils/testHelpers.js` | true | true |
| `src/cypressThing.js` | true | true |
| no-base fallback (`website/`) | true | true |
| `infrastructure/main.tf` only | false | false |
| `.github/workflows/ci.yml` only | false | false |

The last two "true" source rows matter: the regex is directory-anchored, so a source file with `test` or `cypress` in its *name* is not mistaken for a test.

## Test plan

- [x] Filter logic verified against 17 path scenarios, including `set -e` behaviour and the `$GITHUB_OUTPUT` write
- [ ] `Workflow lint` (actionlint + shellcheck) passes
- [ ] This PR touches only `.github/`, so `website` is `false` and both `web-checks`/`web-e2e` skip — expected
- [ ] After merge, on this push: `Deploy website` **skipped** (workflow-only change, `website_deployable=false`), and consequently `Production smoke test` skipped
- [ ] On the next real source change: `Deploy website` runs as before

Note the last two together are the point — this PR's own merge is a live demonstration, since a `.github/`-only change should not deploy.

---

## Summary
- Backend PRs synth-laboratories/backend#1146, #1147, #1148 (stacked, merging soon) stamp five new server-minted fields onto the Sync session projection (`GET /smr/research-intern/sync-sessions/{id}`). `InternSyncSession` is `extra="forbid"`, so without these declarations every typed `sync_.get()`/`create()`/`list()` parse would raise once those PRs deploy.
- Adds typed nested contracts mirroring the backend `SyncSessionResponse` wire shapes (names/optionality from `packages/intern/contracts.py` + regenerated `smr_openapi.yaml`): `SyncTemplateProvisionedResource`, `SyncTemplateProvisioningReceipt`, `SyncTracePublicationReceipt`, `SyncKitAssociatedFile`, `SyncKitIngressSource`, `SyncKitAssociationReceipt`, `SyncKitReadiness` (+ `SyncKitIngressKind`/`SyncKitIngressObservation` literals).
- Declares the five projection stamps on `InternSyncSession` with absent-tolerant defaults: `task_template: str | None`, `provisioning`, `trace_publication`, `kit_readiness` (all `None`), and `kit_associations: tuple[...] = ()`. Old backends (fields absent) and new backends (fields populated) both parse; round-trip via `to_wire()` is lossless.
- Exports the new models through `contracts/__init__.py` and the public research surface (`public.py`).
- No MCP changes needed: `intern_sync_get`/`intern_sync_list` re-serialize the typed session via `to_wire()`, so the new stamps pass through once declared; MCP tools only declare input schemas.
- Async runtime projection (`InternAsyncRuntime`) is a separate model and untouched — these fields are sync-only.

## Dependency
This is forward-compatible either way, but the fields only appear once the backend chain #1146 → #1147 → #1148 lands and deploys. Safe to merge before or after.

## Recommendation (pending decision, intentionally NOT changed here)
`_StrictContract` keeps `extra="forbid"` on response models, which makes every additive backend projection field a breaking SDK change. Recommend relaxing response-side models (not requests) to `extra="ignore"` — left out of this PR pending the standing user decision.

- New SDK contract tests in the testing repo (`backend/unit/synth_ai_sdk/unit/test_research_intern_sync_projection.py`): full new-backend payload (all five stamps, shapes from the backend OpenAPI), old-backend payload (stamps absent), failed trace-publication stamp, round-trips, and typed `sync_.get`/`sync_.list` pass-through. 27 passed against this branch via `SYNTH_AI_DIR` override; the one failure in `test_research_intern_contract.py` (legacy `/sessions` MCP advertisement) reproduces at the origin/dev baseline and is unrelated (from the legacy-gate merge).

body:
Closes #173

## What
Cross-route View Transitions for app-like page transitions, subtle by design.

- **Route outlet wrapper**: ViewTransitionsProvider (client) wraps root-layout children in React's <ViewTransition>, which Next 16 resolves to its bundled (canary) React build at runtime. 250ms ease crossfade via CSS; no wild morphs.
- **Named shared elements**:
  - Project card image -> project detail hero (per-slug project-image-<slug> name, both sides).
  - Nav logo (site-logo) - identical in both snapshots, stays rock-steady while the page crossfades.
- **Reduced motion**: provider renders a plain fragment (instant navigation) + CSS ::view-transition-* kill-switch for the one-frame window before the hook settles.
- **Fallback**: browsers without the View Transitions API render children as-is (React feature-detects document.startViewTransition) - instant nav, verified. CSS ::view-transition-* rules ignored by non-supporting browsers.
- **Focus/scroll**: verified in Chromium - no focus loss mid-transition, no scroll jump; back-nav scroll restoration identical with/without transitions.
- Type shim for the canary ViewTransition export (@types/react@18 lacks it; npm react@19.2 doesn't export it either - Next bundles it).

## Tests
1201 passing (baseline 1198 + 3 new):
- wrapper mounts when motion is allowed
- reduced motion skips the transition entirely
- plain-fragment fallback when the runtime lacks the ViewTransition export

Browser-verified (headless Chromium): transition fires with root + subtree crossfade + project-image-* morph + site-logo group, all 250ms; reduced-motion nav fires no transition; zero console errors.

author: thales-da-vinci
thomaslwang
body:
## Purpose

On PCIe-only boxes whose GPUs form multiple islands — e.g. 2×4 A100/A800, where GPU0-3 and GPU4-7 are each PIX-connected and the two halves are bridged by the CPU interconnect — `CustomAllreduce` is unavailable (`is_fully_connected` is false) and every allreduce falls to the NCCL ring, which crosses the slow inter-island link repeatedly. Profiling DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731 decode on an 8×A800 box put **allreduce at 68.6% of decode GPU time** (292 µs/call at decode shapes), far ahead of attention (2.3%) or the MoE GEMMs.

This adds an opt-in island-aware communicator. It is off unless the operator supplies an explicit island partition, so nothing changes for existing deployments.

## Design

Enabled with `VLLM_HIER_ALL_REDUCE="0,1,2,3;4,5,6,7"`. Two Triton kernels share one set of IPC-registered buffers and dispatch on message size:

- **one-shot** (< 24576 elements): publish the input, reduce the island over direct P2P reads, then one cross-island exchange. Two sync rounds, 4n remote bytes.
- **two-shot** (≥ 24576): reduce-scatter within the island, exchange only the `1/island_size` shard across islands, allgather. Three sync rounds, 7n/4 remote bytes — and only `n/island_size` crosses the slow link instead of `n`.

Three details are load-bearing and worth calling out for review:

1. **Push-based signalling.** PCIe has no native remote atomics, and having a reader poll a remote flag costs a PCIe round trip per spin. Writers instead store sequence tokens into the *reader's* local flag array and readers spin on local memory only, with `fence.acq_rel.sys` for ordering. Same shape as the existing CUDA custom-allreduce kernels.
2. **Device-side sequence counters.** A host-supplied token would be baked into a CUDA graph and replay out of order, so the token comes from a device-side fetch-and-increment. Buffers then alternate by token parity, which makes it impossible for a rank that has lapped a slow peer to overwrite data the peer is still reading (a two-call lap is blocked by the flag waits).
3. **Stripe CTA partitioning in the two-shot kernel.** CTA *k* owns slice *k* of *every* shard rather than one contiguous range, so a reader CTA always waits on the same CTA index of its peers across all three phases. That removes the need for a grid-wide barrier, which Triton has no primitive for.

Note the IPC buffers are allocated and mapped through `cudaIpcOpenMemHandle` with the importing device current, rather than via torch's `_new_shared_cuda`: torch opens IPC handles inside the *owner's* device context, so the mapping is never made peer-accessible to the importing device's kernels — `copy_()` works but a kernel dereference is an immediate IMA, and `cudaDeviceEnablePeerAccess` does not retroactively fix an already-imported handle.

## Not a duplicate of

- **#36834 (Added Hierarchical all reduce)** — that is a *node-level* hierarchy for multi-node inference: intra-node NVLink custom allreduce plus inter-node RDMA through UCCL-EP. This PR is single-node and hierarchical *within* the box, over PCIe islands, on hardware that has no NVLink at all. No overlap in code or target.
- **#44891 (push-based allreduce for small tensor reductions)** — shares the push/poll idea but is a flat (non-hierarchical) protocol in CUDA C++ targeting NVLink (threshold tuned on B200). This is a two-level algorithm in Triton for PCIe-island topologies. They compose: that PR's dispatch entry is above `CustomAllreduce`, this one is likewise independent and gated behind an explicit env.
- **#39633 (Fix PCIe custom-allreduce eligibility on >2 GPU topologies)** — that reuses the *existing* barrier-based kernel on PCIe. I tried exactly that on this hardware first (the P2P access matrix is fully connected here, so the NVLink-only gate looked like policy rather than capability). It runs at 21 µs but returns **numerically wrong results** at `world_size=8` (max error 1.5 to `inf` against an NCCL reference), so I abandoned that route and wrote a separate kernel instead. Details posted on that PR — it may be worth verifying on SM120 before enabling.

## Test plan

New `tests/distributed/test_hier_all_reduce.py` checks the communicator against `torch.distributed.all_reduce` across sizes that straddle the one-shot/two-shot threshold in both directions, plus a size that is not a multiple of the CTA tiling to exercise the masked tails. Each size runs twice so both parity buffers are used.

```
$ pytest tests/distributed/test_hier_all_reduce.py -q
2 passed, 14 warnings in 64.69s
```
(`tp_size` 2 and 4 on an 8×A800 node.)

Standalone correctness/latency sweep against NCCL, bf16, 8×A800, max error ≤ 0.016 at every size (bf16 reduction-order tolerance), µs/call:

| size | NCCL | one-shot | two-shot |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 8KB | 56.9 | **46.5** | 47.5 |
| 32KB | 95.8 | **45.6** | 47.3 |
| 48KB | 64.7 | 54.3 | **49.6** |
| 64KB | **49.8** | 64.5 | 52.9 |
| 128KB | 132.2 | 102.2 | **66.7** |
| 256KB | 169.4 | 174.8 | **91.2** |
| 512KB | 160.4 | 324.2 | **143.0** |

64KB is the one point where NCCL still wins; I left the dispatch alone rather than special-casing around a single measurement.

## Serving results

DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731, 8×A800, TP=8, EP, fp8 KV, `vllm bench serve` with in 2048 / out 512, toggling only `VLLM_HIER_ALL_REDUCE`:

| config | concurrency | on | off | gain |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| DSpark spec decode, `max_num_seqs=16` | 1 | 101.3 | 90.2 tok/s | **+12.4%** |
| | 8 | 356.2 | 315.5 tok/s | **+12.9%** |
| no spec decode, `max_num_seqs=64` | 16 | 402.9 | 384.0 tok/s | +4.9% |
| | 32 | 690.6 | 609.1 tok/s | **+13.4%** |
| | 64 | 911.1 | 845.8 tok/s | +7.7% |

Peak output throughput goes 846 → 911 tok/s. The gain tracks message size: the payload is `batch × hidden × 2` bytes, so concurrency 16/32/64 lands near 128/256/512KB, matching the kernel table above.

Accuracy is unaffected (the op is a drop-in allreduce). As an end-to-end sanity run, the same stack completed Terminal-Bench 2.1 (89 tasks, 18.4 hours, 13,264 requests, 200.7M prompt + 5.5M generated tokens) with no crashes and no numerical corruption.

## Notes

- Opt-in only; when `VLLM_HIER_ALL_REDUCE` is unset the dispatch chain is unchanged.
- Requires exactly two equal islands and bf16 input; anything else falls through to the existing backends.
- AI assistance (Claude) was used for this change.

This pull request was automatically generated by SpaceDock on behalf of [UtilityMaker](https://spacedock.info/profile/UtilityMaker), to add [ManuverTrails](https://spacedock.info/mod/4459/ManuverTrails) to CKAN.

## Mod details

Key         | Value
:---------- | :---------------------
Name        | [ManuverTrails](https://spacedock.info/mod/4459/ManuverTrails)
Authors     | [UtilityMaker](https://spacedock.info/profile/UtilityMaker)
Abstract    | Volumetric lifting-surface trails and realistic wingtip vortices.
License     | MIT
Size        | 36.06 KiB
Homepage    | <>
Source code | <>

## Description

ManuverTrails adds long volumetric lifting-surface trails and realistic wingtip vortices to aircraft in Kerbal Space Program.

This is separate from Manuvering Vapor. ManuverTrails creates the long condensation trails behind lifting surfaces; Manuvering Vapor creates the broad, short-lived cloud that stays over the wing during intense maneuvers. The two mods may be installed together.

The trail positions and visibility are calculated from the craft's real ModuleLiftingSurface geometry and live lift forces. Centerline body lift, vertical fins, and weak non-wing controls are filtered out.

Features:

- Responds to local lift, G-force, airspeed, altitude, atmospheric density, lighting, and aircraft size.
- Groups connected wing panels and controls into aerodynamic wing groups.
- Normal aircraft produce roughly four to six evenly distributed trails.
- Stock flight-toolbar setting controls the maximum visible trails from 0 to 64; default is 6.
- The cap keeps the strongest aerodynamic lanes and applies immediately.
- Supports multi-part, swept, and canted wings.
- Smooth lower-atmosphere TrailRenderer wakes and curved high-speed LineRenderer wakes.
- No dependencies and no craft or save-file changes.

Installation:

1. Exit KSP.
2. Remove GameData/WingtipVortex if installed.
3. Copy the ManuverTrails folder into GameData.

Final path: GameData/ManuverTrails/Plugins/ManuverTrails.dll

Do not install WingtipVortex and ManuverTrails together because both contain the same trail effect lineage. Manuvering Vapor is a compatible separate companion effect.

For KSP 1.12.x. MIT license.
