body:
Closes #96.

An operator reading a failed cascade could not decide what to do next. Two findings, one surface,
both measured while taking all five Springfield teams to full enrichment.

## 1 — a failure that is not `ambiguous` reported no reason at all

`team pull: cascading "Jim Vanderveen" failed (error) — skipped` was the whole diagnosis, while
`PlayerPullResult` carried a populated `message` the warning discarded. A network timeout, an HTTP
404 and a `ParseError` want three different responses and the report distinguished none of them —
the same defect class #94 was opened for, one branch over, surviving #94 precisely because those two
branches were pinned by no test.

Every non-`ok` kind now names its reason, through **one exported line-renderer**:

```
team pull: cascading "Nova Norbury" failed (error) — fetch failed with status 503: <url> — skipped
```

- Sanitized **once, over the whole rendered line** — the reason is a new attacker-influenced value
  (a `ParseError` quotes the document it choked on), so both interpolated values are covered.
- An error carrying **no** message prints no dangling ` —  — ` separator.
- All four non-`ok` kinds asserted as whole strings. `unknown-target` is **unreachable** through
  `pullTeam` (the cascade calls `pullPlayer` with a `url`, never a name target), which is exactly how
  it came to print nothing — so the renderer is exported and that branch asserted directly, with the
  two integration tests binding it to what an operator really sees.

## 2 — only one ambiguity per attempt was ever visible

`pullPlayer` refused at the **first** ambiguity, costing one slow network round trip per remaining
one: `Dale Dixon` took four attempts live, and `NE/Penland` needed **three full `--players` runs**
(~4 min each) because every run re-fetches every roster member to reach the next one.

One pass now collects **every** ambiguity it meets — in encounter order, deduped (the fixture's
partner is named in 3 of 14 records; that is one decision, not three lines) — and reports them
together:

```
team pull: cascading "Avery Ashby" failed (ambiguous) — 2 ambiguous identities — [1] "Nova Norbury"
(match partner) — near: Novo Norbury; [2] "Sawyer Sable" (match opponent) — near: Sawyer Soble — skipped
```

**The abort is unchanged**, which is the part #94 depends on: one refusal, thrown inside the
transaction, rolling back, writing nothing — re-read from `players` / `court_matches` /
`court_match_players` / `rating_observations` rather than inferred from the returned kind. The pass
keeps *resolving* after the first refusal because resolution is what discovers an ambiguity; it stops
*writing*, because every remaining write needs an id the ambiguity denied.

An ambiguous **profile name** no longer hides the history's ambiguities behind it either.

## What did NOT change, deliberately

- **`TeamPullResult`'s shape.** Untouched. `PlayerPullResult`'s ambiguous variant gains `identities`
  **additively** — the three flat fields stay as `identities[0]`.
- **No edit to `src/cli/commands/*.ts` or `src/mcp/tools.ts`** (a parallel change owns them). Both
  already hand `ambiguousMessage` the whole result object, so putting the plural rendering inside the
  shared formatter is what makes `tn player pull` and the `player_pull` MCP tool report every
  ambiguity for free. Asserted end-to-end through `dispatch` and the tool handler rather than argued.
- **`pullTeam`'s own roster loop still refuses at the first.** Collecting there means continuing past
  an ambiguous row, and `retireAbsentMemberships` reconciles departures against exactly that loop's
  `observedPlayerIds`, in the same transaction — the partial-roster hazard its own comment names.
  Recorded in `docs/findings.md` as an accepted residual, not smuggled in.
- **Automatic retry** — out of scope per the issue. Classifying retryable vs permanent in
  `skippedEntries=` is #98, blocked on this.

## Mutation verification

The issue set the bar at "reverting `ambiguousMessage` to `ambiguous target: ${candidates}` must
redden ≥ 9 tests". Measured **before writing a line**, `main` already reddened **12** — so as a
pass/fail gate it was satisfied by doing nothing. Run as intended instead — *do the new assertions
move under a deliberate break* — one mutant per behaviour:

| Mutant | Tests reddened |
|---|---|
| `ambiguousMessage` reverted to the pre-#94 message | **23** (12 at `main`) |
| plural renders only the first identity | 5 |
| collect only the first ambiguity | 5 |
| no dedupe | 12 |
| the refusal is never thrown | 14 |
| the profile-ambiguous branch skips the history scan | 1 |
| drop the reason for non-`ambiguous` kinds (the defect) | 3 |
| append the reason unconditionally (dangling separator) | 1 |
| no `sanitizeValue` on the cascade line | 3 |

Two things fell out of running them separately rather than trusting the headline number:

1. **#95's hostile-name test was vacuous.** It asserted `not.toContain(ESC)` over an **empty** spy —
   the hostile name was a roster row, which makes `pullTeam` refuse before the cascade runs, so the
   line under test was never emitted. It held for any implementation, including one with no
   sanitizer: deleting `sanitizeValue` reddened nothing there. Rewritten to put the hostile name
   where the live #94 report had it (a partner inside the cascaded player's history), to assert the
   emission first, and to pin the whole line. Fixed here rather than filed.
2. **One mutant is *equivalent* and is not claimed as covered:** sanitizing each interpolated field
   instead of the whole line emits identical bytes, so no test can distinguish them. The whole-line
   rule is a robustness argument about future edits, not a behaviour with a test behind it.

Also removed rather than documented: an `if (profiled === null) throw` invariant that no test could
ever kill (`rules/testing.md`). The profile-ambiguous branch now refuses inline, so `profiled` is a
plain non-null const, and pass 1 is extracted as `resolveHistory`, called from both paths.

## Checks

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| `ruby scripts/parity_check.rb` | OK |
| `npm run typecheck` | clean |
| `npm run lint` | clean |
| `npm test -- test/cli-grammar-parity.test.ts` | 10 passed |
| `npm run test:coverage` | **1603 passed**, thresholds met (1585 before) |

`docs/runbooks/pre-tournament-full-pull.md` is updated for both: the failure triage now has three
causes instead of two (with transient vs permanent named), and the ambiguity loop says *rule on
everything the run listed, then re-run once* rather than the old one-per-round-trip dance.

— Claude Code (Opus 5)

author: lgldsilva
body:
## Problem

npm 12 (RFC [npm/rfcs#868](https://github.com/npm/rfcs/pull/868)) **blocks dependency install scripts by default** unless the package is covered by an `allowScripts` policy. Global installs (`npm update -g`, `npm install -g`) then *succeed* while `postinstall` is **silently skipped** — only a `npm warn install-scripts ... blocked` warning is emitted.

For wrapper packages such as `@anthropic-ai/claude-code` this leaves the 500-byte placeholder stub at `bin/claude.exe` instead of the platform-native binary. Every `claude` invocation then fails with:

```
Error: claude native binary not installed.
```

…which also breaks subsequent `claude update` runs (the stub intercepts every subcommand). Reproduced live: `npm install -g npm@latest @anthropic-ai/claude-code@latest` with no allow-scripts entry leaves the stub; with the entry, postinstall runs and the binary is placed.

## Fix

- **npm category** (`batchNpmUpgrade`): pass `--allow-scripts=<every package in the batch>` to `npm update -g` so lifecycle scripts of the updated packages are allowed. Older npm versions ignore the unknown config key.
- **npm-driven agent updates** (Codex, pi, Qwen Code + generic fallback): new `npmGlobalInstallCmd` helper adds `--allow-scripts=<pkg>` to the install command.
- **Claude Code self-heal** (`ensureClaudeNativeBinary`): after any Claude Code update, verify `claude --version`; when the stub marker is detected, re-run the wrapper's postinstall (`node $(npm root -g)/@anthropic-ai/claude-code/install.cjs`) and retry the update once when it failed only because claude was already the broken stub.

## Verification

- `gofmt`, `go vet`, full `go test -race -shuffle=on ./...` green; coverage gate 92.3% (≥90%)
- New unit tests: `npmAllowScriptsFlag`, stub-marker detection, `npmGlobalInstallCmd`, allow-scripts presence on every npm-driven agent command
- End-to-end on the affected host: repaired install, `npm install -g @anthropic-ai/claude-code@latest` now places the ELF, `claude --version` → 2.1.221, `updash --check` reports Claude Code ✓
- Updated `diagnose` suggestion for Codex + its test expectation

Note: `--allow-scripts` is only valid in global/npx contexts (npm throws `EALLOWSCRIPTS` in project-scoped installs) — every call site here is global.

body:
## Resumen

Corrige `/mascota @usuario` para que use el mismo render de ficha que la vista propia y añade una preferencia pública persistente entre **Imagen** y **ASCII clásico** desde **Personalizar**.

## Causa raíz

La ficha propia ya pasaba por `vistas._ficha()`, que sabe adjuntar el retrato cuando existe. La ficha visitante llamaba directamente a `pantalla.render(...)`, por lo que siempre mostraba ASCII aunque la criatura tuviera retrato.

## Cambios

- Añade `estilos_ficha` en SQLite, aislada por persona y servidor.
- Usa **Imagen** por defecto sin crear filas al leer la preferencia.
- Permite elegir **Imagen** o **ASCII clásico** desde el menú efímero de **Personalizar**.
- Centraliza la ficha visitante en `vistas._ficha()` usando la preferencia del dueño, no la de quien mira.
- Mantiene las fichas ajenas sin controles y sin apropiarse de la pantalla persistente.
- Conserva el fallback ASCII cuando falta un retrato.
- Mantiene lápidas y criaturas muertas en ASCII, sin consultar estilo ni saldo vivo.
- Conserva la preferencia al cambiar de gachamon activo.
- Republica la ficha una sola vez después de cambiar el estilo.

## Diseño lean

Se reutilizan SQLite, `vistas._ficha`, `publicar_pantalla`, `republicar_ficha`, `Personalizar` y los componentes Discord existentes. No se añaden dependencias, comandos, modales, modo Auto ni una capa genérica de settings.

author: kraigparkinson
body:
## Problem

`scripts/grounding-readout.test.sh` exists and passes, but nothing in `.github/workflows/` runs it — verified: `git grep grounding-readout origin/main -- .github/` returns nothing. A regression in the readout would merge green.

That matters more than a typical missing test run because of what the script is. `scripts/grounding-readout.sh` is the Check instrument for the PDCA-1 grounding experiment (#60, ADR-0008), and its failure mode is producing a plausible-looking number that is **wrong** — exactly what #123/#124 repaired. The suite is mutation-checked: disabling any single defense in the readout fails it. That value is only realized if something runs it.

## What this adds

`.github/workflows/scripts-test.yml` — one job, three steps:

1. print `bash` / `python3` / `git` versions, so a runner-image change self-diagnoses instead of surfacing as an unexplained test failure;
2. `shellcheck scripts/*.sh` (both files are clean today);
3. `bash scripts/grounding-readout.test.sh`.

Runs on `pull_request` → `main`, `push` → `main`, and `workflow_dispatch`. Runtime is well under a second.

## Choices worth naming

**A new workflow, not a step in `ci.yml`.** `ci.yml`'s own header states the Tier 3 convention — those repos don't standardize a build/test step there — and it is a thin caller to `Integral-Productivity/reusable-workflows` with no room for repo-local steps. There is no org reusable for "run a bash test script," so a direct job is the right shape.

**No `paths:` filter, deliberately.** A path-filtered workflow that doesn't match reports *no conclusion at all*, which is indistinguishable from passing — the same fail-silent shape this suite exists to catch. It's also the trap `version-authority.yml` documents: a skipped check configured as required blocks a PR forever, waiting on a status that never arrives. Separately, a `scripts/**`-only filter would miss a real failure mode, because test §9 derives the directive marker from the live `hooks-handlers/session-start.sh` — a change to the hook alone can break the suite. At sub-second runtime, filtering buys nothing.

**`permissions: contents: read` declared explicitly.** Org and repo default workflow permissions are `read`, and callers omitting their own block have produced opaque 0-job `startup_failure`s in this repo before.

**`actions/checkout@v4`** — matches what `main` carries today (`version-authority.yml`). #121 is the open Dependabot PR moving it to v7; this file will be swept along with the rest when that lands.

**`push: main` leg** is the backstop for a direct push to `main`, which is possible today and which a `pull_request`-scoped check structurally cannot see.

## Verification

- `shellcheck scripts/*.sh` exits 0 on the unmodified files.
- `bash scripts/grounding-readout.test.sh` → `PASS: all grounding-readout tests`.
- **Proved it fails when it should.** Mutated `is_placeholder()` in `scripts/grounding-readout.sh` to `return False` (disabling placeholder exclusion); the suite exits 1 with `FAIL: issue #123 fixtures scored wrong` — `resolve_announce.count` becomes 2 instead of 1, because the placeholder fixture scores. Mutation reverted; the working tree here contains only the new workflow file.
  - Worth noting: `shellcheck` stayed **green** on the mutated file. The two steps catch genuinely different classes of defect; neither substitutes for the other.
  - The mutation was run locally rather than pushed as a deliberately-red commit on purpose. `main`'s ruleset requires only the two version-authority checks, and `gh pr merge --auto` waits only on *required* checks — so a red `Scripts tests` would not have blocked auto-merge, and the mutation would have merged into `main`.

## Known gap (follow-up, not in scope here)

This check **reports** but does not yet **gate**: `Scripts tests` is not in the `main: version authority must pass` ruleset's required-status-check list, so auto-merge will not wait on it. Adding it is a one-line ruleset edit, but it has to happen *after* this workflow is on `main` — a required check that doesn't exist yet blocks every PR. Because this workflow carries no path filter it always reports a conclusion, so it is safe to make required, unlike a filtered one.

Closes #126

author: versoriumx
body:
⚡ Bolt has completed another successful performance optimization!

💡 **What:** Refactored the `checkValue` function in the `electricFence` middleware (`src/security.js`) to eliminate redundant double string scans.
🎯 **Why:** Previously, the middleware used `val.includes('**')` first, followed by `val.indexOf('**')` to find occurrence indexes. This causes the V8 engine to scan the string twice. Replacing it with a single-pass `indexOf()` loop completely avoids the redundant first scan.
📊 **Impact:** 
- ~6% performance gain on normal asterisk-free strings (the hot path for 99.9% of requests)
- Up to 11.6% performance gain on inputs with multiple asterisk pairs
🔬 **Measurement:** Measured and verified via the new benchmark `test/benchmarks/benchmark_check_value.js`. All 39 unit and integration tests are passing perfectly.

author: rakeikahukoti-del
body:
## Summary

`app/add.js` was 1114 lines mixing form orchestration, JSX, and an inline stylesheet. This splits it into 2 files under `components/add/`, following the established pattern (presentational component + co-located `createStyles(colors, ...)`):

- `QuickStartCard`: the template/routine quick-start card — was inline JSX in the original.
- `TemplateRoutinePicker`: bundles the picker `Modal`, its two content modes (`TemplatePickerContent`, `RoutinePickerContent`), and `TemplateCard` — all tightly coupled to one picker feature.

`add.js` drops to **219 lines** (from 1114).

**Checked existing shared form components first**: `HabitFormFields.js` and `HabitFormScreen.js` already own the core form fields and screen shell/header/footer scaffold, and needed no changes — `add.js`'s own content never overlapped with them.

**New orchestration hook**: `hooks/useAddHabitController.js`, mirroring the other four controller hooks, for the screen's form state, validation, and submission logic — 7 field values, 2 `useEffect`s, 4 memoized derivations, and the full save/cancel/template/routine handler set, including the `router.replace`/`Alert.alert` calls that are inseparable from the save/cancel mutation flow itself.

**Reuse checked before creating anything new**: no existing modal shell (`home`/`stats`/`analytics`/`rank`) matched this screen's bottom-sheet style (backdrop `justifyContent: "flex-end"`, card with only top corners rounded) — every prior modal was a centered card, so this builds its own rather than forcing a mismatched reuse. `buttonPressed` is byte-identical to `PRESSED_BUTTON_STYLE` and is reused directly.

**One deliberate, more conservative choice than prior hooks**: the per-field setters passed to `HabitFormFields` are wrapped inline (`clearError()` then the real setter) in the original JSX, with `setName` as the sole exception (left raw, with `clearError` passed separately as `onNameChange`). The hook returns raw setters and this wrapping stays exactly where it was in the screen's JSX, rather than relocating it into the hook — a smaller diff and a more literal transcription.

A few pre-existing quirks preserved as-is (not "fixed" as part of this structural-only refactor): `currentDuplicate` is recomputed on every render with no `useMemo`; `duplicateWarning`'s background-color ternary tests `colors.warning` (always truthy, so effectively a no-op) rather than an actual warning flag.

Structural refactor only — no visual or behavioral change intended.

This is 5 of 6 oversized screens targeted for the same treatment (`analytics/[id].js` remains as follow-up work, not included here).

## Verification

author: tn1dg
body:
One-word fix in `scripts/vercel-build.js`, plus the doc trail. No app code
changes — `src/` is untouched, so nothing user-facing moves.

## The bug

`scripts/vercel-build.js` used `--preview-create`. Per `npx convex deploy --help`:

> `--preview-create <name>` — Like `--preview-name`, but **deletes and
> recreates** an existing preview deployment with the same name.

So every push to a non-production branch destroyed that branch's Convex
deployment and built a new one: empty database, zero environment variables,
every test account gone.

Caught immediately after PR #8 merged. The `staging` rebuild logged
`"Seeded 70 exercises."` and *set* the auth keys — on a deployment that had
been seeded and configured by hand an hour earlier. The tell was that the
`--if-absent` guard from cc8ff07 never skipped: there was never an existing
deployment for it to find, so the session loss it was written to prevent was
happening anyway, by a different route.

## The fix

`--preview-name` reuses the branch's deployment instead of recreating it.

- Test accounts and data survive pushes, so QA on `staging` no longer starts
  with re-registering.
- `--if-absent` becomes load-bearing rather than dead code.
- It rehearses production more honestly: production carries persistent data, so
  a schema change that can't cope with existing rows now fails on a preview
  first, instead of sailing through a clean slate.

What's given up is the guaranteed clean-slate/first-install test. Run
`--preview-create` by hand if that's ever wanted specifically.

## Verification

Confirmed on the `dev` build after the fix:

```
--preview-name "dev"
[setup-auth-env] JWT_PRIVATE_KEY already set (preview: dev) — leaving it alone.
```

That skip path had never run in CI before. `npx convex run exercises:seed
--preview-name dev` afterwards returned "Already seeded — skipped.", i.e. the
database survived the build.

Local: `tsc -b`, `tsc --noEmit -p convex`, oxlint clean, 312 tests passing.

## Reviewing this one

The build triggered by merging this PR is itself the test. It runs with the new
code against the `staging` deployment that the *previous* (`--preview-create`)
build left behind, so it should reuse it — look for `already set … leaving it
alone` in the log rather than three `Setting …` lines.

Known loose end, documented rather than hidden: on a reuse build `--preview-run`
logs no output, where a fresh deployment logs `"Seeded 70 exercises."`. The
seeded state is correct either way, and a brand-new branch takes the
first-deploy path that has been seen working — but that's the place to look if
a new branch ever comes up with an empty exercise library.

Production is unaffected: this whole path is gated behind
`VERCEL_ENV !== 'production'`.

author: silverbeer
body:
## Why

`k3s/match-scraper-agent/configmap.yaml` pointed `AGENT_RABBITMQ_URL` at `rabbitmq.match-scraper`, while the Celery workers consume from `messaging-rabbitmq`. Applying it would have published every match into a void. Of the four divergences behind the standing "never run `deploy.sh`" warning, **this was the only one that could actually break production** — the other three are keys nothing reads.

## What

**The hostname fix**, plus removal of config for things that no longer exist. `AgentSettings` has `extra: "ignore"`, so these were silently discarded — they read like working configuration and were not:

| Removed | Why |
|---|---|
| `AGENT_MODEL_NAME`, `AGENT_PROXY_BASE_URL`, `AGENT_PROXY_ENABLED`, `AGENT_MIN_TOKEN_BUDGET` | dead since PR #42 replaced PydanticAI with the rules engine — no LLM in `src/` |
| `AGENT_ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` (Secret + `deploy.sh`) | same; an unused credential is worth removing on its own |
| `AGENT_JOURNAL_S3_BUCKET`, `AGENT_JOURNAL_S3_KEY`, `AGENT_RELEASE_WATCH_S3_KEY` | replaced by the PVC paths the cluster actually uses (SB-554, SB-555). Setting the bucket still switches both stores back to S3 |

`AGENT_TELEGRAM_CHAT_ID` moves from the ConfigMap to the Secret, matching the cluster and keeping a private chat ID out of a ConfigMap.

`deploy.sh` keeps a warning, but now states the reasons that are actually true: it stands up a **second** RabbitMQ, and it deploys the QoP CronJob that SB-544 deliberately leaves undeployed. The ConfigMap is now safe to apply on its own, and the header says so.

## Verification

The ConfigMap was applied. `kubectl diff` before it showed a purely additive change — three new keys, no value changes, hostname already matching — and after it reports no difference at all. **Repo and cluster are now identical**, for the first time in this investigation.

Cluster-side removals done alongside (not in this diff): the four dead keys patched out of the live ConfigMap and `AGENT_ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` out of the live Secret, via targeted `--type=json` removals rather than an apply.

Fixes SB-558

author: tyhuang9
body:
## Summary

Completes Phase 5 of the runtime-consolidated revamp by replacing the stale backend-oriented shell with runtime-neutral navigation and adding a pre-created, focus-safe native dictation overlay driven by the authoritative coordinator. It also hardens captured-target output, clipboard ownership, exactly-once paste behavior, and accessibility.

## Scope

Included:
- Versioned typed Live/Minimal/Off overlay settings with migration, salvage, and unknown-field preservation.
- General, Models, History, Advanced, About, and gated Debug navigation while reusing existing workflows.
- Pre-created eframe overlay viewport with real coordinator phases, native audio levels, committed/tentative presentation, and platform fail-closed behavior.
- Windows no-activate/tool-window/click-through/topmost hardening, target capture before overlay display, DPI-aware monitor geometry, and current-process rejection.
- Correlated one-frame-deferred output, clipboard generation/content ownership checks, single-batch Windows paste, cleanup for partially accepted input, and copy-only fallbacks.
- AccessKit semantics, visible/non-color state cues, WCAG AA semantic text tokens, reduced-motion support, and 44 px primary targets.
- Async capture startup concurrent with model preload plus race/stale-event regressions.

Intentionally not included:
- Native SPSC PCM/preparation/VAD worker (Phase 6).
- Incremental rolling preview (Phase 7).
- Target reactivation and richer clipboard restoration (Phase 8).
- Persistent history (Phase 10).
- A second runtime handler or any model support promotion.

## Implementation

The overlay accepts only runtime-neutral coordinator state, aggregate levels, and transcript state. Concrete runtime selection remains private to `RuntimeRouter`. Windows visibility fails closed unless the actual HWND reports all required extended styles and non-activating placement succeeds. Final output is consumed once from correlated pending state; tentative text never reaches another application.

The final application state on this branch remains exactly one logical handler, `TranscribeCppRuntime`. `OnnxSpeechRuntime` is omitted, all four normalized primary artifacts remain Experimental, zero models are Supported, and Zipformer remains NO-GO.

## Files and systems affected

- `src/overlay/*`: controller, platform adapter, and view.
- `src/ui/*`: shell, pages, reusable controls, and Scribe theme tokens.
- `src/app.rs`: coordinator integration, async capture/preload ordering, overlay lifecycle, safe deferred output.
- `src/text_output.rs`: target/clipboard verification and Windows input hardening.
- `src/audio.rs`: lock-free aggregate meter publication pending the Phase 6 PCM rewrite.
- `src/settings/*`, `src/config.rs`: typed overlay settings and migration.
- `docs/SCRIBE_REVAMP.md`, `docs/MANUAL_TEST_MATRIX.md`: decisions, evidence, risks, and executable manual rows.

## Tests

PASS on Windows x64, 2026-08-03:
- `cargo fmt --all -- --check`
- `cargo check --all-targets --all-features`
- `cargo clippy --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings`
- `cargo test --all-targets --all-features` — 323 discovered, 318 passed, 0 failed, 5 environment-required ignored
- `cargo build --all-features`
- `git diff --check`
- `wsl.exe python3 scripts/check-catalog-boundaries.py` — PASS, one handler and neutral UI boundary

Automated coverage includes pending explicit stop through late CaptureReady/finalization/one dispatch; preload completion orderings; stale overlay completion/deadline isolation; expired deadline target cleanup; app-level exactly-once output; clipboard content/generation races; every partial Windows input batch and exact key-release cleanup; overlay modes/geometry/a11y; target rejection; and settings migration.

## Risks and unverified behavior

- High release risk: physical Windows hotkey, microphone, overlay focus/taskbar/click-through, foreground paste, screen-reader, multi-monitor, and mixed-DPI behavior remain NOT VERIFIED.
- Medium: inherited CPAL callback still locks and writes WAV samples; Phase 6 replaces it.
- Medium: HWND/PID lifetime reuse, target reactivation, and rich clipboard restoration remain Phase 8 work.
- Medium: non-Windows overlay and automatic paste intentionally fail closed.
- Low: `app.rs` remains large despite bounded module extraction.
- No compatibility or latency improvement claim is made in this phase.

## Rollback

Revert the four Phase 5 commits or return to `revamp/phase-4-session-settings`. No database migration or runtime/model artifact activation is introduced. Existing user settings are preserved by the versioned field-level migration and unknown-field store.

## Manual Testing Instructions

Prerequisites: Windows 11 desktop; microphone; installed verified-local primary runtime/model; browser/editor/native text targets; optional second mixed-DPI monitor; disposable clipboard content.

1. Launch Scribe and visit Transcribe, General, Models, History, Advanced, and About. Enable Developer > Debug and visit Debug.
   - Expected: all routes are keyboard reachable; Debug is hidden until enabled; comparison remains functional inside Models.
2. Focus an external text field and start dictation in Live mode, then repeat Minimal and Off.
   - Expected: overlay never activates, never appears in taskbar/Alt+Tab, remains click-through and topmost; Live/Minimal show real state/level; Off stays hidden.
3. Repeat on each monitor and scaling combination, near every work-area edge.
   - Expected: overlay remains fully inside the captured target monitor work area with appropriate physical sizing.
4. Dictate once without changing focus.
   - Expected: Pasting is visible, finalized text is pasted exactly once, tentative text is never emitted, and clipboard restoration follows settings.
5. Dictate from target A, switch to target B or close A before completion, and independently change the clipboard.
   - Expected: no synthetic input reaches B; external clipboard data is not overwritten; Scribe reports copy-only/not-inserted fallback.
6. Stop immediately while the microphone is still preparing; repeat while model preload is pending, then start a new session quickly.
   - Expected: exactly one finalization/request at most, no stale overlay cleanup hides the newer session, and no stale paste occurs.
7. Navigate using keyboard and a screen reader; test 200% scaling and reduced motion.
   - Expected: visible focus, named controls/status/meter, polite committed/tentative announcements, non-color state cues, and no disallowed animation.
8. Inspect the updated manual matrix and attach dated evidence for every executed row.
   - Expected: unexecuted physical rows remain NOT VERIFIED; do not infer PASS from automated tests.

Cleanup: close Scribe, confirm temporary recording files follow current cleanup policy, and restore disposable clipboard/test settings.

Closes #179.

## Summary

- adds deterministic deadline, fuel, answer, intermediate-cell, UDF-depth, page, byte, and cancellation governance with typed evidence
- returns certified incomplete outcomes distinct from completion and errors, including governed entailment and fallible-view composition
- carries the contract across Rust, CLI query/update, Python, WebAssembly/TypeScript, and the versioned C ABI
- hardens SERVICE, LOAD, UPDATE, output caps, property paths, UDF exhaustion, and pre-allocation cell accounting against stop laundering or unbounded materialization
- preserves an ordinary-query fast path and adds report-only governor/path benchmarks
- freezes 29 governor corpus cases across 25 bands and publishes the consumer-facing governor profile

## Stage 2 remediation

The adversarial review closed the original eleven gap groups plus the final review passes:

1. terminal stop observability across local, remote, resolver, closure, and publication boundaries
2. output-cap, early-stop schema, and evidence invariants
3. non-forgeable partial certificates and witness withholding
4. typed UDF exhaustion and bounded algebra nesting
5. pre-allocation intermediate-cell governance
6. polynomial hostile property-path evaluation with candidate-edge charging
7. a versioned C governor/outcome/evidence carrier with public result-kind constants
8. Python, WASM/TypeScript, CLI, C, and composed fallible-view/federation parity
9. deterministic SHACL focus scheduling and deadline/ordinary-query acceptance oracles
10. the ungoverned fast path and report-only performance contract
11. public doctrine, generated registers, ownership guidance, and stale documentation
12. cancellation-polled OWL reverse mapping, including dataset, axiom, list, literal, and concept-finalization passes

All fourteen final inline review threads were answered and resolved. Detailed dispositions, including the three verified false premises, are recorded in the PR discussion.

## Validation

- `make check` passes at `cc62ffbf`, including formatting, warning-free all-target Clippy, the full workspace test/doc-test suite, hygiene and generated-artifact gates, and every release-crate wasm build

author: hyochangsung
body:
## 작업 내용

Auto Research 브랜치 생성 트리거를 `auto-research` + `experiment` 두 label의 `&&`
조건에서 **`auto-experiment` 단독**으로 바꿉니다.

`auto-research`는 트리거가 아니라 이슈 12건(#470, #428, #427, #426, #425, #424,
#423, #407, #406, #405, #404, #403)이 쓰는 **주제 분류 label**입니다. 트리거 의미와
분류 의미가 한 label에 겹쳐 있어, 분류 목적의 label 정리가 자동화를 건드렸습니다.
그 결합을 끊습니다.

label을 줄이는 것 자체도 목적입니다. Issue Form은 label을 자동 부여하지만
`gh issue create`는 Form을 우회하므로, 이슈를 발행하는 주체가 label 전부를 붙여야
합니다. 하나만 빠져도 `if:` 미충족으로 **skip**되고 skip은 실패가 아니라 체크도
알림도 남기지 않습니다.

`auto-experiment` label은 GitHub에 이미 생성해 두었습니다(머지 전 선행 조치).

## 변경 사항

- `.github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/auto_research.yml` — `labels: ["auto-experiment"]`
- `.github/workflows/auto-research-issue-branch.yml` — 게이팅을 단일 `contains`로
- `.github/workflows/auto-research-promotion.yml` — 이슈 가드를 `auto-experiment`로
- `tests/test_auto_experiment_trigger_label.py` (신규) — Issue Form의 `labels:`를
  정본으로 삼아 워크플로 2곳·문서 2곳이 같은 label을 말하는지 검사하는 드리프트 테스트
- `tests/test_branch_protection_contract.py` — 게이팅 계약을 단일 label로 재작성
  (`&&` 재도입과 옛 label 잔존도 함께 막음)
- `tests/test_auto_research_issue_branch.py` — job `if` 검사 갱신
- `CONTRIBUTING.md`, `.claude/docs/agent-workflow-reference.md` — Issue Form 표와
  "자동화 트리거 label" 절 갱신, `auto-research`가 트리거가 아님을 명시

## 관련 이슈

Closes #507

## 라벨

- [x] `feature` 또는 `enhancement` (minor)
- [ ] `bug` (patch)
- [ ] `breaking` (major)
- [ ] `documentation` / `experiment` (patch — default)

## 체크리스트

- [x] 코드가 로컬에서 정상적으로 실행된다
- [ ] 파이프라인 DAG 정상 실행 확인 — 해당 없음 (DAG 변경 없음)
- [x] 데이터 타입/스키마 변경 영향 범위 확인 — 해당 없음 (계약 스키마 변경 없음)
- [x] 기존 테스트가 모두 통과한다 (아래 "리뷰어 참고사항"의 선행 실패 1건 제외)
- [x] 필요한 경우 테스트를 추가했다
- [x] 관련 문서(README, docstring 등)를 업데이트했다
- [x] 시크릿/개인정보가 코드에 포함되지 않았다

## 리뷰어 참고사항

**두 번째 게이트를 함께 바꿔야 합니다.** `auto-research-promotion.yml:61-62`도
label을 검사하고 없으면 `throw`합니다. Issue Form만 바꾸면 새 `[AR]` 이슈는
`auto-research`를 갖지 않으므로 승격 단계에서 **100% 실패**합니다. 실행 이력이 0건이라
드러나지 않았을 뿐입니다.

**rename이 아니라 신규 생성입니다.** `gh label edit auto-research --name auto-experiment`는
기존 12건에 그대로 반영되어 그 전부가 트리거 대상이 됩니다. 본문 검증이 fail-closed로
브랜치 생성은 막지만, label을 만질 때마다 실패한 run이 쌓입니다.

**마이그레이션 대상이 없습니다(실측).** 두 label을 동시에 가진 이슈 0건, `[AR]` 이슈
저장소 역사상 0건, marker 코멘트 0건, `auto-research-promotion.yml`·
`auto-research-dev-promotion.yml` 실행 이력 0건입니다. 원격 `exp/*` 브랜치 2건은
워크플로가 아니라 사람이 만든 것입니다.

**드리프트 테스트를 변이로 검증했습니다.** 네 가지를 각각 되돌려 실패를 확인했습니다.

| 변이 | 잡은 테스트 |
| --- | --- |
| Form `labels:`에 `experiment` 추가 | 5건 실패 |
| 승격 워크플로 가드만 옛 label | `test_promotion_workflow_guard_requires_the_form_label` |
| 문서 표만 옛 label | `test_documents_list_the_same_labels_as_the_issue_form` |
| 워크플로 `if`를 다시 `&&` 두 label로 | `test_issue_branch_job_gates_on_the_form_label_alone` 외 1건 |

**로컬 선행 실패 1건 (CI는 통과).** 로컬에서
`tests/test_training_comparison.py::test_verify_comparison_rechecks_receipts_and_records_verified_metrics`가
`metric receipt 시간이 run 범위 밖입니다`로 실패하지만, `origin/main`을 worktree로 떼어
돌려도 동일하게 실패하고 **CI의 pytest는 3.11/3.12 모두 통과**합니다. 즉 이번 변경의
회귀가 아니라 로컬 환경(시각) 의존 실패입니다. 나머지는 로컬 `1735 passed, 19 skipped`,
`ruff check` 통과입니다.

**범위 밖.** 자연어 가설을 웹으로 받아 에이전트가 이슈를 발행하는 경로는 별도 작업입니다.
발행 상한·중복 차단은 #490 결정대로 발행 주체가 생기는 시점에 그 주체에 붙입니다.
Issue Form의 필드 구성은 그대로 두었습니다 — 파서는 Form이 아니라 렌더된 본문을 읽으므로
에이전트가 heading 20개를 채워 발행하면 현재 템플릿 그대로 통과합니다.

body:
## 概要

検索品質の改善ループのうち機械判定できる工程を月次ジョブに集約して自動化し、意図の解釈が必要な判断だけを管理画面のレビューキューで求める。

設計判断は ADR 管理サーバーに登録済み:

- **SPOTLIGHT-RAILS-40**: 機械判定は自動化し、人の判断は管理画面のレビューキューで求める
- **SPOTLIGHT-RAILS-41**: ゴールデンクエリの保存先を リポジトリ YAML から DB に移行（管理画面から採用アクションで追加するため）

## 変更内容

### 自動化（月次ジョブの拡張）

- ゴールデンクエリ評価（recall@10）を毎月自動実行し、履歴（`adr_management_search_evaluations`）に保存。推移を追跡可能に
- SPOTLIGHT-RAILS-38 の数値条件（月間報告3件以上・3ヶ月ゼロ報告＋検索あり・ログ10万件超・recall 前回比低下）を機械判定し、点検記録を自動登録（origin: `system:search-quality-report`。発火疑いは計測値付き suspected）
- 月次 Issue に recall・miss 内訳・自動点検結果・レビュー待ち件数・管理画面 URL を記載
- 評価失敗（埋め込み API 不通）時もレポートは発行し、失敗を本文に明記（縮退設計）

### 管理画面（人の判断のキュー）: `/admin/adr/search_quality`

- 概況（30日）・recall 推移・ゴールデンクエリ一覧を表示
- **0件検索キュー**: 「取り逃がしとして記録」（観測メモ必須・到達 ADR 任意）/「問題なし」
- **取り逃がし報告キュー**: 「ゴールデンクエリとして採用」（クエリ文言は自然言語に編集可・期待 ADR は到達 ADR）/「対応済みにする」
- 記録ルールは MCP ツール（report_search_miss_tool）と同じ Action を共有し二重実装しない

### ゴールデンクエリの DB 移行

- `adr_management_golden_queries`（adr_id 外部参照）。ADR 削除に連動して削除され、存在しない期待による評価エラーが構造的に消える
- `rake adr_management:import_golden_queries` で YAML から一回限り移行（冪等・存在しない期待 ADR はスキップして報告）。#44 で追加された表記揺れケースを含む6件が対象。YAML はインポート完了後のリリースで削除予定（本 PR では残置）

## マージ後のセットアップ（必須）

1. `kamal deploy`（マイグレーション3本）
2. 本番で `bin/rails adr_management:import_golden_queries` を一度実行（YAML → DB 移行。取り込み件数とスキップが表示される）
3. 管理画面 `/admin/adr/search_quality` を開き、ゴールデンクエリ6件が表示されることを確認

## 運用の変化・考慮点

- **月次 Issue**: recall と自動点検結果が載る。suspected の場合のみ人の対応（方式見直しの起票等）が必要。レビュー待ち件数と管理画面リンクから処理に進める
- **自動点検の対象は数値条件のみ**: SPOTLIGHT-RAILS-27 の非数値条件（さくらのAI Engine の料金・約款変更）は引き続き手動点検（レポート本文にも明記）
- **recall の分母変化**: ゴールデンクエリの採用・ADR 削除で分母が変わるため、recall の前回比較は「低下＝即劣化」ではなく内訳（details）の確認が必要。自動点検の suspected はそのトリガーとして機能する
- **自動点検の誤判定を見つけたら**: SPOTLIGHT-RAILS-40 の再評価条件に該当。判定ロジック・閾値を見直す
- **レビューキューの滞留**: 月10件以上が翌月まで残る状態が常態化したら自動化拡大を検討（同 ADR の再評価条件）

author: sdkv2
body:
## Problem

`npm run build:native` fails on Visual Studio 2026 (VS 18) with:

```
gyp ERR! find VS You need to install the latest version of Visual Studio
gyp ERR! stack Error: Could not find any Visual Studio installation to use
```

…on a machine with a perfectly good VS Community 2026 install including the "Desktop development with C++" workload. `vswhere` locates it without trouble; node-gyp ≤11 simply doesn't recognise `versionMajor === 18`.

`build-gpu-capture.mjs` already had a patch for exactly this. It just patched the wrong file.

## Cause

The script runs two rebuild steps that resolve **different** node-gyp copies:

| step | node-gyp used |
|---|---|
| `npm exec -- node-gyp rebuild` | plain `node-gyp` |
| `npm exec -- electron-rebuild …` | `@electron/node-gyp` |

`patchNodeGypVs18()` only touched `@electron/node-gyp`, and returned early via `if (!existsSync(p)) return` when it was absent — which is the common case, since nothing in this project depends on it directly. So on a stock install the patch was dead code: it ran, did nothing, and reported nothing, while the failure it was written to fix happened one line later in the step it never covered.

## Fix

Patch every `find-visualstudio.js` present, and `console.warn` when none is found, so an upstream rename surfaces instead of silently reverting to the broken behaviour. Each file keeps its own guards (already-patched check, needle check), so this stays a no-op on platforms and toolchains that don't need it.

No behaviour change on macOS or Linux — the function still returns immediately off win32.

## Verification

Windows 11, VS Community 2026 (v18, MSVC 14.50.35717 → PlatformToolset v145), Electron 43.2.0, RTX 3050 Laptop.

Restored `node-gyp/lib/find-visualstudio.js` from a pre-patch backup to reproduce the clean-checkout state, then ran `npm run build:native`:

- before: aborts at configure with `Could not find any Visual Studio installation to use`
- after: patches both candidates, `✔ Rebuild Complete`, `build:native — gpu_capture.node ready for Electron 43.2.0`

Confirmed by diffing the live file against the backup afterwards — backup `has18=False`, live `has18=True, v145=True`.

The resulting addon was then exercised end to end: `KINO_ELECTRON_CAPTURE=shared` rendered glass-morph through the DXGI → NVENC path at 354/354 frames, verified against the software encode at 46.7 dB PSNR with matching per-channel means (no R/B swap) and upright orientation.

author: clubanderson
body:
## Problem

On a GitHub Enterprise hive (`github.ibm.com`), the **guide** agent cannot read repository content because `git clone` over HTTPS fails:

```
fatal: could not read Username for 'https://github.ibm.com': terminal prompts disabled
```

Meanwhile **scanner** and **quality** on the same hive read repo content fine — they go through the GitHub API (App installation token), not `git clone`. The failure is isolated to guide's git-clone-over-HTTPS path. This is a config/credential-helper bug, not a GitHub App permission problem — the App installation itself is fine, and 403/scope hypotheses in guide's own finding history were stale re-diagnosis before it converged on the credential helper.

Two independent bugs cause this:

### 1. `bin/git-credential-hive.sh` only ever answered for `github.com`

git's credential-helper protocol has git pass `protocol=https` / `host=<the-remote-host>` on stdin for a `get` request. This script ignored that entirely and always echoed back `host=github.com` in its response, regardless of what host git actually asked about. git matches credential helpers (and validates the credential they return) by exact host, so for any `github.ibm.com` remote, this helper effectively returned **no usable credential** — git then fell through to an interactive prompt, which fails hard in a non-interactive agent shell with the "terminal prompts disabled" error above.

**Fix**: the helper now reads git's stdin request (`protocol=`/`host=`) and echoes back the *same* host it was asked about, gated to `https` only. The underlying credential is unchanged — it's still the cached GitHub App installation token at `/var/run/hive-metrics/gh-app-token.cache` (or the per-agent scoped token), the exact same token source scanner/quality's API calls use. This is host-agnostic by design: it works for `github.com`, `github.ibm.com`, or any other configured GHE host without special-casing any of them.

### 2. `v2/deploy/entrypoint.sh` only ever wired the helper for `github.com`

Even with the helper fixed, git never invokes it for a host with no `credential.<url>.helper` entry. `entrypoint.sh` only ran:
```
git config --global credential.https://github.com.helper /usr/local/bin/git-credential-hive.sh
```
so a GHE hive's git config had no helper registered for `github.ibm.com` at all.

**Fix**: added a second `credential.https://<host>.helper` registration, where `<host>` is derived from the hive's configured `github.base_url` / `github.api_url` (`hive.yaml`) — preferring `base_url`, falling back to the host portion of `api_url`, stripping scheme and a trailing `/api/v3`. This mirrors exactly how `GitHubConfig.HostLabel()` derives the host in Go (`pkg/config/config.go`). It's general across any GHE host (not just github.ibm.com), and a no-op on a plain github.com hive (derivation yields nothing extra to wire, since github.com already has its helper registered above).

### 3. `HIVE_REPO_DIR` was `/`

Separately flagged in guide's diagnosis: `HIVE_REPO_DIR` resolved to `/` and guide's workspace (`/data/agents/guide/workspace`) stayed empty.

Root cause: `bin/hive-config.sh` derived `HIVE_REPO_DIR` as `dirname("${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/..`. In the shipped container this file is *copied* (not checked out) to `/usr/local/bin/hive-config.sh`, so that derivation was already wrong (`/usr/local`, not a real checkout) — and it gets actively dangerous when `BASH_SOURCE[0]` is empty in the sourcing context: `dirname ""` returns `"."`, so `cd "./.."` resolves relative to whatever the *caller's* cwd was. `entrypoint.sh` sources this file as root before any `cd`, so the cwd can be `/` — landing `HIVE_REPO_DIR` on `/`.

**Fix**: dropped the `BASH_SOURCE`-based derivation entirely. `HIVE_REPO_DIR` now defaults to `/tmp/hive` (the same fallback the original code already intended for the "cd failed" case) unless explicitly overridden, plus a guard that refuses an empty or `/` value and falls back safely. Added the same guard in the one real consumer, `bin/hive-deploy.sh`, which does a destructive `git reset --hard` / `git checkout --force` inside `$HIVE_REPO_DIR` — so a stray `/` there is not just wrong, it's dangerous.

## Files changed

- `bin/git-credential-hive.sh` — host-aware credential response (parses git's stdin request instead of hardcoding `github.com`)
- `v2/deploy/entrypoint.sh` — wires `credential.https://<host>.helper` for the hive's actual configured GitHub host, derived the same way `GitHubConfig.HostLabel()` derives it in Go
- `bin/hive-config.sh` — fixed `HIVE_REPO_DIR` derivation bug + added an empty/`/` guard
- `bin/hive-deploy.sh` — added the same guard at its one real consumption point (defense in depth against a destructive git operation on `/`)

## Scope / regression check

- General across **any** GHE host — host is derived from the hive's own `github.base_url`/`api_url` config, never hardcoded to `github.ibm.com`.
- No behavior change on a plain `github.com` hive: the existing `credential.https://github.com.helper` wiring is untouched, and the new GHE-host wiring is a no-op when the config resolves to public GitHub.
- No Go files touched, so no Go-level test gap opened by this change; `go build ./...` passes unaffected. The shell changes were verified by hand (credential-helper host-echo logic against `github.ibm.com`, `github.com`, a non-`https` protocol, and a no-stdin legacy call; the entrypoint's host-derivation snippet against a GHE config with `base_url`, a GHE config with only `api_url`, and a plain public config). `shellcheck` is clean on all four changed files — only pre-existing warnings elsewhere in `entrypoint.sh`/`hive-deploy.sh` remain, none introduced here.

body:
## Summary

**INVENTORY · I-LA5 — repository-only, INERT, unexported.** Implements the production-shaped `resolveLocationActive` resolver and **pins** it into the still-unexported `receiveInventoryStock` command via a production composition. Governed by the merged **§3A** validator. Not exported from `index.ts`; no callable; **no permissive/existence-only stub**.

Base `1b04441`, single-parent. **7 files**, backend + CI only.

## Resolver (`receivingLocationResolver.ts`)

`makeResolveWarehouseLocationActive(db)` → `(txn, { type, locationId }) => Promise<boolean>`. Reads `warehouses/{locationId}` **through the passed transaction** and returns **true IFF**: `type === "WAREHOUSE"`, `locationId` non-blank, the doc exists, the **complete** document passes `validateGovernedWarehouse(data, locationId)`, and the validated `status === "ACTIVE"`. Returns **false** (no raw leak) for non-WAREHOUSE types, blank/invalid id, missing doc, **id mismatch**, `INACTIVE`, missing/malformed/legacy/partial §3A records, **lingering `active`**, and invalid provenance/metadata.

## Composition (`receiveInventoryStockComposition.ts`)

`buildReceiveInventoryStockDeps` / `receiveInventoryStockProduction` pin the concrete resolver into the command; the composition input type **omits** `resolveLocationActive` and the test-only hooks, so **no production caller can supply an arbitrary resolver**. Lower-level DI stays on the command for focused tests.

## Command change (minimal)

Added a **test-only** optional `__afterLocationReadHook` (undefined in production) so the concurrency test can flip the warehouse after the resolver read. No behavior change; the resolver read is in the command's transaction, preserving **all-or-nothing** + `DESTINATION_INVALID` mapping.

## Transaction boundary

The resolver reads `warehouses/{locationId}` in the command's transaction. A concurrent `ACTIVE→INACTIVE` transition therefore conflicts the command's commit and fails closed (no stale receipt). *(On the emulator this surfaces as a raw transaction-conflict; real Firestore `ABORT`s and retries, and the retry's resolver re-read of `INACTIVE` yields `DESTINATION_INVALID` — both never commit.)*

## Tests — 14 new + 18 regression

- **9 offline** (`receivingLocationResolver.test.mjs`): ACTIVE → true (read through txn); INACTIVE; non-WAREHOUSE (no read); blank/invalid id; missing; id mismatch; ACTIVE-but-missing version/updated/provenance; lingering `active`; malformed/unknown-status.
- **5 emulator** (`receiveInventoryStockResolverIntegration.test.mjs`): ACTIVE receipt proceeds atomically; INACTIVE → `DESTINATION_INVALID` + zero writes; missing → `DESTINATION_INVALID`; non-WAREHOUSE type → `DESTINATION_INVALID`; **concurrent `ACTIVE→INACTIVE` after the resolver read cannot commit a receipt** (fail closed, zero writes).
- **Existing `receiveInventoryStock` regression stays GREEN (18/18)** — success, rollback, idempotency, authorization + commit-time revocation, immutable PO, ledger, audit, closeout.

Full functions `tsc`: **passes**.

## Inert — zero runtime consumers

`index.ts` references none of the resolver/composition; no other runtime importer beyond tests. No callable export, capability grant, Rules/index/`firebase.json`, migration execution, option-service export, `field-ops-app-vite/**`, or deploy.

## Status

Held at **DRAFT** for Codex review and separate Owner authorization. No merge, no deploy.

body:
## Summary

Cuts the assets UI over from Zustand/`localStorage` to the Task 2 API via Task 3 TanStack Query hooks. Server state is the source of truth now; the old domain persist store is gone.

## Problem

Phase 1 kept assets and types in a persisted Zustand store. After the API and query layer landed, the UI was still on the client cache, so we had two sources of truth and no real path to production data.

## What changed

- List, archived, detail, add/edit, types settings, and onboarding now use Query hooks + mutations
- Filters go to the list API (`filtersToListQuery`); loading/error/empty states wired in
- Conflicts map to existing copy (duplicate unique ID, type-in-use delete, restore clash)
- Domain Zustand store removed; only a tiny UI store remains for onboarding dismiss
- Active/archived lists share one `AssetsTablePage` instead of two near-copies
- Type settings no longer downloads assets just to count them — delete relies on API `CONFLICT`
- Type create/edit waits for the mutation before closing the modal

## Why

Keep the cutover boring: pages call the feature API module, not a parallel client. Shared list shell and CONFLICT-only type delete avoid copying complexity or inventing fake counts from a capped fetch. KPIs: `meta.total` for total assets; open actions / inspections are labeled as page-local until we have real aggregates.

## Out of scope

- Auth / org scoping
- Server-side KPI aggregates or pagination UX beyond the current list limit
- New product pages or dashboard work
- Perfect type-name search (API searches unique ID + display name)


## Manual test plan

- [ ] Create type → add asset → edit → archive → restore
- [ ] Duplicate unique ID on create/edit/restore shows the conflict message
- [ ] Delete a type still in use is blocked with the existing copy
- [ ] Empty/loading/error paths on list and forms look sane
- [ ] Onboarding dismiss still persists; clearing old `assetflow-assets` localStorage is fine

author: suchethac
body:
Two commits, read in order: the first writes #1396's never-written acceptance criterion and pins the defect it exposes; the second fixes it.

## Commit 1 — the missing criterion (#1396)

Acceptance criterion 6 of #1396 —

> *Round-trip validation: a tabulated history that reproduces a parametric SFH gives photometry matching the parametric model's, to tolerance — the test that proves the histories are actually being used.*

— was the one criterion never built. Its absence is how #1522 shipped green: every other test in the W6 suite asserts a galaxy-to-galaxy **ratio**, and the truncation multiplies every galaxy by the same factor, which a ratio divides straight out.

Measured agreement between the two arms on a grid where nothing falls off the end: **1.9e-4** color, 1.0e-4 normalization, 1.8e-5 formed mass — invariant over `n_t` = 128…4096, so a fixed quadrature difference rather than table sampling.

### The fixture had to be built for it

`synthetic_ssp_wide` is **separable** — `base(wave) * f(age) * g(met)` — so its wavelength shape is identical at every age and the SED shape cannot respond to the SFH at all. Measured: doubling τ moves its colors by **3.6e-14**. A color assertion there passes no matter what the code does. The round-trip therefore ships its own age-reddening SSP, a negative control (2× τ lands 92× outside tolerance; a 1 % error just outside), and a test asserting the fixture is non-separable so it cannot quietly become vacuous again.

## Commit 2 — the fix (#1522)

A tabulated history is interpolated onto the SSP lookback-age grid, and the dense integrand spans only `[ssp_ages[0], ssp_ages[-1]]`. Mass beyond the oldest template was never sampled — silently. **27.5 %** lost on an 8 Gyr grid at z=0.05; **46 %** at z=0 on the real PARSEC/MILES grid for a history anchored at the Big Bang.

The same axis was already guarded at its other end: `_build_dsps_sfh_table` zeroes and warns for ages older than the universe (#683), and `_youngest_bin_lookback_multiplier` extends the youngest bin to lookback 0 (#821). One end loud, the other silent.

`_extend_integrand_to_history` appends a tail out to the history's own oldest node. Those parcels sit past the last node, so their CIC fraction clips to 1.0 and they land wholly on the oldest template. When the history stops inside the grid the tail collapses onto repeats of the last node — zero trapezoid width, an exact no-op, which keeps the shape static under jit.

| grid oldest bin | `stellar_mass` / table integral |
|---|---|
| 8 Gyr (truncating) | 0.99998244 |
| 13.8 Gyr (nothing falls off) | 0.99998244 |

The grid edge no longer enters the mass at all.

**Scope.** Only tabulated histories. Parametric and non-parametric families renormalize to `log_total_mass` *after* landing weights on the grid, so mass falling off the end is scaled back in and their totals were never wrong; extending their integrand would move weight onto the oldest template and change long-settled numbers for no correctness gain.

**What remains — now announced, not silent:**

- Those stars still wear the oldest template's colors; no template exists for them. New `SFHBeyondSSPGridWarning` reports the fraction and the template age. Eager paths only, skipped under jit — the same contract `SFHBeforeBigBangWarning` carries, so `Catalog.simulate` (jitted) stays quiet. Tested both ways: it fires on the truncating grid and a negative control asserts it does *not* fire when the history sits inside the grid.
- `age_kernel="dsps"` still truncates — that kernel bins onto `ssp_lg_age_gyr` itself and has no bin past the last template, which an integrand fix cannot reach. Opt-in for cross-code comparison (#964), so the behavior stands, but it now warns with "DROPPED" wording and names `age_kernel='cic'` as the fix. Verified: mass 0.7125, warning raised.

**Also folds three copies of the CIC integrand construction into one `_cic_integrand`** — `apply`'s delta and per-age-metallicity branches, and `compute_joint_weights`. They were identical line for line and had to stay so: #982 exists because a divergence between `apply` and the fast path is invisible until the two disagree on a fit. Building it once means an edge fix cannot land in two of the three.

## Verification

| tree | result |
|---|---|
| `tests/components` | 2419 passed |
| `tests/physics` | 432 passed |
| `tests/unit` | 278 passed |
| W6 + #1522 | 33 passed |
| age-weight set, serial | 76 passed |

The age-weight set is the targeted blast radius: #964 (old edge), #538 (young knot), #758, #765, #1016, #1030, #1395, #29, the `age_kernel` contract and the `csp_integration` contract.

`tests/regression` and `tests/contract` OOM this box under xdist — every failure reads `worker 'gwN' crashed`, and the counts move run to run (4 then 17). Left to CI's shards, which have the headroom.

All 12 lint gates green, each run individually rather than fail-fast.

Closes #1522. #1396 can close once this merges (criterion 6 was its last open box).

author: dtiern55
body:
The old driver was scripted against known results — each bot had a skill percentage deciding how often to use the actual boot:

```python
def pick(kind) -> str:
    """A boot on a hit, a random non-boot on a miss."""
    if hits(kind) or not wrong_pool:
        return boots[...]      # the actual answer
```

Two problems. It made every measurement of player behaviour circular — the rank movements and play-frequency numbers I cited across #300 and #307 were bots echoing back an input. And it could only run on a season already watched, which rules out using it for David vs. Goliath.

## What changes

The commissioner writes a **pre-episode read** (`scripts/bot_reads/season_N.json`): who the room would vote out, who they'd aim a double at, and a draft desirability order. Bots sample from it; survivoR supplies the outcome. Nothing in the pipeline knows the result before the commissioner does.

Picks come from an exponential race weighted by each persona's `spread`, so bots **cluster without being identical** — real leagues read the same edit and converge, which independent coin-flip bots could never reproduce.

Seventeen bots, the agreed mix: 4 consensus, 6 reader, 2 contrarian, 3 roster loyalist, 2 vote gambler. Rewritten for the weekly play (#307) — one play per episode, no tokens, and a swap past the free one spends it.

`play N` becomes `week N` deliberately: the semantics inverted from *after* an episode to *before* it, and a silently-reversed verb would be a nasty way to find that out.

## Verified locally, end to end

| | |
|---|---|
| Draft | over-rosters the named favourites, as intended |
| Clustering | 15 of 17 bots on the top read name, tail spreading |
| Cascade | booting the most-rostered castaway triggered 17 free swaps |
| Charged swaps | a second boot forced 14 swaps that consumed 14 plays |
| Persona integrity | only the 3 loyalists kept a double — they carry a dead slot rather than trade it |
| Idempotency | every command re-runs to zero |

Two bugs found and fixed during that testing: the draft was including castaways already voted out at roster lock, and the flex personas collapsed to "roster double every week" because the draft over-rosters exactly the names the read marks as targets — they now weigh how confident the read is about the boot.

Also adds `bot_reads/README.md` documenting the format and the three things that steer bot behaviour most.

author: mdheller
body:
## Summary

Two first-class WebExtensions closing BearBrowser's biggest competitive gaps vs Arc and Firefox.

---

### Bear Spaces (`extensions/bear-spaces/`) — Arc Spaces gap

Arc's defining feature: named spaces isolate tabs with separate identities.

- **Named spaces** (Work / Personal / Research seeded by default) — create, rename, delete
- **Tab isolation** — `browser.tabs.hide()` hides non-active-space tabs; switching restores them
- **Auto-assignment** — new tabs while in a space are automatically assigned to it
- **Context menu** — right-click: "Assign tab to Space ▶" per-space submenu
- **Memory mesh** — every space switch fires `POST localhost:7788/api/append` (silent fail)
- Sidebar panel + browser action; full `browser.storage.local` persistence

### Bear Containers (`extensions/bear-containers/`) — Firefox Multi-Account Containers gap

Firefox's most-used privacy feature: cookie/storage isolation per container.

- **Seeds Personal / Work / Shopping / Banking** containers on first install (idempotent)
- **Tab reassignment** — create new tab in target container then remove old (no flash)
- **Context menu** — right-click: "Open in Container ▶" submenu rebuilt on install + startup
- **Popup** — current tab's container at top; one-click switch; new container form with color picker
- **Memory mesh** — container switches push events to mesh (silent fail)
- Graceful fallback when `contextualIdentities` API unavailable (shows enable instructions)
- Requires: LibreWolf → Preferences → Privacy → Enable Container Tabs

---

## Load instructions

**Both extensions** — `about:debugging` → **This Firefox** → **Load Temporary Add-on…** → select `manifest.json` in each extension directory.

For Bear Containers: enable container tabs in LibreWolf preferences first.

## Test plan

**Spaces:**
- [ ] Default spaces appear; switch hides/shows tabs correctly
- [ ] New tab in active space auto-assigned
- [ ] Right-click → Assign works across spaces
- [ ] Rename / delete via sidebar

author: bonclay7
body:
# feat(petfood-rs + cdk): OTel metrics migration and managed Prometheus collector

  This PR delivers two related workshop changes: (1) migrates petfood-rs from
  Prometheus-native metrics to the OpenTelemetry SDK, and (2) adds a CDK construct
  that pre-creates an Amazon Managed Prometheus Collector with a CloudWatch dataset
  destination, powering a new workshop module.

  ## Part 1: petfood-rs OTel migration

  Migrate from the raw `prometheus` crate to the OpenTelemetry Meter API so metrics
  flow through the same OTLP pipeline as traces. This eliminates the Prometheus
  `/metrics` scrape endpoint in favor of push-based export to the CloudWatch Agent
  sidecar on `localhost:4317`.

  ### Changes
  - Enable `metrics` feature on `opentelemetry`, `opentelemetry_sdk`,
  `opentelemetry-otlp`
  - Remove `prometheus` crate dependency
  - Rewrite `observability/metrics.rs` using OTel `Counter`, `Histogram`,
  `UpDownCounter`
  - Add `init_opentelemetry_metrics()` OTLP metrics pipeline in `tracing.rs`
  - Remove `/metrics` handler and route
  - Update middleware to record via OTel instruments; drop `encode()` assertions from
  tests

  ### Metric names follow OTel semantic conventions
  - `http.server.request.total`, `http.server.request.duration`,
  `http.server.active_requests`
  - `db.client.operation.total`, `db.client.operation.duration`
  - `petfood.food.operation.total`, `petfood.cart.operation.total`,
    `petfood.recommendation.request.total`, `petfood.error_simulation.trigger.total`

  In PromQL, dots flatten to underscores (e.g., `http_server_request_total`).

  ## Part 2: Managed Prometheus Collector CDK construct

  Adds a new CDK construct behind the `CUSTOM_ENABLE_ZEUS` flag that pre-creates an
  Amazon Managed Prometheus scraper delivering to a CloudWatch dataset. This
  supports a new workshop module that would otherwise need participants to wait
  ~15 minutes for scraper provisioning.

  ### New: `src/cdk/lib/constructs/managed-prometheus-collector.ts`
  - Uses `AwsCustomResource` to call `amp:CreateScraper` with `cloudWatchConfiguration`
    destination (this destination type is not yet modeled in CloudFormation)
  - Delivers to `arn:aws:cloudwatch:REGION:ACCOUNT:dataset/default` by default
  - Uses AWS Cloud Map DNS service discovery (`dns_sd_configs`) targeting services in
    the `Workshop-space` namespace on port 8080
  - Adds a self-referencing ingress rule on the ECS security group (port 8080)
  - Pre-creates with a single target (`payforadoption-go`); participants add
    `petlistadoption-py` via a hands-on `aws amp update-scraper` exercise
  - Exports scraper metadata via SSM Parameter Store:
    - `/petstore/prometheus-collector/scraper-id`
    - `/petstore/prometheus-collector/scrape-config-yaml` (initial single-service
  config)
    - `/petstore/prometheus-collector/scrape-config-yaml-with-all-targets` (target
  config for the update exercise)
    - `/petstore/prometheus-collector/dataset-arn`
    - `/petstore/prometheus-collector/alias`

author: egorbo
body:
Backport of #131736 to release/10.0


## Customer Impact

- [x] Customer reported
- [ ] Found internally

Reported in #131716. Wrong code on x64: a `switch` with exactly 64 cases and two distinct targets branches to the *opposite* target. `TryLowerSwitchToBitTest` inverts the bit table when its upper 32 bits are all set (so the table still fits a 32-bit immediate) and swaps the two targets, but the swap only updated `bbCase0`/`bbCase1` while the code after it consumes `case0Edge`/`case1Edge`. So `SetCond` wired the `JCC` to the wrong successor and the dup-count fixup decremented `bbRefs` on the wrong blocks.

This shape is very easy to hit from Roslyn's `async` state-machine dispatch: an `async IAsyncEnumerable<T>`/`async` method with 61 awaits+yields produces exactly a 64-entry, two-target jump table. The reporter saw the iterator body re-entered millions of times (hang) and frameless `NullReferenceException`s on captured variables. Reproduces at Tier0, MinOpts and fully optimized code.

## Regression

- [x] Yes
- [ ] No

Introduced in .NET 10 by #116933, which replaced the `fgRemoveAllRefPreds`/`fgAddRefPred` pair (that re-derived the edges from the swapped blocks) with in-place dup-count adjustment, leaving the edge swap behind.

## Testing

Added regression test `Runtime_131716`, covering both the inverted (64-case) and non-inverted bit table shapes. Fails without the fix, passes with it. The original PR also ran SPMI: no asm diffs on benchmarks.run, libraries.pmi and libraries.crossgen2 (~660K contexts).

## Risk

Low.

author: notdoogles
body:
## What

Adds a **Skip** button next to Guess that passes on the current message. It advances to the next message and consumes one guess — exactly like a wrong guess — but does **not** reveal the easy-mode hint that a real guess would unlock. Skipping the last message ends the round as a loss, same as running out of guesses.

## Why

Players sometimes get stuck on a message they don't recognize (e.g. a low-effort or off-topic line) and want to move on without wasting a guess *and* without being handed a free hint. This gives them that middle option.

## How

- **`lib/game.ts`**: extracted a shared `fetchRound()` helper (round + answerer color/badges lookup); added `skipMessage(roundId, guessNumber)` which behaves like the wrong-guess path of `submitGuess` but never returns the `hint` field.
- **`app/api/game/skip/route.ts`** (new): `POST /api/game/skip` mirroring the guess route's validation/logging.
- **`components/GameBoard.tsx`**: Skip button in the input row; `handleSkip()` posts to the new endpoint and updates state/persistence. Skips are recorded in the same guesses list (so they consume a pip and appear in history) but render with a distinct `⏭` marker instead of a ❌.
- **`components/GameBoard.module.css`**: ghost-style `.skipButton` secondary to the primary Guess button.

## Tests

- 5 new `skipMessage` unit tests: unknown round, invalid index, advances + burns a guess, **no hint revealed** (even at hint-unlock boundaries), and game-over-as-loss on the last message.
- Full web suite: 141 tests pass; `tsc --noEmit`, `next lint`, and `next build` all clean.

author: feihou
body:
## What

- Keep the realtime audio-buffer callback behind a stable reference while it is shared through `OSAllocatedUnfairLock`.
- Release retired callback captures after unlocking.
- Add a regression test that performs 20,000 buffer deliveries and then clears the callback.

## Why

Long recordings repeatedly read the callback from lock-backed closure storage. Swift accumulated nested closure reabstraction wrappers, and clearing the callback during recorder shutdown recursively released that chain until the app stack-overflowed.

That crash happened before `RecordingSession.finish` could persist the meeting. The recording therefore disappeared from the meeting list, and the next orphan sweep could remove its unreferenced audio file.

author: jonathanmcohen
body:
Implements the storage foundation from the spec in #164.

## The problem this fixes

Assets were **disk-only** under `${filesRoot}/.assets/<docId>/`, invisible to
Postgres. `pgbackweb` backs up the database; the asset bytes lived only in the
container volume. **A restore returned documents with broken images.**

## What landed

- **`0028_db_backed_assets.sql` + schema** - `assets(doc_id, filename, mime, byte_size, sha256, bytes)`, unique on `(doc_id, filename)`, cascade delete.
- **`lib/uploads/assets-repo.ts`** - upsert/get/list/delete plus a DB-based quota sum.
- **Upload route** writes the row **before** placing bytes, so a failed byte write cannot leave an unrecorded file behind.
- **Serve route** reads the DB first, falling back to disk for pre-v0.2.12 assets.
- **Quota** switches from globbing `.assets` to `sum(byte_size)` - cheaper, and correct after a restore.

S3 is untouched: when `BACKUP_S3_*` is configured the bytes stay in S3 and `bytes`
is null, but the row is still written so metadata, quota and the mirror share one
source. The spec had not accounted for the existing S3 adapter; this does.

## A mistake worth flagging, because it shaped the design

My first revision had `putAsset` write the DB row. That made
`lib/uploads/store.ts` impossible to unit-test without Postgres and **broke
`tests/unit/uploads-store.test.ts`** - 4 failures with `ECONNREFUSED`. I confirmed
it was mine by stashing and re-running against `main`, where it passed.

Fixed properly rather than by mocking: DB concerns moved into the route layer, and
the storage adapter went back to pure byte placement. That is also the better
separation - the adapter is about *where bytes go*, not about rows.

## The safety constraint (spec D3)

Asset sync is **one-directional, DB to disk**. `relPathIfManaged()` already
rejected `<DocName>.assets/` via its `endsWith` arm; that is now documented and
**pinned by tests**, so an image on disk can never be mistaken for an edited
document. Documents already reconcile four shadows and that is exactly what let
the release-notes bug survive three fixes. Assets get two shadows and one writer.

## Not in this PR

- Writing the mirror copy **beside the `.md`** and rewriting markdown references.
- Migrating the existing legacy assets (production holds **1 file, 12 KB**).
- The legacy `.assets` tree is still written this release, deliberately, as the rollback path.

This is the storage foundation; the mirror half is the follow-up.

## Gates

- **2460 unit tests pass** (7 new), typecheck 0, biome clean on changed files.
- Not yet live-verified. Per the honesty rule this is **not** DONE until it is.

author: aaron-zeisler
body:
## Summary

Makes the Relay Proxy reject SDK keys and mobile keys that are scoped to a view, so they never enter the accepted credential set. Filtering happens in `envfactory.BuildAcceptedSet` so a view-scoped key is absent from the credential lookup map entirely. An SDK presenting one gets a 401.

## Background

A view-scoped key (payload filtering v2) is only entitled to a subset of its environment's flags. Relay serves the entire environment payload and has no view support, so accepting one would silently over-deliver every flag in the environment to an SDK that only wants a subset.

## Commit details

The first two commits are the feature, the third is a cleanup task.

**1. `chore: carry the hasViews marker through the credential wire format`**

Adds a `hasViews` flag to each SDK key and mobile key the backend sends us, and passes it inward to where relay assembles an environment's credentials. Nothing acts on it yet.

**2. and 3. `fix: reject SDK keys and mobile keys scoped to a view`** 

Discards view-scoped keys while the payload is being read, so they never join the set of credentials an environment will accept and an SDK presenting one is turned away as unrecognized. An environment's own default SDK key and mobile key are deliberately exempt, since refusing either of those would take the whole environment offline.

**4. `refactor: make every credential-set rejection a malformed-payload error`**

When a payload left us with no usable SDK key, relay reported that as a different kind of error than it uses for other unusable payloads, which made offline mode log a misleading reason. They are now the same kind, so nothing downstream has to tell them apart.

## Integration coverage

Integration tests for this change are stacked in #796 .

## Open questions for review

**Should `/status` show the rejected view-scoped keys?**, so support can diagnose without asking the customer for logs? Deliberately excluded here: it would require carrying view-scoped values into `EnvContext`, reintroducing exactly the state the ingestion filter exists to avoid, and would add a field to a rep that was only just stabilized.


<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> **Overview**
> Relay now reads **`hasViews`** on each `sdkKeys` / `mobileKeys` entry and **drops view-scoped credentials in `BuildAcceptedSet`**, so they never enter the accepted lookup map and SDKs using them get **401**. The environment **anchor SDK key** and **primary mobile key** are always kept even if marked view-scoped.
> 
> **`BuildAcceptedSet`** now returns **`(AcceptedSet, []string, error)`** — the string list is wire **key** identifiers that were filtered — and auto-config / offline handlers **WARN** when any were rejected. Stream **credential validation** still fails only on errors (malformed payloads), not on filtered keys.
> 
> An environment with **no usable SDK key** after filtering (empty `sdkKeys[]` or every entry view-scoped) is treated like other bad payloads via **`MalformedCredentialSetError`** (`no usable SDK key in sdkKeys[]`), replacing the separate builder error so offline mode logs consistently.
> 
> <sup>Reviewed by [Cursor Bugbot](https://cursor.com/bugbot) for commit cef83932f283b43d4064373f217a139544e35964. Bugbot is set up for automated code reviews on this repo. Configure [here](https://www.cursor.com/dashboard/bugbot).</sup>

body:
Part of #4. Fixes the last "diff pipeline" serial failure.

## Problem
In char-cell (TUI) rendering, removed/replaced diff lines render as ghost rows that `DisplayLattice` reads from `CharCellState::temporary_blocks`. But `RenderState::layout_temporary_blocks` only laid incoming `TemporaryBlock`s into the **GUI** block tree (`reset_temporary_block`) — nothing populated the char-cell ghost list outside tests. So a TUI diff body rendered **zero** removed/ghost lines (`display_lattice().ghosts()` was always empty).

## Fix
When the render state is in char-cell mode, translate the temporary blocks via the existing `CharCellTemporaryBlock::from_temporary_block` and store them with `set_temporary_blocks`, instead of the GUI block-tree path (char-cell rendering doesn't consult that tree).

## Result
- `diff_pipeline_computes_added_lines_and_ghost_blocks` passes (1 ghost, content `"old\n"`, `insert_before` line 1).
