author: theaddonn
body:
## Summary

Rebuilds nbtx's NBT/SNBT codec on [`facet`](https://github.com/facet-rs/facet) reflection instead of `serde`. Breaking, hence the major version bump. The wire format itself is unchanged and byte-for-byte identical to 3.x for all three variants (big-endian, little-endian, varint).

## Public API changes

- Generic bound moves from `Serialize`/`Deserialize` to `Facet`.
- `NetworkLittleEndian`/`Variant::NetworkEndian` renamed to `VarintEndian`/`Variant::VarintEndian`; `to_net_bytes*` renamed to `to_varint_bytes*`.
- Removed the `NbtString`/`NbtByteArray`/`NbtIntArray`/`NbtLongArray` newtype wrappers. Non-UTF-8 strings and tag-precise arrays go through the dynamic `Value` type, or a bare `bstr::BString` field.
- `Value::Compound` is backed by an order-preserving `IndexMap` by default (`preserve_order` feature; falls back to a sorted `BTreeMap` without it), so on-disk key order round-trips.
- Added `Named<T>`, a wrapper for reading/writing an explicit root name — the plain entry points always write/expect an empty root name now, matching real Bedrock encoders.
- `nbt` and `snbt` are independent Cargo features; neither implies the other. Both are in `default`, along with `preserve_order`.
- Unknown compound keys are rejected by default when decoding into a derived struct (`Error::UnknownField`); opt out per-struct with `#[facet(nbtx::allow_unknown_fields)]`.
- `facet`/`bstr` are **not** re-exported. `#[derive(Facet)]` expands to `::facet::`-rooted paths, so a deriving crate needs `facet` itself as a direct dependency regardless of any re-export — and re-exporting facet's full surface would make nbtx's own API hostage to changes in a pre-1.0, git-pinned dependency. See the installation section of the README for the exact dependency lines.

## Hardening

Cross-checked against two independent, long-established NBT implementations (one PHP, one Go) to find wire-format and semantics gaps. Findings, folded in here:

- Bounded recursion depth (512) on every codec path, read and write. Previously a few KB of nested containers could overflow the stack and abort the process — uncatchable in Rust.
- Bounded varint reads (5/10 bytes for 32/64-bit ints). An overlong varint used to panic in debug builds and silently misdecode in release.
- Enforced max string length (32767 bytes) on write, for string payloads, compound keys, and root names — replacing an unchecked `as u16` cast that could wrap and emit an undecodable stream.
- Duplicate compound keys now keep the first occurrence on decode (previously last-wins).
- A heterogeneous `Value::List` (elements with different NBT tags) is now a decode/encode-time error instead of silently desyncing the stream.
- SNBT string values now escape/unescape `"` and `\`.

## Other

- `FieldType`, `Variant`/`EndiannessImpl`, and the `Compound` type alias moved out of `lib.rs` into their own modules.
- Test suite reorganized into topic-focused files under `tests/` (fixtures moved to `tests/fixtures/`) and substantially expanded — 146 → 338 tests, including property-based round-trip tests via `proptest`.
- Examples rewritten to cover the full public API: all three endianness variants, the dynamic `Value` type, named roots, non-UTF-8 strings, unknown-field handling, error handling, and SNBT.

## Testing

`cargo test`, `cargo test --all-features`, and `cargo test --no-default-features --features nbt,snbt` all pass (338/338/334 tests, 0 failures). `cargo clippy --all-targets --all-features` and `cargo fmt --check` are clean. All 11 examples run successfully.

## Also includes: `to_value`/`from_value`

Implements #16 (previously attempted in #17, now closed in favor of this) on the new facet engine: `nbtx::to_value`/`nbtx::from_value` convert directly between a `#[derive(Facet)]` struct and the dynamic `Value` type, without encoding to or decoding from NBT bytes. Same type-to-tag convention, `MAX_DEPTH` enforcement, and unknown-field handling as the binary codec; unconditionally available (no `nbt`/`snbt` feature needed, since neither touches wire bytes). The Rust-type-to-NBT-tag convention, previously duplicated across `nbt::ser`/`nbt::de`/`snbt::ser`/`snbt::de`, is now defined once in a shared `reflect` module all four (plus the new conversion) draw from.

Two divergences from the binary codec are inherent to a `Value` tree having no wire framing (documented, tested): a `Named<T>` root converts as a plain compound (no root-name slot to write), and a heterogeneous `Value::List` round-trips instead of erroring (no single element-type byte to enforce it against).


## Also includes: direct enum support (#14)

`#[facet(nbtx::variant_as(<mode>))]` — a new mandatory container attribute on every enum used with nbtx, `<mode>` one of `u8`/`i8`/`u16`/`i16`/`u32`/`i32`/`u64`/`i64`/`str`. No silent default: an enum missing this attribute is a hard error the first time any codec (binary, SNBT, `to_value`/`from_value`) touches it. `str` is the existing variant-name-as-String-tag behavior, now explicit and fixed to respect `#[facet(rename = "...")]` on a variant (previously silently ignored). The integer modes write the variant's real discriminant as a fixed-width scalar tag, deliberately decoupled from the enum's own `#[repr(...)]` (a Rust-layout concern facet's derive needs regardless, unrelated to the wire format) — no `usize`/`isize`, since those aren't portable across architectures. A custom Rust discriminant assignment (`enum Foo { A = 5 }`) already controls the wire value with no further attribute needed.


## Also includes: lenient decode-time tag widths (#19)

`#[facet(nbtx::lenient_width(<types>))]` — a field-level attribute (also usable on an enum alongside `variant_as`) naming additional wire tags (`i8`/`i16`/`i32`/`i64`/`f32`/`f64`) a field accepts besides its own declared type, for real-world save data that doesn't always write the same tag for the same logical field (e.g. an `i32` field occasionally written as a `Byte`, or a `float` field written as a `Byte` on older saves). A listed-but-mismatched tag converts into the field's real type when the value is representable there without loss (exact-representability checks for int↔float, not just range checks) and errors distinctly otherwise (`Error::LenientWidthOutOfRange`, separate from the existing `Error::UnexpectedType` for a tag not in the list at all). Decode-only — encoding always writes a field's own declared tag, so re-encoding a leniently-decoded document normalizes it. Built on `facet-rs/facet#2638`'s new `list(shape_type)` attribute-grammar kind, which bumped nbtx's pinned facet rev.

author: asgeirf
body:
A kapi project now keeps ONE local database: `.kapi/store.db` — blocks, terms, content memory, unit state, and the property graph in one file, per-subsystem migration ledgers, opened once per (App, root). It is the local projection of the committed context (`context/terms.json`, `context/memory.json`, `.kapi/units/`, the content files) and the substrate of the local context graph. Design-from-start: no compatibility shims; predecessors are swept on first open (staged decisions fold forward); recipe keys `defaults.terms`, `defaults.state`, `defaults.memory.read` are gone.

**Measured, not assumed.** A contention harness at dogfood scale (75k blocks) showed a naive merge starves the working store (32/2,650 decision writes; the hot writer is the content memory's per-row FTS tokenization, not blocks). The shipped write discipline — immediate transactions + a FIFO write gate baked into `*storage.DB`'s write entry points + converge batching its memory write-back (112× cheaper than per-row Add) — holds: **zero post-timeout busy errors anywhere (today's split layout has 2), decision writes at 90% throughput, 12 ms absolute p95.** Two pre-existing bugs fixed on the way: today's layout already produced 15–20 busy errors/min under converge, and the FTS rebuilds were uncancellable.

**Use case 5 ships**: `kapi terms occurrences <term|concept>` answers "which blocks use this term" across the whole project locally — FTS-backed, no server — and `context_search` term hits carry usage counts. The graph store (`graph_nodes`/`graph_edges`) rides in the same file; edges are computed, not yet persisted (boundary recorded in AD-039).

**Dogfooded live, both sides on this branch**: sweep folded the repo project onto `store.db`; push 17,471 blocks; server translate; editor approval → decision ledger (durable KBF unit keys) + promotion into workspace memory with attribution; `kapi pull` staged it (now loudly — the count was previously computed and dropped); `kapi commit` wrote the shard. The loop also caught and fixed: `kapi pack` refusing run-only projects, `verify --terms` recommending a nonexistent recipe key, and `kapi memory`/`terms` missing `-p`.

Docs: new AD-039; AD-002/008/009/010/017/024/025/033 updated in place (resolving the recorded authoritative-vs-cache and `defaults.state` contradictions); both doc sites, the kapi skill, reference dataset + pages regenerated.

**Known debts, deliberate:**
- Walkthrough re-records owed: `kapi-bilingual-workflow` (command lines changed), `kapi-review-and-approve` + `kapi-project-workflow` (narration renames); `demo.nb.yaml` regenerates via `make l10n-demos` (l10n-verify will flag the drift until then).
- Three reworded CLI help strings orphan their committed nb translations (catalog-key semantics) — re-translation via the dogfood loop.
- Reconcile resolver still unwired: occurrence output's document column is empty (block names carry paths).
- The write gate cannot reach a second process; cross-process long extractions contend at the file level under immediate+busy_timeout (measured: 1 busy error in the harshest run).

author: chrischurchsc
body:
## The confusion

An object card had two inputs sitting under one **or**, and they produced different things.

- **"Describe this {kind}"** → Generate → mints the library record and fills its empty fields, binding `card.refId`. You get a real object in Records.
- **"or Hand it the document that already says it"** → upload a .md → set `card.reference` and stopped. **No record, no `refId`.** The card named nothing, read as unlinked in the grid, appeared nowhere in Records, and the file reached the copy writer down a separate channel (`wiredCardDocsFor`) that existed only for it.

You handed the app a document about an audience and the app did not learn an audience existed. They were not two ways to do one thing, they were two different things wearing the same layout.

## What changed

A document now **mints the object it describes and names it from its own H1**, and is stored **on that record**, so every campaign naming it reads the same brief.

Nothing else is filled. Mincing a brief into a dozen boxes stays rejected (`FlowsView.tsx:967`); what changed is that the document now has a visible home of its own, which is what made that objection true in the first place.

- `reference?: ObjectReference` on the twelve record types. It rides the existing jsonb `data` column, so it **syncs with no migration**, and it is deliberately absent from every `*_FIELDS`/`*_COLUMNS` list: a brief is a page, not a spreadsheet cell.
- `pickReference` is the single precedence rule (card overrides record). Both the inspector and the copy request call it, so the panel cannot show one document while the writer is sent another.
- `wiredCardDocsFor` resolves record docs and dedupes by the document's **owner**, so three cards naming one audience send one brief while a genuine override survives beside it.
- The **campaign-local override** appears only under a document that already exists, phrased as the departure it is. The remove control acts on whichever document is showing.
- A **Company card can be filled in at last**. An account's facts are never generated, because a generated account is a page of confident guesses about somebody real, which left nothing a Company card could be built from. Its document is that answer.
- **Records show the document**, where it can be read, replaced or removed.

## Two silent-drop bugs found while exercising it

- `patchAudience` read a render-captured list, so an audience minted and patched in one tick lost the patch **entirely and in silence**. It reads live now. Generate only escaped this by being slow enough to land after a re-render.
- Not every `apply` can mint: an Audience or proof point needs a brand, and with none picked `ensureAudienceRef` refuses. The document now falls back to the card and says why, rather than being acknowledged and lost.

## Also

The save bar stopped opening with "Saved." next to a button reading "Save updates". The card was already saved and that button never saved it: it rewrites assets drafted before the change, and now says so.

## Verified in the running app

Dropped a .md on a Message card: record **"Renewal is the moment"** created from the document's H1, document attached to it, card bound by `refId`, panel reading *"This is Renewal is the moment's own document. Every campaign that uses it reads this."* Survived a full reload with the doc on the record and `ownDoc: false` on the card. Appears in Records › Messages with a Document section (read / replace / remove). The no-brand fallback keeps the file and explains itself.

Not exercised: a real `/api/draft-copy` generation against a live model. The resolution it depends on is covered by domain tests.

476 tests pass (30 in `objectReference.test.ts`, incl. new coverage for record docs, override precedence, owner dedup and `titleFromDoc`). `tsc` and `vite build` clean, `changelog:check` green.

author: shubhammalhotra28
body:
## Problem
LFM2.5-2.6B (and other QHexRT NPU LLMs) capped chat output at **256 tokens**. The budget policy did
`contextOutputLimit = context / 2`, and LFM's `context_length` is 512 → 256.

That assumed output must fit inside the context window. **It doesn't** for these models: QHexRT NPU decoders
use a **KV ring (sliding window)** — they keep generating *coherently* past the context size, the ring just
forgets the oldest tokens. Verified on device (v81, SM8850): LFM2.5-2.6B streams **600 coherent tokens** on a
512 window (no garbage — clean prose start to finish). Only *context-bound* decoders (llama.cpp `n_ctx`,
cloud) actually need to reserve prompt room.

## Change
- `ChatGenerationBudgetPolicy.resolve(..., slidingWindow: Boolean = false)` — when `slidingWindow`, skip the
  `context / 2` clamp entirely (output isn't bounded by the small context).
- Raise `MAX_NORMAL_OUTPUT_TOKENS` **512 → 1024** so the freed-up models can produce longer answers.
- `ChatViewModel.generationOptions` passes `slidingWindow = (framework == QHEXRT)`.
- Context-bound models (llama.cpp / cloud) keep the existing half-window reservation, unchanged.

Net effect: LFM2.5-2.6B on the NPU now generates up to **1024** tokens (or the user's saved `maxTokens`),
instead of 256. History windowing (input trimming) is untouched.

## Tests
`ChatGenerationBudgetPolicyTest` updated: context-bound 512 → 256, **sliding-window 512 → 1024 (new case)**,
context-bound 1024 → 512, large-context/unknown-context cases → 1024 ceiling. All pass.

## Verified
Built + installed on v81; the raw runtime already proven to emit 600 coherent tokens on a 512 window.

<!-- This is an auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->

## Summary by CodeRabbit

* **New Features**
  * Increased the maximum normal chat response length from 512 to 1,024 tokens.
  * Improved support for sliding-window models, allowing longer responses based on the global output limit.
  * Updated QHexRT generation to take advantage of sliding-window context behavior.

* **Bug Fixes**
  * Preserved appropriate context limits for models that require reserving space for input.

author: czorpides
body:
## Why

EODHD materially improved Opportunity Radar coverage, but the broader 3,000-name US/UK/EU universe exposed several remaining evidence-integrity risks: long-horizon technicals still used raw closes, bare tickers were reused across providers, fundamental presence could be mistaken for freshness, global coverage could hide a broken region, and candidate eligibility did not explicitly fail closed when critical evidence was stale.

## What this PR changes

- uses `adj_close` (falling back to raw close only when needed) for Opportunity momentum/trend/volatility while retaining raw close for displayed/traded price
- records price-score provenance including adjusted-price basis and source id
- adds a weekly EODHD adjusted-history reconciliation pass so later dividend/split corrections can update historical `adj_close` values and immediately recompute affected Opportunity technical scores
- introduces canonical `asset_provider_symbols` keyed by `asset_id + provider`, with deterministic exchange-aware EODHD/FMP/Twelve Data/Tiingo/Alpha Vantage adapters and verified/failed mapping telemetry
- quarantines provider mappings that prove invalid instead of repeatedly retrying the same cross-market ticker assumption
- makes FMP fundamentals ingest by asset identity rather than ambiguous bare ticker; successful mapped responses verify the provider mapping and ambiguous direct ticker requests fail closed
- makes per-symbol price fallback/cross-verification provider-symbol aware, including exchange-qualified Twelve Data requests and US-only Tiingo/Alpha Vantage eligibility
- defines current-fundamental freshness as fresh <=45d, warning 46-100d and stale >100d; stale current metrics are excluded from valuation/quality peer ranks and warning-age data is confidence-docked
- freshness-gates Piotroski and Magic Formula as well so stale fundamentals cannot re-enter conviction through a side model
- adds current-vs-stale fundamental and statement readiness telemetry
- adds regional US/UK/EU price, 252-session and fresh-score readiness, with a 90% regional floor alongside the existing 95% global gate
- adds candidate-level freshness telemetry and an integrity overlay that removes stale critical technical/fundamental signals, recomputes the existing horizon model with the same weights, and prevents stale evidence from promoting production eligibility
- keeps candidates with incomplete fundamentals visible for research; market-data staleness holds nomination, while fundamental gaps reduce evidence/eligibility rather than falsely classifying the company itself as an Avoid
- adds a candidate evidence-integrity panel showing technical/fundamental freshness and current holds
- modernizes legacy UK/EU Radar coverage descriptions now that EODHD market data is live
- adds regression tests for provider-symbol derivation and evidence freshness

## Adjusted-history maintenance

The daily whole-exchange EODHD bulk path remains authoritative for routine prices. After the longer 252-session bootstrap is complete, a separate single-flight maintenance queue reconciles roughly 520 calendar days per asset from EODHD's single-symbol historical endpoint. EODHD charges one API unit per single-symbol history request regardless of history depth, so a complete 3,000-name weekly pass is approximately 3,000 units against the verified 100,000-unit daily allowance.

The maintenance worker is guarded so it cannot compete with the primary historical bootstrap and automatically recovers stale worker claims.

## Boundaries

No Opportunity model weights are changed. No Swing scoring logic or Runtime Trust Gate threshold is changed. EODHD remains the authoritative managed-universe/EOD provider; FMP remains the fundamental source where its mapped symbol is supported.

## Deployment

Publish application code first, then apply in order:

- `20260805170000_opportunity_radar_evidence_integrity.sql`
- `20260805170500_opportunity_candidate_freshness.sql`
- `20260805171000_preserve_provider_mapping_quarantine.sql`
- `20260805171500_opportunity_adjusted_history_reconciliation.sql`

Application telemetry paths fail soft during a code-before-migration deployment. The adjusted-history worker remains dormant while the main EODHD historical queue has pending/running dates.

author: ekson73
body:
**purpose-tag**: `PR-as-Correction-Prompt`

## Context

`artifact-registry lookup --type <t>` crashed instead of filtering:

```
$ ./bin/artifact-registry lookup --type skill
jq: error (at <stdin>:272): Cannot index boolean with string "type"
```

Root cause (bin/artifact-registry:132): in jq, `|` binds **looser** than `or`, so

```jq
$hastype | not or (.type == $qtype)
```

parses as `$hastype | (not or (.type == $qtype))` — the boolean is piped into the
*entire* disjunction, and `.type` is then evaluated against `true`/`false`.

## Objective

Restore `--type` filtering. This matters beyond cosmetics: `lookup` is the **dedup gate**
that Anima (naming) and Forge (creation) consult before minting a new artifact. A crashing
`--type` filter silently degrades that gate.

## Change

One line — explicit precedence:

```diff
-      | map(select( $hastype | not or (.type == $qtype) ))
+      | map(select( ($hastype | not) or (.type == $qtype) ))
```

## Acceptance / evidence

Verified with a **positive control** against the live 20-entry registry
(13 `skill` / 3 `bin` / 2 `adr` / 1 `script`), proving the filter *discriminates*
rather than merely no longer erroring:

| invocation | expected | actual |
|---|---|---|
| `--purpose "self-referential session-method audit"` | DUP-RISK | ✅ DUP-RISK, 2 matches |
| `… --type skill` | admits (same 2) | ✅ DUP-RISK, same 2 matches |
| `… --type bin` | excludes | ✅ CLEAR, 0 matches |

Pre-fix, the same invocations errored out entirely.

- `gitleaks protect --staged` → **rc=0**, no leaks (exit code captured directly, not through a pipe)

## Risks / rollback

Minimal — single-expression change in one jq filter, no interface or schema change.
Rollback: revert this commit.

## Cross-links

Closes #281

body:
## Summary

> Stacked on #7207. The first two commits are that PR; review this one after it lands, or review only the third commit.

- Replace the `isFastModeActive()` boolean with `AgentSession.fastModeState()` returning `off` / `active` / `blocked`, and paint `blocked` with the error color so fast mode that is on but not working reads as red instead of vanishing
- Add `UsageReport.priorityEntitlement`, parsed from the Claude usage endpoint's `spend.enabled` / `extra_usage.is_enabled`, and skip an activity-lease priority request the account cannot use
- Mark `disabledFeatures` when standard OpenAI Responses echoes a served `service_tier` below the requested `priority`
- Bump the Anthropic usage-report cache key to v4

## Why

A refused priority request looked identical to no request at all: the status-line icon simply disappeared. Three signals now feed one state.

Anthropic gates fast mode on usage credits and answers `429 rate_limit_error … Usage credits are required for fast mode` without them, so the entitlement is knowable before the request. An explicit `/fast on` still attempts it, since the snapshot can be stale, and warns up front.

The OpenAI downgrade marker is scoped to `provider: "openai"`, matching `applyOpenAIResponsesServiceTierCost`. That is the only endpoint whose echo is authoritative; the Codex endpoint answers `service_tier` with a value unrelated to what it served, as `resolveCodexCostServiceTier` already assumes, so reading a downgrade out of it reports every Codex turn as refused.

Live provider evidence outranks the account snapshot in both directions, so a served priority turn clears a blocked model without an explicit re-arm. The cache-key bump is required because the report cache is persistent sqlite shared by every omp process on the machine: without it a build predating `priorityEntitlement` keeps refilling the slot with entitlement-free reports.

## Verification

- `bun test packages/coding-agent/test/fast-mode-scope.test.ts packages/coding-agent/test/status-line-model.test.ts packages/ai/test/claude-priority-entitlement.test.ts packages/ai/test/openai-priority-downgrade.test.ts` (40 pass)
- `bunx tsc --noEmit -p packages/ai/tsconfig.json packages/coding-agent/tsconfig.json`
- Entitlement parsing checked against a live Claude usage response through `claudeUsageProvider.fetchUsage`, which returned `{"available":false,"reason":"usage credits are disabled"}` for an account with extra usage switched off
- Status-line tests assert the blocked icon uses `error` and explicitly not the model color

author: brettluelling
body:
## Summary

`/wrapup`'s session-transcript discovery encoded `~/.claude/projects/` directory names by
replacing only `/`. Claude Code also replaces `.`, so any session running inside a Claude Code
harness worktree never matched its own project directory — and the "newest wins" fallback
silently delegated an unrelated transcript instead.

## Bug

BUG-152: /wrapup session-JSONL discovery silently delegates the wrong transcript in harness worktrees
Severity: high
Primary repo: adlc-toolkit

## Root Cause

Three compounding defects in `wrapup/SKILL.md` Step 4:

1. **Incomplete encoder.** `sed 's|^/||; s|/|-|g'` produced `-…-repo-.claude-worktrees-<slug>`
   where the real directory is `-…-repo--claude-worktrees-<slug>`. The leading `-` is not a
   prefix — it is the path's leading `/` run through the same substitution, so stripping it
   and re-adding one `-` is only accidentally correct for paths whose components contain no `.`.
2. **`ROOT` de-worktree'd the wrong way.** `sed 's|/\.worktrees/.*$||'` strips the `/proceed`
   pattern but not `/.claude/worktrees/` — dead code for the case that matters. The intent was
   also backwards: a harness worktree owns the *only* transcript of the session, so climbing to
   the repo root skips the correct answer.
3. **Phase 2 guessed instead of refusing.** With a REQ id in hand and no candidate matching it,
   every remaining candidate is by definition a transcript of different work. That turned a
   *detected* miss into a silent wrong answer, and the resulting lesson gets committed to
   `.adlc/knowledge/` with nothing marking it suspect.

Observed 2026-08-05 wrapping up BUG-154 in `teton-code`: discovery chose an Aug-1 transcript
with zero mentions of the feature being wrapped up.

## Files Changed (this repo)

- `wrapup/SKILL.md` — correct fork-free encoder; exact-match-then-normalized-scan lookup;
  walk starts at the working tree; Phase-2 refusal; prose + MANDATORY-paragraph correction
- `.adlc/bugs/BUG-152-wrapup-jsonl-worktree-path-encoding.md` — bug report

## Verification

Behaviour matrix on an offline fixture (worktree dir + an older repo-root dir given a
*newer* mtime), in both bash and zsh:

| anchor | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| in worktree transcript | root's stale file | worktree transcript |
| in root transcript | root transcript | root transcript |
| in neither | silent wrong file | **REFUSED** |
| no id | worktree | worktree |

Also: non-git cwd falls back to `$PWD`; the slow path finds a real directory that preserves
`_` where the encoder predicts `-`; and against the live `~/.claude/projects/` listing the
current session's worktree transcript is selected and sorts first.

Two defects were caught by the adversarial pass and fixed before shipping, both introduced by
the first draft of this fix and neither visible by reading:

- **Performance regression** — normalizing every listing entry with a `sed` fork at every
  ancestor level measured **15.2s** with 500 project dirs on a deep path (~4500 forks). The
  exact-match fast path plus parameter-expansion encoding brings it to ~1.9s wall, nearly all
  shell startup.
- **Fast path skipped the loop** — `while IFS= read -r` returns false on an unterminated final
  line, so the newline-less single-entry `$MATCHES` made *every* scenario refuse. Caught only
  by re-running the full matrix after the performance fix.

## Scope

`/wrapup` Step 4 is the only site in the toolkit that encodes a `~/.claude/projects/` path.
`/bugfix` drafts lessons from in-context memory and does no transcript discovery; no partial
does path encoding. Nothing to fix in parallel.

## Test Plan
- [x] `tools/lint-skills/check.py` clean
- [x] 465 Python tests pass
- [x] `sh partials/tests/run.sh` green
- [x] Behaviour matrix verified in bash and zsh
- [ ] CI green on this PR
- [ ] n/a — this repo ships skill source, not a deployed service

author: mo4islona
body:
`--verify-tx-sender`, `--verify-tx-root` and `--verify-withdrawals-root` were parsed into `RpcOptions` and never read. An operator who enabled them got silence instead of verification (GAP-8). Closing that alone would not have made the switches usable, so this also closes the two gaps around it: the per-network exemptions the checks need to avoid false failures (GAP-9), and the path a failure takes (GAP-32).

## What changed

**All six checks are applied per block.** Block hash, transaction root, sender recovery and withdrawals root in `verify_header`; logs bloom, receipts root and the log-index/cumulative-gas coherence checks in `verify_logs`/`verify_receipts`.

**A failed check is incoherence, not a session fault.** It marks the block, so WP-11.2 re-acquires it `P-ENRICH-RETRIES` times and WP-11.3 ends the session naming it, delivering the blocks already acquired below it first. Previously these checks called `bail!`, which the ladder retried forever.

**The head path no longer conflates an incoherent block with an absent one.** `ingest.rs` treated both as "not produced yet" and polled forever in silence, so an enabled `--verify-block-hash` simply hung ingestion. A missing block still polls unbounded — that is ordinary head-following.

**Chain quirks are a registry, not a flag per network.** `NETWORKS` maps a chain id to `{quirks, unencodable_txs}`; each check asks `has(Quirk::StateSyncTx)` rather than testing chain ids, and call sites now read why (`Quirk::NonSequentialLogIndexes`) instead of who (`is_stable`). Adding a network is one row.

## Defects the inert code was hiding

The verification primitives were ported but never called, so two bugs sat in them:

- `decode_hex_big_int` returned an empty vector for odd-length hex. RPC quantities are minimal-length, so an `r` or `s` with a leading zero nibble is ordinary — 22 of 157 transactions in one mainnet block. Signature bytes became zero, breaking both sender recovery and the transaction root.
- `transactions_root` and `receipts_root` swallowed encoder failures with `unwrap_or_default()`, putting an empty leaf in the trie. The resulting root verifies against nothing and reads as a forgery.

Also: Arbitrum's `0x6a` was dispatched to an encoder that did not implement it (now implemented). Tempo's `0x76` has no encoder — such blocks are now **exempt** from the transaction-commitment check rather than reported as forged, recorded under GAP-16.

Separately, on the receipt-by-transaction path the coherence checks judged a copy of the logs taken *before* the Stable renumbering, so the two receipt paths disagreed. Both now judge what will be served.

## Tests

29 new, written before the fix.

| File | Tier | Cases |
|---|---|---|
| `evm-source/tests/verification_corpus.rs` | CT-5 | 17 — every check over recorded blocks from 7 networks: honest accepted, one forged field per switch rejected, the baseline's system-transaction exemptions honored |
| `evm-source/tests/verification_switches.rs` | CT-5 | 7 — the real fetch layer, each switch decides alone (on rejects, off accepts) |
| `harness/tests/ct4_verification.rs` | CT-4 | 5 — bounded re-acquisition then fail-loud, on both the plain and the enriched head path |

Fixtures are the predecessor's own captures (`evm-rpc/test/fixtures`), vendored for 7 networks under `fixtures/verification` (860K). Pre-Byzantium receipts are deliberately excluded — they trip GAP-14.

Workspace: 222 tests green, `cargo clippy --all-targets` clean, `scripts/check-spec.py spec` 0 findings.

## Spec

GAP-8, GAP-9 and GAP-32 retired; INV-36, REQ-14 and REQ-15 go U→P and HC-4 C→P. GAP-11 and GAP-16 widened where this change widened them: a verification failure on the range path now re-requests instead of erroring, and the two missing encoders are recorded there. WP-11.4 gained the rule that a check the build cannot compute leaves the block unverified rather than rejected — scoped to the networks REQ-15 knows emit that type, so an upstream cannot disable a check by choosing its input.

author: davmunrey
body:
`Next` was empty after 1.0.0. Honest — every planned item had shipped — but this file's stated purpose is that *"the ordering is a commitment, the calendar is not"*, and it was committing to nothing.

Four entries. **Two of them exist because writing a roadmap meant checking claims rather than restating them**, and the first of those is the more uncomfortable finding.

## 1.1.0 — Releasing without remembering

Three releases are queued behind this, and each currently needs a human to remember to build, tag, verify the tarball and publish.

The design decision worth reviewing: **npm trusted publishing (OIDC), not a stored `NPM_TOKEN`.** A long-lived publish token would be the highest-value credential this project holds, sitting in repository secrets permanently for something used a few times a year. OIDC needs `id-token: write` on the job and stores nothing — which matches the posture the rest of the repo already takes. Provenance comes free with it.

And it must **refuse to publish a version that does not match the tag**. A tag reading `v1.2.0` against manifests reading `1.1.0` is the one mistake that cannot be corrected after 72 hours.

⚠️ **Needs you once:** `@trazum/core` currently **404s** on the npm registry — the scope does not exist yet, so it has to be created and this repository configured as a trusted publisher. Nothing to paste into secrets, nothing to rotate.

## 1.2.0 — The error band, measured

This is the finding I did not expect.

**`±15%` is printed on every report, appears twice in the README and in the tokenizer's own doc comment — and is asserted nowhere.** `estimateTokens` is tested for exactly three things (`optimize.test.js:190-206`): zero on empty input, monotonic growth, and never returning `NaN`. Every dollar figure Trazum prints descends from a number no test has ever checked.

`security.test.js` opens by saying *"a promise nobody checks is a promise that expires."* This is that promise, and it is holding up the product's central claim.

It is also **one number for all text**, which is unlikely to be true. The only CJK test asserts a Japanese string does not produce `NaN`. If the real error there is 60%, every figure for a Japanese prompt is wrong while the report says ±15%.

⚠️ **Needs you once:** ground truth comes from the official counting API, so the corpus figures have to be generated with a key and committed as fixtures. The corpus and harness do not need one.

## 1.3.0 — Prompts where they actually live

`check` and `diff` read `.txt`, `.md`, `.prompt` and `.tmpl`. Real prompts live in TypeScript template literals, Python strings and YAML — so adopting Trazum today means **refactoring somebody's application first**, as the price of admission.

Zero runtime dependencies rules out an AST parser, which leaves one approach that holds up: an explicit `// trazum:prompt` marker, then the following template literal taken by delimiter matching. **Guessing which string in a file is a prompt would produce false positives in something used as a gate**, and that is not a trade worth making.

The neat part: the masking pass already handles `${x}` correctly, because a template literal's interpolation is exactly the placeholder shape `segment.ts` protects. That half is a special case that already works rather than one to build.

The Action's `diff` against the base branch (deferred from 0.11.0) folds in here rather than earlier — before source extraction it would only diff standalone files, which `trazum diff` already handles by hand.

## 1.4.0 — The front door catches up

The web app optimises and nothing else: no diff view, no budgets, no pricing overlay, no awareness of a config file. Five releases of CLI features never reached it, so anyone arriving through the web sees a 0.1.0 product.

Scheduled rather than parked because the gap costs adoption even though it costs nobody money. **Last** because it changes how the product *looks* rather than whether its numbers are *right* — and that ordering should be visible in the file rather than argued about later.

## Also

`Tokenizer per model family` under `Under consideration` now says it is **pending 1.2.0**, rather than reading as a pure dependency-cost decision. Measuring the band is what decides whether a real tokenizer is needed at all: within 5% on prose and the dependency is not worth taking; 40% out on CJK and it is. Deciding now would be deciding without the number that settles it.

Fixes a doubled `---` left in `ROADMAP.md` by the 1.0.0 edit.

## Verification

No code changes.

- `npm run verify` clean (406 tests) — confirms nothing crept in alongside the document
- `Released` runs 0.1.0 → 1.0.0 unbroken; `Next` contains exactly the four entries in order
- Both cross-references resolve: the tokenizer entry → 1.2.0, and 1.3.0 → the 0.11.0 deferral
- No doubled horizontal rules
- Both owner prerequisites are stated **in the entries themselves**, not only in the PR — a roadmap that hides a blocking dependency in a side channel is the same failure as a config that silently restores a default

---

author: rubenvdlinde
body:
## What

`phpcs-custom-sniffs/CustomSniffs/Sniffs/Functions/NamedParametersSniff.php` declared:

```
 * @license   https://joinup.ec.europa.eu/collection/eupl/eupl-text-eupl-12 EUPL-1.2
```

URL first, SPDX identifier second. Hydra **gate-28 (license-triangle)** extracts the
licence with `awk '{print $3}'` — the *first* token after `@license` — so this shape
resolves to the URL and compares unequal to `composer.json`'s `"EUPL-1.2"`.

Swapped to the fleet shape:

```
 * @license   EUPL-1.2 https://joinup.ec.europa.eu/collection/eupl/eupl-text-eupl-12
```

The licence named is unchanged. This is a field-order fix, not a relicence.

## Honest note on the gate

This repo has **no `lib/` directory**, so gate-28 iterates zero files and emits PASS
without examining anything — its PASS is vacuous and is *not* evidence that this header
was correct. I verified the defect is real with a synthetic control: the identical
URL-first shape placed under `lib/` produces

```
lib/UrlFirst.php file_license=https://joinup.ec.europa.eu/... composer_license=EUPL-1.2 rule=license-triangle-drift
```

and passes once swapped. Fixed here because it is the right declaration regardless of
whether the gate can currently see it.

## Deliberately NOT changed

- `analysis-bootstrap.php` — already `@license EUPL-1.2` (SPDX first). Correct; not churned
  to add the URL.
- `LICENSE:177` — "GNU Affero General Public License (AGPL) v. 3" is an entry in the
  EUPL-1.2's own **Appendix of compatible licences**, not a declaration.
- `ex_app/lib/main.py` — the actual Python application carries no licence header at all.
  Adding one is out of scope for a *normalisation* sweep; flagged for the repo owners.
- All `@copyright` / `SPDX-FileCopyrightText` lines.

## Verification

This repo has **no test suite** — `composer.json` states this explicitly. The nearest
equivalent, run identically before and after under PHP 8.5 in a container (host PHP is
8.2, below this repo's `^8.3`):

| check | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| `php -l` (all PHP) | clean | clean |
| phpcs | clean | clean |
| phpmd | clean | clean |
| psalm | No errors found | No errors found |
| phpstan | OK, no errors | OK, no errors |
| gate-28 | PASS (vacuous) | PASS (vacuous) |

## Purpose
The CSM Portal dashboard's "View more" drill-down page (`shape: "list"` widgets) silently
dropped the current team's filter, returning every team's data instead of the viewer's own.
Resolves one reported CSM Portal dashboard issue (tracked internally).

## Goals
- Stop the "View more" drill-down page from silently widening its query to every team.
- Make the drill-down page's actual query criteria visible to the viewer instead of implicit.

## Approach
- `DashboardWidgetTile.tsx`: the "View more" link now resolves the widget's team-placeholder
  filter before building its URL (`resolveTeamPlaceholder(filters, selectedTeamGroupId)`),
  mirroring the count-shape widget's own click-through link, which already did this correctly.
  Previously the raw, unresolved filter reached the URL, and the destination page — which has
  no team context of its own — fell back to its documented fail-open behavior and dropped the
  filter entirely.
- `widgetPreviewUrl.ts`: new `describeWidgetFilters()` helper flattens a widget's filters
  (both shapes this app uses) into a human-readable list, reusing the existing case-filter-DSL
  handling rather than duplicating it.
- `DashboardWidgetPreviewPage.tsx`: renders the above as a "Filtered by: ..." chip row above
  the results.
- `CsmCaseDetailPage.tsx`: un-hides the case detail SLAs tab (`hidden: true` was reintroduced
  with no recorded rationale three weeks after the tab shipped visible; the underlying data
  path already works and is fetched on page load — only the tab button was unreachable).

## User stories
As a CS engineer, when I drill into a dashboard widget's "View more" I see the same
team-scoped data the tile showed me, plus a clear summary of what's being filtered. Separately,
I can reach the case detail SLAs tab again.

## Release note
Dashboard "View more" pages now keep the current team's filter and show the active filter
criteria. The case detail SLAs tab is visible again.

## Documentation
N/A — internal-tool UI behavior change, no external-facing docs to update.

## Automation tests
- Unit tests: added/updated across the 3 touched dashboard source files (8 new tests: 2 for
  the team-placeholder resolution on the "View more" href, 3 for the filter-criteria display,
  5 for the new `describeWidgetFilters` helper).
- Integration tests: none added; verified manually end-to-end against a real ServiceNow DEV
  backend (local full-stack run), confirming the filter-criteria chips reflect real data
  correctly.

## Security checks
- Followed secure coding standards in http://wso2.com/technical-reports/wso2-secure-engineering-guidelines: yes
- Ran FindSecurityBugs plugin and verified report: N/A (TypeScript/React change; `eslint`/`tsc -b` ran clean)
- Confirmed that this PR doesn't commit any keys, passwords, tokens, usernames, or other secrets: yes

None

## Migrations (if applicable)
N/A — no schema/data change.

## Test environment
Verified locally: Vitest (jsdom), Node/pnpm per repo's `package.json`, Chrome (manual
end-to-end check against a local full-stack run with real ServiceNow DEV data).

## Learning

author: naingthet
body:
## The race

Filename is the identity everything outside the store addresses an output by, but nothing enforced that a conversation held only one output per name. `sync_output_directory` takes one snapshot of the conversation's live outputs and then decides, per scanned file, whether to create or revise. Two scans running at once — routine now that background runs publish into their parent conversation while the foreground turn is still writing — both see no `report.md`, both derive a distinct `OutputId::for_call_artifact(call_id, filename)`, and both create. The conversation ends up with two live outputs answering to one name, and "newest live match" resolution forks between them with nothing to tell the user which document they are looking at.

A test that runs two scans of `report.md` concurrently reproduces this on `main`: two live outputs, one name.

## Mechanism: serialize creation per conversation, first writer keeps the name

`create_output` already begins a transaction and takes the owning chat's write lock — the same lock `append_output_revision` uses to keep ordinals from colliding. Creation is therefore already serialized per conversation; all that was missing was the check. It now runs inside that transaction, after the lock: if a live output in the chat already carries the filename, the creation is refused with `AgentError::OutputFilenameTaken` naming the winner.

Serializing on the existing lock rather than catching a constraint violation and retrying keeps the whole decision in one place and needs no new transaction structure or backoff. The partial unique index on `(chat_id, filename) WHERE deleted_at IS NULL` is still there, as the schema-level statement of the invariant: no future write path can quietly reintroduce the fork, and the check above can read a single row rather than a list. Retracted outputs are excluded from the index because deleting `report.md` must leave the name free for a later one.

The scan handles the refusal by doing what it would have done had its snapshot been current: it re-reads the winning output and appends its bytes as a revision, publishing them under the winner's id. The create and revise paths were factored into one `revise_output` helper so both reach the store the same way. The loser leaves behind one unreferenced file at its own (never-recorded) revision path in conversation scratch — inert, and only on the racing path.

## Restore

Excluding retracted outputs from the index gives restore a new failure mode: undeleting an output whose filename has since been reclaimed would violate the index. `restore_output` now takes the chat write lock and reports the same `OutputFilenameTaken` conflict, so the caller gets an actionable message instead of a raw constraint error.

## Schema

Baseline edit, so `DESKTOP_SCHEMA_EPOCH` moves 5 -> 6 and pre-v1 local databases are rebuilt, per the pre-v1 lifecycle.

## Still open

This is only the half of #1555 that is wanted under either answer to its product question. **Whether cross-producer filename merging is intended** — one document with many producers, versus producers namespacing their outputs — is untouched and still open. A background run writing `report.md` still appends to the user's foreground `report.md`; that is now deterministic rather than forked, but the UI still says nothing about who produced the head revision. Part of #1555.

## Tests

One added: `concurrent_scans_of_one_filename_land_on_a_single_output` runs two barrier-synchronized scans of the same filename from separate workspaces into one conversation and asserts the conversation holds exactly one live `report.md` with two revisions, that both scans addressed it, and that both revisions' bytes are readable where the record says they are. Verified red on the pre-fix code (two live outputs), green after.

One modified: `output_writeback_filename_resolves_to_the_newest_live_output` seeded two live outputs with one filename to prove filename resolution picks the live record. That state is no longer constructible, so it retracts the first output instead and keeps the same assertion.

## Verification

`cargo test -p openwave-core --locked --lib`, `cargo test -p openwave-server --locked --lib`, `cargo check --workspace --locked --all-targets`, `cargo clippy -p openwave-core -p openwave-server --locked --all-targets`, `cargo fmt --check` — all clean. The partial unique index follows the same `and_where` form as the existing ones in the baseline, so it renders for both backends, but I have not exercised it against PostgreSQL locally.

author: ajccarlson
body:
First slice of Phase 2 (OPS-004). `GeneralErrorBoundary` has always called `captureException`, but **nothing ever initialized a client**, so every one of those calls was a no-op and every browser crash went unrecorded.

(The roadmap's audit correction was right that server-side Sentry is initialized — it happens in `instrument.server.mjs`, loaded from `index.js`. Only the browser half was missing.)

## Why not just initialize the Sentry SDK

I measured it before deciding:

| approach | gzip |
|---|---|
| `@sentry/react-router` browser init | **180 KiB** |
| + build-time flags to strip tracing/replay | 180 KiB (saved 2 KiB — the package index re-exports everything regardless) |
| `@sentry/browser` instead | 166 KiB |
| this change | **~0** |

The SDK ships tracing, session replay and user feedback; this app uses none of them. That is a large payload on every visit to answer one question, in a codebase with an open entry for trimming payloads.

**What this gives up is real and I want it on the record:** stack symbolication, breadcrumbs, and release health. If those become worth 180 KiB, the endpoint stays and the SDK goes back in front of it.

## What it does

Crashes post to `/resources/client-errors`, which forwards them through the **server's existing Sentry client** — so browser and server errors still land in one place.

- Throttled to 5 per page and deduplicated, so a render loop that throws every frame says it once
- Only the **path** is sent; a query string carries search terms that are the viewer's business and are not needed to locate a crash
- `credentials: 'omit'`, so no session cookie travels with a report
- `keepalive`, so a report survives the navigation a crash often triggers
- The endpoint bounds and shapes everything it accepts and tags it browser-reported, so it can never be mistaken for something the server observed itself
- Window `error` and `unhandledrejection` listeners catch what React never sees

Also removes a `beforeSendTransaction` filter matching an `x-healthcheck` header nothing has ever sent — the traces sampler already drops those by URL.

## Verification

17 tests. Mutation-tested, 10/10 caught: reporting outside production, removing the flood cap, allowing duplicates, letting the query string travel, reporting empty messages, unbounded message length, installing listeners outside production, accepting full URLs, accepting oversized stacks, and accepting non-POST requests.

All 17 bundle budgets pass, and the build gains no new chunk.

author: fernandobandeira
body:
Four fixes from looking at the ledger in production.

## Project selector on `/task/:taskId`

A task belongs to exactly one project, so offering a selector implied the page could be re-scoped, which it cannot. `/task/:taskId` moves from `global-project-context` to `path-scoped`, and `TaskSessionPage` resolves its project from the task's own `project_id`, falling back to the global store only while the task is still loading.

This also fixes a real bug rather than just removing a control: the session slug came from the *selector*, so a deep link into a task outside the currently selected project could not load its sessions at all.

## The ledger did not fill its pane

`SessionLedger`'s root is a flex column inside a flex row, and without `flex-1` it sized to content — which is why there was dead space to the right and the scrollbar sat mid-screen rather than at the edge. `min-w-0 flex-1` puts the scrollbar and the live footer where they belong.

## The rail was squeezed

`w-52` wrapped each acceptance criterion into three cramped, clipped lines. Widened to `w-72` with looser leading, so criteria read on one or two lines.

## Content measure

The scroll container now fills the pane, but the column inside stays centred and bounded at `max-w-5xl`. Full-bleed text is unreadable on a wide display — the pane fills the screen, the measure does not.

## Verification

- `tsc -b` and `eslint` clean.
- 396 pass / 1 expected-fail across `src/lib`, `App`, and the session components.
- Route-scope tests updated for the new scope, plus one asserting `/task/:taskId` is `path-scoped`.

## What

Adds the version-pinned, adversarially verified architecture for observing and eventually orchestrating Claude Code, OpenAI Codex, and GitHub Copilot CLI from Maximal.

## Core rule

Terminal bytes are presentation. Provider-supported structured channels are semantic evidence. Scraped terminal text never becomes an approval, tool event, diff, usage record, or completion signal.

## Architecture

- persistent Ghostty PTY per harness slot, independently show/hide-able

body:
## Summary

Closes #7.

There was previously no way to edit a config entry after setup at all — not even a working options UI would have helped, since `BridgeScheduler` read `time_pattern` once at construction and nothing ever reloaded the entry after a change.

- **`async_step_reconfigure`** for the data fields (entities, shared discovery prefix, sensor value prefix, bridge name), pre-filled with current values. Renaming the bridge is allowed; colliding with a *different* entry's slug is rejected via an explicit check (excluding the entry being reconfigured itself).
- **`GrapevineOptionsFlow`** for `time_pattern_minutes`, following the current (HA 2025.12+) pattern of not setting `self.config_entry` manually.
- A single `entry.add_update_listener` in `__init__.py` reloads the entry on either kind of change — both reconfigure and the options flow go through `hass.config_entries.async_update_entry`.
- **Depublish on removal (Option C from the issue discussion), both directions:**
  - `ProtocolAdapter.async_depublish_entity(entity_id)` publishes an empty retained payload to both the discovery and state topics. Empty retained payload on a discovery topic is the standard MQTT Discovery removal convention, so blueprint-based receivers clean up for free via their own `mqtt` integration — nothing new needed on their side.
  - `RemoteEntityManager` now tracks which `unique_id` it last associated with each topic, and removes the native entity (+ purges its entity_registry entry) when an empty payload arrives on that topic — correlated by topic, since an empty payload carries no `unique_id` to key off.
  - Reused for `async_remove_entry` (new): depublishes every bridged entity when the whole integration is removed, closing a related gap flagged earlier in the same issue thread (orphaned entities on other instances after uninstall).
- `PROTOCOL.md` gets a new §5b documenting the removal-signal convention.

## Summary

- make first TOTP enrollment atomic with Redis `SET NX`
- deny disclosure of an already-enrolled TOTP secret and fail closed on Redis outages
- add rotating refresh-session families with `jti`, successor CAS, replay detection, and family revocation
- reject legacy refresh tokens without session identity
- ensure initial refresh-family creation completes before access/refresh cookies are built
- add regression coverage for concurrency, replay, outages, stale/revoked sessions, cookie ordering, and absence of password-only TOTP recovery

## Why

The previous TOTP setup path could return an existing enrolled secret to a pending principal. Refresh tokens were also reusable without server-side one-time consumption, so predecessor replay and concurrent refresh could not be deterministically contained.

## Impact

Administrators must sign in again if they still hold a legacy refresh token. Existing TOTP secrets are never returned by enrollment; lost-device recovery or rotation is intentionally denied until a separate authority and policy are approved. Redis failures return `503` without issuing authentication cookies.

author: atomantic
body:
## Summary

Wires a real installer/runner behind the `LOCAL_CUDA` execution lane the image-to-3D target registry already declared, and replaces the hardcoded `caps.cuda = false` with an actual NVIDIA capability probe.

**CUDA detection** (`server/lib/cudaCapability.js`) — the one place that shells to `nvidia-smi`. It reports a three-way `status` (`available` / `absent` / `unknown`) so "the probe could not run" never collapses into "there is no GPU"; there is deliberately no boolean field a caller could misread. Memoized, with an `unknown` verdict held only briefly, so a host whose driver is mid-update costs one stalled spawn a minute instead of one per request (`nvidia-smi` can hang to its timeout). `pythonSetup.js#hasNvidiaGpu` now delegates here rather than running its own `nvidia-smi`, so the FLUX.2 installer and the 3D page can no longer disagree about the hardware.

**The CUDA lane** (`trellis2Cuda.js` + `trellis2CudaGenerateRunner.py`) — installs upstream `microsoft/TRELLIS.2` (recursive clone; `setup.sh` *sourced* in a login shell, since it calls `conda activate`, with upstream's documented extension flags). Upstream ships no CLI — only a hard-coded `example.py` — so PortOS provides its own entrypoint over the documented public API (`from_pretrained` → `run(image)` → `o_voxel.postprocess.to_glb` → `export`). It prints the Apple-Silicon lane's stage banners, so one progress parser serves both lanes. The export budget (atlas size + decimation target) scales with the card: upstream's H100-tuned settings would OOM the 24 GB floor this lane supports.

**Registry** (`targets.js`) — a `trellis2Cuda` descriptor on upstream's stated floor (24 GB VRAM, CUDA 12.4, Linux-only), a `LOCAL_CUDA` gate, and `UNFIXABLE_HARDWARE_REASONS` so a target blocked by hardware the host simply lacks is omitted rather than shown permanently red. That is applied symmetrically — a Mac no longer sees a dead CUDA card, and an NVIDIA box no longer sees a dead Apple-Silicon one. A Windows host *with* a qualifying card still sees the target, reporting `requires-linux-host`, because WSL2 is a blocker the user can act on.

`detectHostCapabilities()` became async (sizing a card requires a subprocess) and its result is now threaded down to the runner, so the render reads the same capabilities the readiness gate used.

**Shared machinery** (`laneRunner.js`) — the install step-runner (transient-network retry, optional steps, cancel) and the generate child-driver were extracted so the MPS and CUDA lanes share one implementation instead of ~200 duplicated lines. This also gives the CUDA lane the `optional`-step degradation it would otherwise have lacked.

The Apple-Silicon lane remains the default; an existing Mac install behaves exactly as before.

## Test plan

- `server/lib/cudaCapability.test.js` (new) — pure CSV parsing against real driver output, all three probe outcomes, the `[N/A]` VRAM edge (kept as a sized-`null` GPU, not dropped and not `0`), memoization incl. concurrent callers, and the bounded `unknown` retry.
- `server/services/imageTo3d/trellis2Cuda.test.js` (new) — conda-env resolution, install-step construction (recursive clone, sourced setup, resume-skips-clone), export-budget selection, arg building, install retry/cancel/incomplete-verify, and the render guard, HF-auth + CUDA-OOM classification, progress streaming, and kill. All via injected `exists`/`spawnImpl` — no GPU, no 15 GB download, no live render.
- `server/services/imageTo3d/targets.test.js` — extended for the CUDA gate (reason ordering, VRAM floor, probe-failed vs no-GPU) and the symmetric hiding.
- Full server suite run and diffed against `main`: the only failures are this repo's pre-existing Windows-host ones (posix path literals in `trellis2`/`models`/`pythonSetup`/`spawnCwd` assertions, and a `python3`-not-on-PATH runner test), all present identically on `main`. Client `Media3D` suites pass.
- Detection validated end to end on real hardware (RTX 3090, 24 GB, driver 596.36): reports `cuda: true, cudaVramGb: 24`, correctly gates to `requires-linux-host` on Windows, and resolves to available when the host is Linux/WSL2.

Note: the CUDA install + render path itself is exercised through injected subprocesses, matching how the Apple-Silicon lane is tested; end-to-end validation needs a Linux + NVIDIA host.

author: ironship
body:
## Problem
The UI test suite (`Tests / test` workflow) fails randomly: **a different test on every run**, 1–5 failures per run, all green in isolation and green on re-run of the same binary. Victims so far: `SyntaxTextEditorTests` (4 different tests), `MainMenuKeyboardActivationTests`, `TextBoxTagTogglerTests`, `SyntaxHighlightingTextPresenterCanaryTests`, `SplitManagerTests` (5 in one run), `HistoryButton_MouseClick_OpensFlyoutWithItems`.

Root cause — two failure modes, both depend on xUnit's default **parallel test-class execution**:
1. **Shared static state**: the headless UI tests share the global `Se.Settings` instance; many test classes mutate it (e.g. `SubtitleLineMaximumLength`, `MinimumBetweenLines`) without restoring. A class running in parallel with another can change a setting the other is reading → wrong behavior → assertion failure. Proven: in one audit run, a probe test leaked settings and 5 `SplitManagerTests` failed; those tests pass 28/28 in isolation.
2. **CPU contention on timing-sensitive tests**: keyboard/input-simulation tests (SyntaxTextEditor, menu-keyboard activation) assert timing-sensitive behavior and starve on the 2-core CI runner while other classes run concurrently.

## Fix
`tests/UI/AssemblyInfo.cs` — `[assembly: CollectionBehavior(DisableTestParallelization = true)]` for the UI test assembly. Test classes now run one at a time, which removes the concurrency both failure modes depend on. Pure-logic assemblies (libse tests) are untouched and stay parallel.

Measured locally on this machine: **no runtime cost** — full suite 27–32 s both ways (1442/1442, 3 consecutive green runs with the fix; the suite is CPU-bound, not throughput-bound).

## Verification
- [x] `dotnet build src/ui/UI.csproj` — EXIT:0, 0 errors
- [x] `dotnet test tests/UI/UITests.csproj` with the fix: **3 consecutive runs, 1442/1442 green each** (27–32 s)
- [x] Control: suite green on the same machine without the fix (flakes reproduced in CI on 4 PRs today — evidence in comments on #13251/#13262/#13264/#13266)
- [x] SplitManagerTests 28/28 in isolation (the flake-victim class from the audit incident)

## Notes

author: zachway
body:
## Problem

On the Holdings-by-archive-and-instrument treemap, each instrument leaf's box area is `log10(n+1)` so small instruments stay visible. The archive (parent) node had value `0`, relying on Plotly's default `branchvalues: 'remainder'` mode to size it as the sum of its children's values.

That's wrong: `log10(a+1) + log10(b+1) != log10(a+b+1)`. Summing logs across children means an archive's box size tracked how many instruments it had almost as much as how many holdings it had. An archive with 10 small instruments could visually dwarf an archive with one enormous instrument, even with far fewer total holdings.

## Fix

- Archive nodes now get an explicit value of `log10(archive_total+1)`, computed from the real per-archive total (already tracked in `archive_totals`).
- The trace now sets `branchvalues: 'total'`. In this mode each node's own value is authoritative for how it compares to its siblings, while its children are apportioned inside it by their own relative values (rescaled to fit) — so archive sizing reflects real totals, and instrument leaves within an archive still show up individually instead of collapsing to invisible slivers.

## Test plan

- [x] `python3 -m py_compile webapp/app.py`
- [x] `pytest tests/` — 18 passed
- [x] Ran the app against a synthetic DuckDB/Parquet fixture and inspected the emitted `values`/`customdata` arrays directly: e.g. CARMENES (200,000 + 180,000 = 380,000 holdings across 2 instruments) now emits archive value `5.5798` = `log10(380001)`, matching its true total, instead of the old `10.556` (sum of the two children's logs).
- [ ] No browser/Node available in this sandbox, so the actual rendered treemap wasn't visually checked — the values feeding Plotly were verified numerically instead.

## Summary
Kept lines now get their phrasing judged after they earn the keep: load-bearing specifics stay verbatim, driftable inventories drop, and the result records as a new **rewrite** verdict.

## Why
A line can pin a real boundary and still carry specifics that drift (a class inventory, an enumerated list). Cutting it loses the rule and keeping it as-is preserves the rot, so the audit needed a verdict between the two.

The "precise but generic" summary of this standard's intention was coined by @jltanicuchi (https://github.com/jltanicuchi).

The wording was hardened through a multi-model panel (Sonnet low, Opus low, Codex) and verified with blind known-answer probes at low effort: the final text scores 15/15, including the trap case where a pure inventory must downgrade to cut instead of being rescued as a rewrite.

## Solution
A "Precise but generic" section after the audit steps defines the load-bearing test, constrains rewrites (never widen scope, weaken the boundary, or add advice), and disambiguates the two senses of "generic" against step 2's cut of generic best practices.

author: david-engelmann
body:
## Cluster 156.0.1 — production-safety defaults (arc 1, part 1)

First of the post-v155 **enterprise-hardening** arc: two safe-by-default fixes
from the production-readiness research.

### SIGTERM graceful shutdown
`main.rs` waited only on `ctrl_c()` (SIGINT). Kubernetes and systemd send
**SIGTERM** on rollout/stop, so pods were killed mid-request instead of draining
through `with_graceful_shutdown` (which then runs the existing worker
`shutdown()` sequence). Now selects on SIGINT **and** SIGTERM (unix); falls back
to SIGINT-only if the handler can't be installed; non-unix unchanged.

### Default `statement_timeout`
`MAIDAN_DB_STATEMENT_TIMEOUT_MS` defaulted to `0` (disabled) — a runaway query
could pin a pooled connection indefinitely (a noisy-neighbor / DoS vector).
Default is now **`30000` (30 s)**. Boot migrations already reset it to `0` under
the advisory lock (unaffected); the operator reindex path and the
`maidan reindex-embeddings` CLI are documented escape hatches; set `0` to
restore the uncapped behavior.

### Tests / docs
- `db_config_defaults_are_safe` (30 s default), `db_config_statement_timeout_can_be_disabled` (`0` restores uncapped), override test uses a distinct value.
- `docs/Production.md` updated to the new default + caveat.
- SIGTERM handling isn't unit-tested (signal wiring in `main`, matching the codebase norm); it compiles and reuses the tested graceful-shutdown drain.

### PR-level retro
- **Safe by construction:** migrations are exempt from the timeout; the smoke
  jobs do sub-second queries, well under 30 s.
- **Deferred to later arc-1 clusters:** auth fail-closed (coordinated
  manifest/CI-env change) and default-on rate limits / body cap (per-route care)
  — each its own cluster to keep the required smoke jobs green.

author: yukon-autoresearch[bot]
body:
Yukon submission `e5c524e0-b306-4dbd-a3e1-7427cd34d94b` against https://github.com/Layr-Labs/lighter-prover-challenge at `46cfe262ee0dbe43b40f36f6d941df1586aaeba5`.

Current best score: 3.36381608915175. This PR's own benchmark run scores the head commit;
the PR is merged automatically if the submission is accepted, and closed with the result otherwise.

---

**Submitter note**

Model: GPT 5.6 Sol

# Reuse lookup inversion inputs and eliminate per-row combo allocations

## Context and objective

This submission starts from the promoted frontier commit `46cfe262ee0dbe43b40f36f6d941df1586aaeba5`, submission `a973141`. That frontier already removes redundant deep polynomial-buffer clones in the general prover path and disables redundant eager intermediate proof verification in release builds. This candidate keeps both improvements and targets a different hot path: lookup polynomial construction inside Plonky2.

Agent: Codex desktop.

The benchmark is scored on private active-witness fixtures. The checked-in public fixture is synthetic, provisional, cacheable, and known to differ materially from a clean ranked host. I therefore used the local benchmark as a proof-compatibility gate and gross-regression check, not as a precise predictor of the official throughput delta. The optimization was selected from the structure of the active lookup loop: it removes repeated heap allocation and memory traffic without changing proof arithmetic, transcript order, circuit definitions, verifier data, or serialization.

At the start of this work, `yukon submissions --all` reported `a973141` as the promoted frontier with an official score of `3.36381608915175`. Two CPU-scheduling submissions were still validating. This candidate deliberately does not reproduce their heavy/light proving concurrency or transaction/chain pipeline. It is an independent backend improvement that can be layered with scheduling changes if either direction is promoted later.

## Hot-path analysis

`compute_lookup_polys` in `vendor/plonky2/plonky2/src/plonk/prover.rs` constructs the RE, partial Sum, and partial LDC polynomials for every lookup challenge. It walks every lookup-table row and every lookup-use row. Before this patch, each lookup-table row allocated and populated four short-lived vectors:

1. the `(input + a * output)` combinations used for the Sum denominator;
2. the corresponding `(alpha - combination)` batch-inversion inputs;
3. the returned batch inverses;
4. a second `(input + b * output)` combination vector used to update RE.

Each lookup-use row similarly allocated three vectors:

1. `(input + a * output)` combinations;
2. `(alpha - combination)` inversion inputs;
3. returned batch inverses.

The function also cloned the complete `lookup_rows` descriptor vector before walking it, even though the loop only reads three `usize` boundaries from each descriptor.

These allocations are individually small, but they occur inside a nested row-by-challenge proof loop. Active witnesses exercise the lookup machinery more meaningfully than the all-empty public fixture. The repeated allocate/fill/scan/drop sequence creates allocator metadata work and memory traffic on every proof, including transaction and recursive proofs that contain lookup gates.

## Implementation

The patch changes one editable file: `vendor/plonky2/plonky2/src/plonk/prover.rs`.

### Reusable inversion input buffer

`compute_lookup_polys` now allocates one `inverse_inputs` vector with capacity equal to the larger of the lookup-use and lookup-table slot counts. Each row clears and refills the vector without releasing its allocation. Because `clear()` retains capacity and both slot counts are fixed by the common circuit configuration, the buffer does not need to grow during the row loops.

For lookup-table rows, the buffer is filled directly with:

```text
alpha - (looked_input + a * looked_output)
```

For lookup-use rows, it is filled directly with:

```text
alpha - (looking_input + a * looking_output)
```

The existing field implementation still returns the vector of multiplicative inverses. That output remains necessary to index partial Sum/LDC slot ranges. The change removes all other per-row combo-vector allocations while leaving the batch inversion itself untouched.

### Direct RE fold

The previous code materialized every `(looked_input + b * looked_output)` value into `lookup_combos`, then immediately traversed that vector once to update RE. The patch performs the same ordered recurrence directly from the witness:

```text
re = re * delta + looked_input + b * looked_output
```

The fold iterates `0..num_lut_slots` in the same order as the old vector construction and subsequent loop. Addition and multiplication grouping is preserved: the old loop computed `re * delta + combo`, where `combo` was `input + b * output`; the new fold computes the identical field expression. No challenge is sampled or consumed here, so the transcript is unaffected.

### Borrow lookup descriptors

The outer loop now borrows `&prover_data.lookup_rows` and copies its three numeric row boundaries into local variables. It no longer clones the descriptor vector. The lookup descriptors and prover data remain immutable for the entire computation.

## Allocation change

The steady-state row-loop allocation count changes as follows:

| Row kind | Before | After | Removed |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Lookup-table row | 4 vectors | 1 vector | 3 vectors per row |
| Lookup-use row | 3 vectors | 1 vector | 2 vectors per row |

The remaining vector is the batch-inverse result required by the downstream indexed slot folds. The reusable input allocation is paid once per challenge invocation rather than once per row. The complete `lookup_rows` clone is also removed once per invocation.

This is intentionally narrower than changing the general `Field::batch_multiplicative_inverse` API or implementing an in-place inverse routine. A field-wide API change could remove the remaining result allocation, but it would expand the correctness and review surface substantially. This submission captures most of the row-allocation reduction while preserving the existing, tested inversion implementation.

## Correctness argument

The patch does not change any of the following:

- circuit gates, constraints, degree, lookup slot counts, or public inputs;
- witness values or lookup multiplicities;
- Fiat-Shamir challenge generation or challenge ordering;
- the `alpha`, `a`, `b`, or `delta` field expressions;
- row traversal order or partial-polynomial slot ranges;
- batch inversion inputs or returned inverse indexing;
- polynomial commitment ordering;
- proof structure, verifier data, or proof serialization.

For Sum and LDC, the old intermediate `combo` vector was used only to derive `alpha - combo`. Constructing that value directly is field-identical. For RE, the old `lookup_combos` vector was consumed once in insertion order; folding the same witness-derived values in the same order is identical. Reusing a vector after `clear()` cannot retain logical elements because its length becomes zero before `extend`, while its capacity is intentionally retained.

The no-lookup path is unchanged: `compute_all_lookup_polys` still returns an empty vector when lookup support is disabled. Multiple lookup tables are unchanged because the reusable buffer is cleared at the start of every row, and row boundaries continue to come from each borrowed `LookupWire` descriptor.

## Validation

The candidate was validated through the repository's submission build and focused bench tests:

```sh
cargo fmt --manifest-path vendor/plonky2/Cargo.toml --all
git diff --check
yukon setup
cargo test --release --locked -p bench --bin prove
yukon run
```

`yukon setup` verified the pinned trusted verifier and completed the optimized release build. The focused bench binary test suite reported four passing tests and no failures, covering the fixed production mixed-circuit parameters, final proof shape, li

author: mattfidler
body:
## Problem

`_rxode2_codegen` emits C from the parser's **global** `.rxModelVarsLast`, not from the model variables passed to `rxCompile()`. The guard before it only asked whether *some* model was loaded:

```r
if (.Call(`_rxode2_codeLoaded`) == 0L) .rxModelVarsCharacter(setNames(.mv$model, NULL))
```

So whenever a *different* model happens to be the parsed one, the C written out is that other model's, while the artifact keeps this model's md5-derived name — and the `modVars` read back from the DLL describe the wrong model entirely.

`rxode2()` never hits this: it parses, then compiles immediately. A **re-compile** does. An existing model object whose `.so` is gone reaches `rxCompile()` via `rxDynLoad()` → `$compile()` long after some other model was parsed — which is exactly what happens to a saved fit restored in a new session, since its DLL lived in the original session's `tempdir()`.

Measured on a restored SAEM fit (nlmixr2's `broom` article, which loads a cached fit):

```
requested mv params:  tcl, tv
.rxModelVarsLast:     tcl, eta.cl, tv, eta.v     <- what got compiled
```

and every solve after that failed with

```
The following parameter(s) are required for solving: eta.v, eta.cl
```

## Fix

Re-parse unless the loaded model is provably this one (`parsed_md5` comparison). Only the model *syntax* (`normModel`) is parsed — the sibling `indLin` slot holds generated matrix-exponential C and is restored from `.indLinInfo`/`.rxMECode` a few lines below anyway.

In the ordinary `rxode2()` path the md5s match, so nothing re-parses and behavior is unchanged.

## Tests

New `tests/testthat/test-recompile-model.R`, covering both the direct `rxCompile()` call and the `rxLoad()`-after-the-`.so`-is-gone path. Verified the tests fail against the old guard (emulated by neutering the re-parse) — model A came back reporting model B's parameters — and pass with the fix.

Downstream check: nlmixr2's `broom` article, which failed to build on `setOfv(fit.s, "gauss3_1.6")`, now renders, and the full nlmixr2 article precompute (10 cached articles) renders with 0 failures.
