author: gautamgb
body:
Adds `mcpindex` as a remote MCP server entry.

mcpindex indexes MCP servers and exposes them to agents as tools: find a server by
natural-language task, search and compare candidates, get the install command, and run
advisory trust checks against a server's declared tool contracts.

**Entry details**

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Type | `remote` (hosted, no Dockerfile) |
| Transport | `streamable-http` |
| URL | `https://mcpindex.ai/api/mcp` |
| Auth | None. The endpoint is public, so there is no `oauth` block. |
| Category | `ai` |
| License | MIT ([`mcp-server-mcpindex`](https://github.com/mcpindex-ai/mcp-server-mcpindex)) |
| Docs | https://mcpindex.ai/docs |

**Tools** (6, discovered dynamically)

- `recommend_mcp_for_task` — ranked server recommendations for a natural-language task
- `search_mcp_servers` — keyword and semantic search across the index
- `get_install_command` — install command for a given server
- `compare_servers` — side-by-side comparison
- `check_tool_trust` — advisory trust check on a tool contract
- `assess_server` — advisory trust assessment for a server

`dynamic.tools: true` is set because the server advertises
`capabilities.tools.listChanged: true`, so the tool list is discovered at runtime rather
than pinned in `tools.json`.

**On the advisory framing:** `check_tool_trust` and `assess_server` return advisory signals
about whether a server's tool contracts have changed since they were last observed. They
are not a certification and do not assert that a server is safe.

**Validation**

`go run ./cmd/validate --name mcpindex` passes all checks locally:

```
✅ Name is valid
✅ Directory is valid
✅ Title is valid
✅ YAML formatting is valid
✅ Commit pin not required (non-local server)
✅ Secrets are valid
✅ Config env is valid
✅ License validation skipped (remote server)
✅ Icon is valid
✅ Dynamic tools are valid
✅ Remote is valid
✅ OAuth dynamic configuration is valid
```

The endpoint was also exercised directly: `initialize` and `tools/list` both respond over
`streamable-http` and return the 6 tools listed above.

author: maw-agents
body:
Michael, holding the `pm` code: *"says nav hidden so i never expect to see the exhaustive list of course info docs in the nav."* He was right, and `nav: hidden` was not the thing that was broken.

## The bug

`courses/index.md` on uritp declares `router: pm`. `courses/course-info/index.md` declares `nav: hidden`. The router seal was **pass 3 of `prune_nav` at stage 00b**, so it harvested the whole courses subtree into the sealed manifest *before* navstate ran at 00bb. By the time `nav: hidden` was read, its folder was already out of the tree and the cut had nothing to act on — and all 43 course pages sat in the AES payload, ready to be injected back into the sidebar the moment a correct code was typed.

Verified in the built HTML on `gh-pages`, not inferred: an empty Courses `<ul>` beside a ~6KB `data-subtree` blob, buildstamp 13:36 ET.

⚑ **Sixth instance of one shape in this engine** — a rule correct in isolation and unreachable in place — and **the ordering comment caused this one.** navstate must run after the prune because it reads index pages the prune can delete. True, and exactly what let the seal reach the subtree first. Same shape as `_mark_indexes` one file over: a rule defended in one direction is not a rule that was thought about in both.

## The fix is the ORDER, not a second check

`_collect` is **not** taught about `nav:` and its docstring says it must never learn. It walks a tree navstate already trimmed, so a hidden folder contributes its own row and nothing under it, for free — no second copy of the rule that can drift from the first.

```
00    sort     instance.py orders the tree
00b   prune    unlisted pages leave            <- prune_nav
00bb  shape    `nav: hidden` folders are cut   <- navstate.shape
00bc  seal     routers take what is LEFT       <- NEW
00c   chain    prev/next rebuilt from all of it
```

## And the regression is detectable now, which is the half that outlives this PR

`state.NAV_SHAPED` is raised by `navstate.shape` and checked by `seal_nav`. Unregister, rename or renumber 00bb and the seal goes straight back to harvesting untrimmed subtrees — **silently**, invisible until somebody types a code and sees pages a folder had shut. That is why the bug lived five hours: nothing could notice it. Belt and braces on purpose, because a `hooks:` list is one edit away from being wrong forever.

The flag is set at the top of `shape()`, unconditionally. It means *the stage ran*, never *the stage changed something* — a site with no `nav:` anywhere still shapes its tree, and a detector that cries on healthy sites is a detector nobody reads.

## Decided, not guessed: hidden beats a seal

A routed folder whose own index says `nav: hidden` now seals **nothing** and says so in the report. Not a conflict needing a tie-break: *never offered* is a stronger claim than *offered to whoever has the code*, and the stronger one wins by arriving first. But "router declared, no manifest" is a silent surprise otherwise.

That seam was **undocumented in both directions** before today — §3 described `nav:`, §7 described the seal, and nothing said what happens when both land on one branch, which is the live uritp case. README §3 now has it.

## 🔴 My own defect, recorded rather than amended

The first commit here claimed *"20,266 → under it, against a 22,528 B hard limit"* and **shipped 23,495 B — over the hard limit**, in a commit whose body asserted the opposite, one file over from #85 correcting this exact error four hours earlier. I read that entry this session and repeated it.

The generalisable part is not "measure." I trimmed two docstrings, felt the file get smaller, and **reported a direction as a magnitude.** Fixed in the next commit; `visibility.py` now sits at **20,738 B**, measured off the write, ~1.8KB inside the ceiling. ⚠️ That is still past the 18,432 B warn line, as it was before I touched it — flagged rather than chased, because a third rewrite of this file today buys a warning threshold and risks the settled decisions in it.

## Files

`docrender/visibility.py` (split), `docrender/state.py` (+`NAV_SHAPED`), `docrender/navstate.py` (one line — full-file write disclosed per #85), `hooks/00bc_seal.py` (new), `hooks/00b_unlisted.py` (its docstring described a 3-link chain that now has 5), `mkdocs.yml` (**the edit that turns it on**), `hooks/README.md`, `README.md`.

🚩 **Separate, still open:** `navigation.prune` is absent from the built uritp site, so something there resolved to `expanded` while root and `courses/` both say `collapsed`. Not touched here.

## Context

`CLIRunner.Run` re-defaulted `Bin`, `Model`, and `Timeout` before launching the synthesis subprocess. `NewClaudeRunner` and `NewCodexRunner` already set all three, and `NewRunner` was their only caller, so those branches could never fire. They read as configuration but nothing reaches them, and with no tests in the package nothing verified them either.

## Changes

- Inline both constructors into `NewRunner`, which now sets `Bin`, `Model`, and `Timeout` in one place.
- Read those fields straight off the struct in `Run`; drop the `if bin == ""`, `if model == ""`, and `if timeout <= 0` branches.
- Delete `defaultModel` and the duplicated `"gpt-5.6-luna"` literal, which only the dead branches used. The real defaults live in `settings.BackendOptions`.

No behavior change: every reachable path already carried the values the fallbacks would have supplied.

The `default:` case in `Run`'s backend switch stays. It is unreachable the same way, but removing it would leave `args` and `parse` nil on a zero-value struct rather than returning an error.

- `make -C collector test` — passed

body:
## What

All app metadata (`composer.json`, `package.json`, `appinfo/info.xml`, `LICENSE`) already declares **EUPL-1.2**, but 71 source files still carried `AGPL-3.0-or-later` declarations left over from the original Nextcloud app scaffolding. This aligns them with the project licence.

| Category | Count |
|---|---|
| `@license AGPL-3.0-or-later` → `@license EUPL-1.2` (`src/**`, `.vue`/`.js`/`.ts`) | 47 |

| **Total** | **71** |

No trailing-dot (`EUPL-1.2.`) or field-order (`@license <url> EUPL-1.2`) defects existed in this repo — all four metadata files were already correct and were not touched.

- No third-party or vendored file. `vendor/`, `node_modules/`, `dist/`, `build/` are excluded, and this repo has no vendored upstream source carrying a foreign copyright holder.

- `src/modals/menuItem/menuItemIconCatalogues.js` **was** changed. Its prose mentions a CC0 OpenGemeenten icon sample and a CC BY-NC-ND npm package — those statements describe the *icon data*, not this file, and are left verbatim. The file itself is ours.

## Diff shape

71 files changed, 71 insertions(+), 71 deletions(-) — exactly one line per file, and **every changed line contains `license`**. Nothing else in any file moves.

Identically conditioned before and after:

| Check | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| vitest (`npm run test:unit`) | 6 files / 56 tests passed | 6 files / 56 tests passed |

author: kevinushey
body:
Two additions to the protection-stack diagnostics, both aimed at the
failure mode where an `UNPROTECT` with too large a count releases a
value belonging to the caller.

## 1. A protection floor (`--enable-strict-barrier` only)

`unprotect()` only detects underflow past zero
(`R_signal_unprotect_error`). A function that does `UNPROTECT(3)` having
protected 2 pops one of its *caller's* entries and keeps going. Today
that is noticed only indirectly and after the fact:

- `check_stack_balance` may report `stack imbalance` when control
  reaches the enclosing primitive, but only if the miscount survives
  that far -- a later compensating `PROTECT` in the same primitive hides
  it completely, while the caller's value has still been left
  unprotected in between;
- otherwise nothing reports it until the value is collected and used,
  which needs `gctorture` and some luck to catch.

This adds `R_PPStackFloor`, the lowest stack entry the code currently
running may release. Calls into code expected to manage its own
protections raise the floor to the current top:

- a primitive's C function, via the new `R_callPrimFun` in `eval.c`;
- a native routine reached through `.Call`/`.External`, in
  `R_doDotCall`.

`unprotect()` and `unprotect_ptr()` then signal an error at the
offending call:

```
unprotect(2): only 1 protected item belongs to this call
```

The floor is saved and restored by `begincontext`/`R_restore_globals`
alongside `cstacktop`, so non-local exits behave. This mirrors
`R_BCProtTop` and `CHECK_SET_BELOW_PROT`, which already do exactly this
for the byte code node stack.

The global, the `RCNTXT` field and the checks are all under
`TESTING_WRITE_BARRIER`; a default build is unchanged.

## 2. Stack balance checking in the byte code interpreter

`check_stack_balance` has been called around the AST interpreter's
primitive dispatch for a long time, but its five call sites are all in
`eval` (`SPECIALSXP`/`BUILTINSXP`), `applyMethod` and `do_internal`.
The byte code interpreter's own dispatch sites -- `OP(CALL)`,
`OP(CALLBUILTIN)`, `OP(CALLSPECIAL)`, `OP(SETTER_CALL)`,
`OP(GETTER_CALL)` -- never checked, and with the JIT on by default most
primitive calls now take the unchecked path. `R_forceAndCall` had no
check either.

Routing all of them through `R_callPrimFun` gives compiled code the same
coverage. The cost is one integer save and one comparison per primitive
call. This is left unconditional to match the AST interpreter; happy to
put it behind `TESTING_WRITE_BARRIER` instead if that is preferred.

## Testing

Built and tested on aarch64-apple-darwin, with and without
`--enable-strict-barrier`.

- Default build: `test-Reg` passes in full, with **no** new
  `stack imbalance` reports anywhere in the regression suite or in the
  byte-compilation of the base packages -- i.e. the newly-checked byte
  code paths are clean today.
- Strict barrier build: `test-Specific` passes, and `test-Reg` output is
  byte-identical to an unmodified strict-barrier build of the same
  commit. Both hit the same pre-existing failure in `reg-tests-1d.R`
  (`row.names(trees) <- 42 + seq_len(nrow(trees))` trips the existing
  `inserting non-tracking CDR in tracking cell` assertion in `SETCDR`);
  that reproduces without this patch and looks like a separate issue.
- A native routine that unprotects one too many is reported at the
  offending `UNPROTECT` rather than at the `.Call` boundary:

  ```
  # before: Warning: stack imbalance in '.Call', 18 then 17   (execution continues)
  # after:  Error: unprotect(2): only 1 protected item belongs to this call
  ```

  A routine that leaks a protection is still reported by the balance
  check on `.Call`, and a correct routine is silent.

## Notes

- The mechanical part of the diff is
  `PRIMFUN(f) (call, f, args, rho)` -> `R_callPrimFun(f, call, args, rho)`.
- The existing outer `check_stack_balance` calls in the AST paths are
  left alone: their `save` spans `evalList` too, which is coverage the
  inner check does not give.
- The floor is only raised at primitive and `.Call`/`.External`
  boundaries. Raising it per closure application would catch more but
  costs more; that seemed a separate question.
- Documented in R-exts, "Checking memory access".

Before requesting review, please confirm you have run the appropriate checks:

## Skipped checks

If you skipped any checks, please list them below and explain why:
- 

## Description

The generated font tables include codepoints that are not present in the source fonts. FreeType renders many of these codepoints as the same `.notdef` glyph, but the generators previously stored a separate copy of that bitmap for every glyph.

Those duplicate rasters account for a significant portion of the firmware image.

## Changes

- Add a shared `BitmapPool` that stores each distinct packed glyph bitmap once.
- Key pooled entries by packed bytes, width, and height so bitmaps with different row boundaries cannot be incorrectly shared.
- Update all five font generators to emit metrics that reference the pooled bitmap data.
- Keep `BitmapPool` in a dependency-free module so its behavior can be tested without installing Pillow.
- Regenerate the checked-in Literata and Merriweather tables.
- Add regression tests covering:
  - reuse of identical bitmaps
  - separation of identical packed bytes with different dimensions

Only bitmap storage offsets change. Glyph length, dimensions, placement, and advance metrics remain unchanged.

## Size impact

| Generated tables | Before | After | Reduction |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| **Total bitmap data** | **2,014,522 bytes** | **1,214,582 bytes** | **799,940 bytes (39.71%)** |

The generated tables are shared across boards, so both X3 and X4 firmware receive the same reduction in embedded font data.

The table-data delta is reported directly because the final firmware binary size can vary slightly with linker layout.

## Correctness

- All 49,802 glyphs retain the same length, width, height, placement, and advance values.
- Glyph fingerprints remain unchanged.
- Golden frames remain byte-identical.
- Repeated and non-monotonic bitmap offsets remain valid because runtime lookup uses each glyph metric’s own offset and length.
- No reader layout version bump or repagination is required.

author: arzuparreta
body:
## Qué pasaba

Cerrar Soundsible y volver a abrirlo (PWA en iOS) devuelve la sesión donde estaba, en pausa — eso es correcto. Pero aparecía además el aviso *"Audio was interrupted — tap play to resume"* y la OmniBar se quedaba con **Tap play to resume**, sin que nada se hubiera interrumpido.

La causa es `abandonGraph`: cuando el grafo de mezcla se cae y hay que reconstruirlo — una sesión de audio de iOS interrumpida mientras la app estaba fuera, un contexto cuyo reloj no arranca — informaba `resumed: false` sin mirar si había algo sonando. Con el reproductor en pausa no hay nada que restaurar, así que `resumed: false` es el resultado esperado, no un fallo; la store lo traducía igual en `needsGesture` más toast de error.

Y `needsGesture` lo cobra el *siguiente toque en cualquier parte de la página* (`installAudioUnlock`), que llama a `resume()` directamente. De ahí la segunda mitad: una canción que se dejó en pausa arrancaba sola al volver, sin pasar por play.

## Qué cambia

- `GraphFailure` lleva `wasPlaying`, y sólo un grafo que se llevó por delante música que estaba sonando se convierte en una oferta de reanudar. Lo demás sigue viajando a telemetría (`ui_graph_state` con `was_playing`), que es donde tiene que estar.
- `prime` pausa la pletina antes de asignarle el stream: `unlockDecks` gasta un sample mudo en cada pletina vacía desde cualquier gesto, y una restauración que aterrizaba con ese play en vuelo podía heredarlo.
- El manejador del primer gesto sólo reanuda si además hay pista actual.

El comportamiento al volver es el que ya era la intención: la sesión se restaura entera — cola, sitio, modo, y el taller de Auto si era el que conducía — y se queda **en pausa**, sin badge y sin arrancar por su cuenta.

## Tests

Tres nuevos, los tres fallan sin el arreglo:

- `stores/index.test.ts` — una sesión restaurada a la que le reconstruyen el grafo por debajo no queda con `needsGesture`, no saca toast, y un `pointerdown` posterior no la pone a sonar.
- `stores/index.test.ts` — el contrario: música que sí estaba sonando y perdió el grafo sigue ofreciendo continuar, y cualquier gesto la reanuda.
- `lib/audio.test.ts` — el grafo se reconstruye bajo un reproductor en pausa sin llamar a `play()`, informando `wasPlaying: false`; y `prime` deja la pletina pausada.

`npm test` completo en verde (76 ficheros, 621 tests) y `tsc --noEmit` limpio.

## Segunda puerta: el sample mudo del desbloqueo

Con lo anterior desplegado el aviso seguía apareciendo, y la telemetría del motor dice por qué. En la app instalada hay **13 abandonos de grafo con `resumed: true`, posición 0 y la sesión en `idle`**: no había música, pero `abandonGraph` veía una pletina "sonando".

Era el sample mudo de `unlockDecks`. Se gasta en cada pletina vacía desde cualquier gesto, y `play()` limpia `paused` en cuanto se llama — la plataforma contesta cuando le apetece, y en un arranque en frío de iOS esa ventana dura cientos de milisegundos. Dentro de ella una pletina vacía es indistinguible de una que suena: el grafo restauraba un WAV mudo en la pletina de repuesto como si fuera la pista actual, informaba `wasPlaying: true`, y el aviso volvía por otro camino. Live leía lo mismo a través de `broadcastPlaybackActive`.

`holdsUnlockSample` reconoce el sample por lo que es, y tanto el watchdog del grafo como Live lo descuentan. Test nuevo que falla sin el arreglo (`never mistakes the unlock sample for music the graph took down with it`), con el `play()` dejado pendiente para reproducir la ventana.

Con esto, en el arranque la pletina activa sólo puede estar vacía, con el sample mudo, o con la sesión restaurada en pausa — ninguna de las tres es música que se pueda haber perdido, así que el aviso no puede salir.

## Aparte, para mirar en otro sitio

De 100 eventos de grafo, **48 son `context_stalled` con el contexto en `suspended` y posición 0 en la app instalada**: el `AudioContext` no arranca en los 600 ms que le da `probeContext`, así que la app instalada se queda sin grafo de mezcla — sin blends, sin nivelado, sin tap de Live — en prácticamente cada lanzamiento. Eso no es este PR, pero es lo que hacía que el aviso saliera tan a menudo.


---

## Y la causa de fondo: la mesa de mezclas moría en cada arranque

El aviso falso salía tanto porque hay algo debajo que falla siempre. `unlockAudio` lleva escrita la única secuencia que iOS acepta:

> *(...) create and unlock the context in the gesture, prime the session with a silent buffer (...) and route the decks **before either has ever played**. That is the sequence that works (...)*

Y su primera línea era `unlockDecks()`, que pone el WAV mudo en las dos pletinas y **las arranca**. Veinte líneas después `createMediaElementSource` reclamaba esos mismos elementos con el `play()` todavía en vuelo: exactamente la secuencia que el comentario dice que WebKit castiga, alcanzada por el otro lado. Y es irreversible.

El resultado: el contexto se queda en `suspended`, `probeContext` lo da por muerto a los 600 ms, y la sesión entera corre sin grafo — sin los filtros de las transiciones, sin limitador, sin el vigilante de silencio, y con Live capturando pletina en vez de bus de programa.

**Telemetría del motor, por dispositivo:**

| dispositivo | modo | reproducciones | muertes de grafo |
|---|---|---|---|
| instalación actual (desde 02-ago) | standalone | 66 | **46** |
| instalación anterior (hasta 02-ago) | standalone | 334 | 4 |
| navegador de escritorio | browser | 754 | 6 |

Los 63 `context_stalled` del registro tienen el contexto en `suspended`, sin una sola excepción. `unlockDecks()` se movió al principio de la función el 31 de julio en `e11dfe0`; los primeros `context_stalled` son del 1 de agosto.

El sample se gasta ahora con las pletinas ya enrutadas y todavía intactas, dentro del mismo gesto — así sigue cumpliéndose lo que buscaba `e11dfe0`: que una canción pueda arrancar sin gesto, con el móvil bloqueado.

Test nuevo que falla con el orden viejo: `routes decks that have never played, and only then spends their unlock sample`, con un contexto que anota qué estaba haciendo cada pletina en el instante en que la reclamó.

**Cómo se verifica:** es una señal binaria. Si el arreglo es el correcto, los `context_stalled` de la app instalada desaparecen del registro de telemetría a partir del despliegue.

body:
Two document-only issues in milestone 1, landed together because separate
landings would each move the mainline under the other.

Closes #2
Closes #10

## What changed

`docs/decisions/0002-track-order.md` records that rendering fidelity is built
first and the macro compatibility track second, on one workbook model built once.
It carries the four reasons in the order they carry weight, the cost including
who the first release does not serve, the list of what the macro track may and may
not assume about the rendering track, and the measurement that would reverse it.

`CONTRIBUTING.md` gets a contributor from a clone to the run that exists today,
with the exact command for each of the two gates that reproduce locally, a plain
statement that two other gates have no local form here, the commands that print
the current gate rather than a list of it, and the three rules a contributor
cannot guess.

`DCO.md` carries the certificate text verbatim.

## What failure this prevents

An order that lives only in the reasoning of whoever started gets renegotiated
per issue, and milestone 8 ends up designed against a guess about milestone 2.

The sign-off gate is live and refuses a commit without a matching trailer, so
before this change an outside pull request met a red check pointing at a document
that did not exist.

## Evidence

The last condition on #2 is a claim about the tracker, so it is read from the
tracker rather than from memory. No issue, open or closed, assumes the other
order:

    gh issue list --state all --limit 300 --json number,body --jq '.[] | select(.body|test("macro (track|runtime) (first|before)|renderer (waits|second)|macro half first";"i")) | .number'

prints nothing over all 111 issues, which

    gh issue list --state all --limit 300 --json number,state --jq '[.[].state]|group_by(.)|map({(.[0]):length})'
    [{"OPEN":111}]

counts. The milestone titles run in the same order the record states, rendering
before macro:

    gh api repos/iderex/rechenblatt/milestones --jq '.[] | "\(.number) \(.title)"'
    4 M4 The rendering engine
    8 M8 The macro compatibility track

The last condition on #10 asks that a contributor following the guide exactly
reaches a green local run, verified on a clean clone rather than in the tree the
guide was written in. Cloned fresh at `b44b0dcac065f39689e93df5d318377ec7d640e3`,
running the two commands the guide gives, copied out of it unchanged:

    git grep -nIP '(*UTF)[\x{202A}-\x{202E}\x{2066}-\x{2069}\x{200E}\x{200F}\x{061C}\x{200B}-\x{200D}\x{2060}]' -- .
    (no output, exit 1)

    for sha in $(git rev-list --no-merges origin/main..HEAD); do ... done
    ok    b44b0dcac065f39689e93df5d318377ec7d640e3
    ok    4d150bb2c25de7ed56d822d3f74d185cd6d99c8c

    git ls-files .github/workflows
    .github/workflows/dco.yml
    .github/workflows/dependency-review.yml
    .github/workflows/scorecard.yml
    .github/workflows/unicode-guard.yml
    .github/workflows/zizmor.yml

The other two gates were not reproduced locally and the guide says so rather than
implying otherwise. The workflow audit needs a Python package runner that is not
present here:

    command -v uv uvx ; echo "exit=$?"
    exit=1

and the dependency review runs against an advisory database on the server, so it
has no local form at all.

## What this does not do

The guide names no build command and no test command, because the tree holds no
code and there is nothing to build. That is stated in the guide itself rather
than left as an absence a reader has to notice, and the issues that add those
commands are named there.

`DCO.md` records that clause (a) of the certificate speaks of the licence
indicated in the file and that this repository has no licence file, so a
contributor signing off today cannot point at the terms. That is the open
question in #111 and the file lands in #88. Nothing here decides it.

The failure message in `.github/workflows/dco.yml` points a contributor at
`./DCO`, and the document this change adds is `DCO.md`, which is the name #10
asks for. The workflow is outside the `Scope:` #10 declares, so it is not touched
here and the mismatch is filed separately.

Nobody other than the author has read this change. There is no second reader on
it, and the evidence above stands in place of one rather than alongside one.

author: zir0-93
body:
Fixes the third defect on #156 (the `Any` pollution). The imports and granularity halves of that issue
are **not** addressed here and stay open. Version bumped 10.0.0 → 10.0.1.

## The defect

`externalDependencies()` on Python reported a dependency on `Any` for essentially every component:

```
CLASS       src.svc.Svc                                ext=[typing.List, typing.Any, Any, int, None, requests.Response]
CONSTRUCTOR src.svc.Svc.__init__(helper: Helper) : Any  ext=[typing.Any]
FIELD       src.svc.Svc.anything                        ext=[typing.Any]     <-- annotated `Any`
FIELD       src.svc.Svc.helper                          ext=[Any]            <-- unannotated
METHOD      src.svc.Svc.returns_none() : None           ext=[None]
METHOD      src.svc.Svc.untyped(n: Any) : Any           ext=[typing.Any]     <-- nothing annotated at all
```

`Any` is a type-system construct rather than something code depends on, and clarpse *substitutes it
itself* wherever an annotation is missing — so the label was usually not even written by the author.
`None` on a `-> None` return had the same problem, where Java's `void` yields no reference. The
consequence is false positives, not silence: any rule of the form "X must not depend on anything
external" fires everywhere, so `externalDependencies()` could not be trusted on Python without the
consumer filtering these itself.

## The fix

Two layers, because there were two distinct causes:

1. **The daemon no longer invents a reference where there is no annotation.** `extractParams`,
   `extractMethod` and `extractFunction` only resolve a type ref when an annotation node exists, and the
   field extractors no longer fall back to `externalLabel: 'Any'`. `Any` is still what a missing
   annotation *displays* as — signatures and unique names such as `untyped(n: Any) : Any` are unchanged —
   it just is not a dependency.
2. **`PythonModelAssembler.buildReference` drops type-system placeholders** (`Any`, `typing.Any`, `None`,
   `NoneType`, `NoReturn`, `Ellipsis`) when the annotation did not resolve inside the repo. Only the
   unresolved path is filtered, so a repo class that happens to be named `Any` is still a real
   dependency. This layer is needed because `buildReference` also falls back to the raw annotation text,
   and because an explicitly written `Any` is a real annotation that still is not a dependency.

After:

```
CLASS       src.svc.Svc                                ext=[typing.List, int, requests.Response]  int=[src.helper.Helper]
FIELD       src.svc.Svc.anything                       ext=[]
FIELD       src.svc.Svc.helper                         ext=[]
METHOD      src.svc.Svc.returns_none() : None          ext=[]
METHOD      src.svc.Svc.untyped(n: Any) : Any          ext=[]
METHOD      src.svc.Svc.typed(n: int) : Helper         ext=[int]  int=[src.helper.Helper]
```

## Tests

`PythonTypePlaceholderReferenceTest` over a new `type-placeholders` fixture asserts that no component in
the model depends on a placeholder, that an unannotated method / an explicit `Any` field / a `-> None`
return each carry no references at all, that real annotations all still resolve (internal
`src.helper.Helper`, builtin `int`, generic `typing.List`, third-party `requests.Response`, and the type
inside `Optional[Helper]`), and that a missing annotation still displays as `Any` so unique names are
unaffected.

674 tests pass locally, checkstyle and PMD clean.

## Deliberately not changed

`int` is still reported as an external dependency. Python's `int` is a real class, so recording it is
defensible — but Java skips primitives entirely while recording `java.lang.String`, so "builtin types"
are still not treated alike across languages. That is a judgement call about what a builtin is, noted on
#156 rather than decided here.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

author: korrakottum-code
body:
## Summary
Rescheduling a queue keeps the original row in place (status `rescheduled`) for history, and cancelling/no-show works the same way — but neither should keep blocking that original time slot for new bookings. Confirmed 34 real "rescheduled" queues today/future are affected right now.

Two layers had the bug:
- **Server-side** (`fetchQueuesForRoomDate`, used by the fresh conflict check before saving): only excluded `cancelled`/`no_show`, not `rescheduled` — so rebooking into a rescheduled-out slot actually failed at save time.
- **Client-side** (`BookingPage.jsx`, `TimelinePage.jsx`, `RoomTimeGrid.jsx`): the occupied-slot calculations didn't filter by status at all, so cancelled/no_show/rescheduled slots visually showed as busy in the time grids too.

Added a shared `isActiveQueueStatus()` helper in `helpers.js` and applied it everywhere a slot's occupancy is computed. `rescheduled_in` (the new queue created at the destination slot) is untouched — it's a real active booking.

- [ ] Manually reschedule/cancel a queue and confirm the original slot becomes bookable again

Successfully implemented Vercel Speed Insights for this plain HTML/CSS/JavaScript project.

author: pjordanandrsn
body:
0.11.0 shipped `enable_batched_train` — measured **24x** over the reference loop — with **zero README coverage**. It existed only in the CHANGELOG and a docstring. Same for `enable_fast_train(..., dgrad=True)`.

The symptom table offered exactly one answer to "each step is slow", and it was the one requiring the `[fast]` extra to build.

This is the failure mode that produced #38: a capable reader went to the source, hit documentation that did not describe what was there, and concluded the feature did not exist.

## What changed

The symptom-table row splits by the actual constraint:

| what ran out | call | needs |
|---|---|---|
| each step is slow, VRAM to spare | `enable_batched_train(model)` | — |
| each step is slow, VRAM is tight | `enable_fast_train(model)` | `[fast]` |

And a new **Which training path?** section carries the measured comparison, because the choice is not "which is faster":

| | step | vs loop | peak |
|---|---|---|---|
| reference per-expert loop | 601.2 ms | 1.00x | 59 MB |
| `enable_fast_train(model)` | 132.6 ms | 4.53x | 108 MB |
| `enable_fast_train(model, dgrad=True)` | ~26 ms | ~23x | ~134 MB |
| `enable_batched_train(model)` | 25.0 ms | 24.01x | 417 MB |

The batched path wins on speed and spends peak memory to do it — 417 MB against 108 here, ~1.6 GB per layer against a few MB at production width. **Under offload or VRAM pressure the `[fast]` lane is still the answer**, and the section says so rather than presenting the fastest number as the recommendation.

Also documented: `dgrad=True` and its `grouped-nf4-gemm >= 0.7.0` requirement, that the two paths are mutually exclusive and each refuses to patch over the other, that the return value must be asserted (`0` and "silently still on the loop" are indistinguishable to a caller), and the numerics caveat — group-sorted summation for both, plus dgrad's ~2.9e-3 against an exact loop and its **unmeasured** layer-composed fidelity.

`scripts/check_readme_links.py` passes locally: 0 relative, self-repo refs consistent, 35 GitHub links answer 200.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> **Low Risk**
> Documentation-only README edits; no runtime or API behavior changes.
> 
> **Overview**
> **Documents training accelerators that shipped in 0.11.0 but were missing from the README** — especially `enable_batched_train` and `enable_fast_train(..., dgrad=True)`.
> 
> The **“each step is slow”** row in the symptom table is split into **VRAM to spare** → `enable_batched_train` (no `[fast]` extra) vs **VRAM tight** → `enable_fast_train` (`[fast]`). Imports and examples now show all three `enable_*` calls and stress **asserting the patch count** so callers do not stay on the silent per-expert loop.
> 
> A new **“Which training path?”** section compares reference loop vs `enable_fast_train`, `dgrad=True`, and `enable_batched_train` with step time and peak memory, recommends the `[fast]` lane under offload/VRAM pressure, notes mutual exclusivity and `disable_*` switching, documents `grouped-nf4-gemm >= 0.7.0` for `dgrad`, and adds numerics caveats (group-sorted summation, approximate dgrad backward).

author: sukramj
body:
## Why

The openccu-loom daemon has been the naming authority for its own entities since 0.45.0 and names them in both locales — but those names only ever reached its MQTT discovery plane. This integration therefore rendered its own copy of the same words from `strings.json`: "Alarmmeldungen" lived in two places with nothing comparing them, and the two drift apart on the first edit to either.

For the daemon's new Security & Safety entities the second copy did not exist at all — they would have shown their raw tokens ("security smoke").

## What changes

With openccu-loom 0.54.0 the daemon serves its entity-name catalogue over REST, the client reads it **in Home Assistant's UI language** (which this integration already passes down as `locale=self.hass.config.language`), and a hub data point that carries a resolved name is rendered verbatim.

The data point keeps its English token in `name`. That is the core of the change: `entity_helpers/descriptions/hub.py` matches on `var_name_contains` against `data_point.name` — `ALARM_MESSAGES`, `SERVICE_MESSAGES`, `INSTALL_MODE_HMIP`, `INBOX_SENSOR_NAME`, `CONNECTIVITY_SENSOR_PREFIX`. A localized token there would cost the entity its icon, device class and category. Hence a change to the `name` property rather than a rename at the source.

Language coverage is unchanged: this integration ships `de` and `en`, and so does the daemon catalogue.

## No version bump, no changelog entry

The loom backend is Beta and its user-facing details stay out of the changelog until it ships — the same rule the existing entries state. The version stays **2.8.4**; only the bundled client pin moves.

## What does not change

**aiohomematic is untouched.** Its data points carry no such attribute and `GenericHubDataPointProtocol` does not declare it — the read is an optional `getattr`, so CCU-backed entities fall through to exactly today's behaviour. Nothing about the CCU backend changes.

The read additionally checks `isinstance` rather than mere truthiness: `getattr` on a mock answers with a truthy mock, and a plain truthiness test would pull every mocked data point in the suite into the new branch.

The `strings.json` entries for `alarm_messages`, `service_messages`, `inbox` and `connection_latency` stay: unused on the loom path now, still required for the aiohomematic path.

## Guards

Four tests in `tests/test_generic_entity.py`: the resolved name wins, the match token is untouched, without a resolved name the previous behaviour stands, and an empty name does not blank the entity. **Measured**: without the new branch, `test_resolved_name_wins` fails.

871 tests green, 8 skipped.

## Dependency

Requires `openccu-loom-client` **2026.8.4** (tagged; pinned here in `manifest.json` and `requirements_test.txt`), which needs openccu-loom **0.54.1** / API 5.2.0. CI here goes green once the client is on PyPI.

author: digital2analogue
body:
## What & why

The weekly drift report against `portfolio-vercel` (#174) has been **100% false positives, and had been for a week**:

- `parsimony#114` in a comment read as the hex colour `#114`
- a JSDoc explaining *why* a colour fails contrast — "OTKit's accent-yellow `#FDAF08` is 1.86:1, hence the darkened `#A97405`" — read as someone hardcoding it
- the consumer's own detector tests were reported for containing the deliberately-bad snippets that are the entire point of a detector's tests

Every rule in `rules.mjs` exists to stop a hardcoded value reaching rendered UI. A comment never does. A checker that cries wolf gets ignored, which costs more than the rule enforces — the Curtis line about a rotted contract being worse than none, applied to a detector.

## Three changes

1. **`lintLines` and `lintSnippet` strip comment bodies first**, blanked in place so line numbers and columns stay true.
2. **The hex pattern gains a `(?<!\w)` guard**, so an issue reference *outside* a comment isn't a colour either.
3. **`drift-scan` skips `*.test.*` / `*.spec.*`.** `validate.mjs` §2 has skipped them in this repo since it was written — the comment there literally reads *"tests contain sample violations"* — but the consumer scan never did. Same rule, same exclusion, both sides.

`lintSnippet` is in scope deliberately: `check_usage` (MCP) and `drift-lint` disagreeing about the same text is worse than either being wrong alone.

## What is *not* stripped

String literals. A hex inside one may well ship — which is exactly `portfolio-vercel`'s `lib/checkUsageRules.ts`, whose `SAMPLE_VIOLATIONS` template literal is the lint playground's preset snippet and is genuinely rendered. That file stays correctly flagged and gets a `.driftignore` entry in the consumer (separate PR there).

## Result, verified against `portfolio-vercel@main`

| File | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| `lib/tokenValues.ts` | flagged (`parsimony#114`) | clean |
| `lib/reservationDetail.ts` | flagged (JSDoc contrast note) | clean |
| `tests/unit/checkUsageRules.spec.ts` | flagged (fixtures) | not scanned |
| `lib/checkUsageRules.ts` | flagged (shipped sample strings) | still flagged → `.driftignore` |

**4 files → 1.**

## Alternative considered

`.driftignore` for all four. Rejected — it hides a real detector bug behind per-consumer configuration, and every other consumer would hit the same false positives and write the same ignores.

## Checklist (from CONTRIBUTING.md — CI enforces most of these)

- [x] Rebased on current `main` (branched from `ef76978`)
- [x] `npm run validate` passes
- [x] Ran the tests CI runs: `npm test --workspaces --if-present` **and** `npm run test:unit -- --run`
- [x] Tokens changed → n/a
- [x] Component/metadata changed → n/a; `build:meta`, `docs:components`, `docs`, `docs:design --check` all re-run clean
- [x] Stories added/changed → n/a
- [x] Decisions recorded in `docs/decisions.md` (2026-08-04 entry)

## Verification

| Gate | Result |
|---|---|
| `npm run validate` | all checks pass |
| `npm run lint:stories` | 24 story files pass |
| `npm test --workspaces` | 285 + 70 passed |
| `npm run test:unit -- --run` | 211 passed across 11 files |
| `npm run drift -- ../portfolio-vercel` | 4 flagged files → 1 |

18 new synthetic-fixture tests: comment handling per rule, a line-number check pinning the blank-in-place behaviour, a `lintSnippet`/`lintLines` agreement pair, and a temp-tree suite for `drift-scan`'s file selection (including that skipped files are counted as *not scanned*, not as clean).

author: seantunley
body:
Two pages read customer data for whoever asked. Found while working the page-guard audit.

## What was wrong

**Dashboard (`src/app/(app)/page.tsx`)** — `requireUser()`, then `showSales` / `showService` computed from `hasAnyPermission`. Those only chose which **tab rendered**. All 22 queries sat in one unconditional `Promise.all`, so a workshop technician with no sales permission still made the server count every open lead, sum the whole pipeline, list quotes out for signature with their recipients, and load the customer names attached.

In a server component that is not a near miss: **what a query returns is serialised into the RSC payload whether or not a component renders it.** Not rendering is not a boundary. The rows were on the wire.

**Leads board (`src/app/(app)/leads/page.tsx`)** — no check at all. `getCurrentUser()`, then the full open pipeline: every lead, its value, its assignee, its customer, for any signed-in user — including one whose leads permissions had just been revoked. Its own siblings (`/leads/list`, `/leads/closed`, `/leads/[id]`) already demand `leads.view_all` / `leads.view_owned`, and the sidebar only offers the link to someone holding one.

## What changed

Every dashboard group is **skipped** when its tab is hidden, and every surviving query carries an explicit record-scope predicate built from the existing `getAccessible*Ids` helpers:

```
null  → owner / *.view_all → no filter
[]    → no accessible rows → `in: []`, an impossible match
[id…] → those rows
```

Collapsing the first two — `ids?.length ? … : {}`, `in: ids ?? []` — silently hands every row to a user with no access, and is what the tests target.

Also removed three whole-row `include`s that existed to print one field:

| was | shipped into the payload | to render |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `include: { assignedTo: true }` (agenda ×2) | the whole `User` row, **password hash included**, 20× per day column | a first name |
| `include: { contact: true }` (fleet) | every customer's phone, email, address, notes — for the entire fleet | a customer name |
| `include: { user: true }` (activity feed) | the whole `User` row | nothing — never read |

## Two judgement calls worth reviewing

**1. `/leads` is guarded on the page, not in `ROUTE_RULES`.** `routeAllowed` fails closed on tokens minted before a rule existed, and there is no `sessionVersion` bump for "a new rule appeared". Adding `/leads` to the table would bounce **every already-signed-in rep** off the busiest page in the product until they signed out and back in. The page guard is the authoritative boundary (`permissions.ts`); the edge table is a pre-filter in front of it. Happy to add the rule as a follow-up alongside a forced re-auth if you'd rather.

**2. The fleet query stays unbounded.** "Service due" is computed in JS from the latest service record + mileage log, so a `take` would silently under-report it — worse than a slower query. The `select` is the bound instead (~90% smaller payload, and the PII is gone). The "Fleet" tile now comes from a separate `count()` rather than `vehicles.length`, so the number stays exact.

## Tests

`tests/dashboardRecordScope.test.ts` — 7 structural tests over both pages. Extracts every `prisma.<model>.<op>( … )` by bracket matching and asserts each one on a scoped model (a) names its scope variable and (b) is the consequent of its tab's gate — reading the ternary condition exactly, not looking for the gate name *somewhere nearby*, because a neighbouring array element's gate is always nearby.

`tests/recordScopeContract.test.ts` + `tests/stubs/prismaRecordScopeSpy.ts` — 7 behavioural tests running the **shipped** helpers through a module-loader intercept (the `journeyRetention.test.ts` pattern). Proves no view key → `[]` **and zero queries**; `*.view_all` → `null` and zero queries; a broken/uninitialised RBAC snapshot → `[]`, never `null`; `view_owned` → a list whose SQL names all three ownership arms.

**Sabotage-verified** — each bug reintroduced individually, the specific test confirmed failing, then restored:

| sabotage | caught by |
| --- | --- |
| drop `...leadScope` from the open-lead count | scope test |
| run the vehicle query on `true` instead of `showService` | gate test |
| pull `lead.count` out of its ternary entirely | gate test |
| `leadIds?.length ? … : {}` | null-vs-empty test |
| resolve `getAccessibleVehicleIds` regardless of tab | lookup-gate test |
| `assignedTo: true` back on the agenda | whole-row test |
| leads board back to `getCurrentUser()` | guard test |
| unscope the board's lead query / the customer picker | board scope test |
| `signatureRequest` back to `quoteId: { not: null }` | scope test |
| no-view-key returns `null` instead of `[]` | contract test |
| broken RBAC snapshot returns `null` | contract test |
| `view_all` pays for a query anyway | contract test |
| activities fall back to unrestricted | contract test |
| the owned-lead SQL stops naming the caller | contract test |

`npm run test:unit` **1096/1096** · `tsc --noEmit` clean · `eslint` no new findings (the 2 `react-hooks/static-components` warnings on the dashboard pre-date this branch — verified by stashing).

## Conflicts to expect

- **#331** edits `src/lib/permissions.ts`. This branch does not, but `tests/recordScopeContract.test.ts` asserts on those helpers' behaviour; after #331 merges it should still pass — the tenant predicate it adds is orthogonal to the `null` / `[]` / `[id…]` contract. Worth a re-run rather than an assumption.
- No overlap with #327 (`tests/oneAuthorizationSource.test.ts` is untouched — `/leads` stays out of `ROUTE_RULES`, so its existing assertion remains true).

Not merged. Yours to land.

author: jbj
body:
Fixes #73.

## What was wrong

Not the composition. The scenery is already drawn once across the whole board — the hole bands have nothing to do with it. The seam is one gradient counted twice.

`#ground` fills two shapes: the near ground band (a rect hundreds of units deep) and the hill crest that rises out of it (a path a few dozen units tall). It was declared in SVG's default `objectBoundingBox` units, so each shape ran the *whole* light-to-dark wash inside its own box. The crest therefore finished at its darkest along its flat bottom edge — `L width y+depth L0 y+depth Z`, straight across the full width — sitting on a band that was still at its lightest. That is the hard horizontal line.

Portrait shows it worst because there the near band is deepest, so the mismatch between the two is largest, and it lands between two rows of holes. Landscape had a fainter copy of the same line.

## The fix

Measure the wash against the canvas: `gradientUnits="userSpaceOnUse"` from the top of the near band to the bottom of the board. The band and the crest become two shapes cut from one wash rather than two copies of it, and the crest's flat bottom edge disappears into the band it stands on. What is left at the join is the crest's own silhouette, which is what it was always meant to be.

The crest's `opacity="0.95"` still softens it against the far band above, and is now invisible below the join — 95% of a colour over the same colour is that colour.

## Checked

Rendered both orientations before and after, at level 6 (sea) and level 10, plus the full `npm run shot` run. Sampling a pixel column across the join in portrait: before, `#E2CE99` → `#F0E0B3` in one row; after, a smooth ramp. Landscape gains the same.

`tests/scenery.test.ts` grows a check that every backdrop's ground wash is measured against the board and spans the near band to the bottom, in both orientations — it asserts the shapes sharing the wash are more than one first, so it cannot pass by finding nothing. Broken on purpose and confirmed failing before being put back.

`npm run verify` passes.

author: jimmyejones
body:
## What & why (docs-only)

The owner spends long stretches watching a stack run or browsing the gallery, and asked for an **optional ambient soundbed** while they do. Filed at the top of "Features that serve real workflows" with a full implementation plan.

**Flagged honestly as *enjoyment polish*, not a workflow feature** — the entry states it must never displace a bug or PRIORITY 1–4 work, and should be pulled on a slow run. The `AGENTS.md` §1 priority banner is **deliberately left untouched**. It is fully self-contained (one frontend module + a toggle; zero backend, zero engine, zero schema), so it carries no risk to the imaging path.

## The load-bearing decision
**Synthesise the audio in the browser via the Web Audio API — do not ship or fetch an audio file.** Rationale captured in the entry:
- **Licensing** — an agent must not pull music off the internet, and there is no cleared track to bundle.
- No multi-MB binary asset in the repo/Docker image.
- **Nothing downloaded at runtime** — consistent with the offline-first, nothing-leaves-the-NAS rule.
- A synthesised bed **never loops audibly**; a short bundled sample always does over a multi-hour session.

No new npm dependency required.

## Also specified
- **Sound design** — detuned drone pad + filtered pink/brown noise bed + sparse pentatonic bells, into a **runtime-generated** reverb impulse (decaying noise burst, no asset), then a compressor as a safety limiter.
- **Traps baked in** — default **OFF**; `localStorage` per-device rather than `webapp/config.py` (no config migration, nothing on the server); `AudioContext` resumed **only from a user gesture** (autoplay policy, or the toggle silently lies); **suspend, don't mute** when off (a convolver burns CPU in an hours-open tab); gain ramps to avoid clicks; pure scheduling logic split from the node graph so it is testable under jsdom with a stubbed `AudioContext`.
- **Precedent to follow** — `jobNotify.ts` (client-only opt-in toggle read fresh at use time) and the `astrostack.*` key convention from `SampleTourNote`/`MergeSuggestionsCard`.
- **Explicit non-goals** — no user-uploaded tracks, no per-page themes, no job-completion sound effects, no visualiser.

Docs-only; no code, schema, config, or behaviour change.

author: mrnetwork0001
body:
`app/api/bridge/estimate/route.ts` formats the amount for App Kit with `toFixed(2)`:

```ts
// App Kit expects amount in human-readable decimal format
const amountString = amountNum.toFixed(2);
```

But USDC has 6 decimals, and `app/api/bridge/rebalance/route.ts` executes the transfer at full precision:

```ts
const bridgeAmountString = (amountNum + estimatedBridgeFee).toFixed(6);
```

Two consequences:

**The quote prices a different amount than the transfer.** `12.3456` USDC is estimated as `12.35`, then bridged as `12.3456 + fee`.

**Sub-cent amounts are estimated as zero.** `components/dialogs/use-bridge-fee-estimates.ts` fires an estimate for any `parseFloat(amount) > 0`, so `0.001` USDC reaches the route and is sent to App Kit as `"0.00"`.

This changes the estimate to `toFixed(6)`, matching the precision the rebalance route already uses, so the quote is priced for the amount actually transferred.

One-line change plus a comment explaining why the precision matters.

body: ## The bug Reported: fill in the tutor profile, submit, see "Tutor profile required" again next login — as if nothing saved. On both the student and tutor profile pages, the error notice renders **above the form**. A failed save (`!res.ok`) set the error but never scrolled to it — only the network-error and success paths did: ```tsx if (!res.ok) { setError(data.error ?? t("edumatch.profile.tutor.saveFailed")); setSaving(false); return; // <- no scroll, unlike the other two paths below } ``` After scrolling down to reach the submit button on these long forms, a failed save left the viewport right where it was — nowhere near the error banner, now off-screen above. That reads as "nothing happened," not "it failed." ## Fix Add the same `scrollIntoView` the network-error and success paths already have. ## Not yet confirmed as the *whole* explanation The tutor profile's submit button is also disabled until at least one subject **and** one level are selected — the screenshot in the original report showed neither selected. An incomplete form silently doing nothing on click would produce the identical "I did it and nothing stuck" symptom, for an unrelated reason. This PR fixes the one confirmed defect (the invisible error); worth checking with the user whether it fully resolves their report. ## Verification - `turbo typecheck --filter=edumatch` — clean - `pnpm --filter edumatch test` — 235 passed - Not verified visually — reproducing needs a live failing submit (e.g. a validation/moderation rejection), not triggered in this session. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) --- ## Summary by CodeRabbit * **Bug Fixes** * Error notices on student and tutor profile submissions now automatically scroll into view, making validation and save failures easier to notice. * Existing scrolling behavior for successful saves and network errors remains unchanged.

author: nomah4
body:
## The problem

The `hotvds.com` vhost had `root /var/www/dev.hotvds.com/dist` — the exact directory the staging workflow rsyncs into. Both hostnames served the same files, so:

- every merge to `main` published straight to customers, with no step in between;
- `dev.hotvds.com` was not a staging environment, just a second hostname over the same directory with `noindex` headers;
- `rsync --delete` overwrote the live site in place, leaving no previous build to roll back to.

This was live behaviour, confirmed on the host — not a theory. Both vhost configs are in `/etc/nginx/sites-available/` and both carried the same `root`.

## What changed on the server

Already applied — production was serving from its new root before this PR was opened, so merging it changes nothing by itself.

```
/var/www/hotvds.com/releases/<utc-timestamp>-<ref>/   last 10 deploys
/var/www/hotvds.com/current -> releases/<...>         nginx root
```

The switch was seeded with a byte-identical copy of what was already live, so no served content changed at cutover. Staging still serves `/var/www/dev.hotvds.com/dist` and is untouched. Backups of the vhost and `authorized_keys` are in `/root/backup-*.20260806055354`.

## What changed in the repo

`deploy-prod.yml` — runs on a `v*` tag or a manual dispatch, **never** on push, and re-runs lint, types, tests, and build before publishing, because a tag can point at a commit no PR ever saw. `main` keeps auto-deploying to dev.

`deploy/hotvds-prod-deploy` — installed on the host as the forced command of the production deploy key. That key gets no shell and can only run `deploy` / `rollback` / `list` / `current`, as the unprivileged `hotvds-deploy` user. The build arrives as a tar stream, is unpacked outside `releases/`, and is checked for `index.html` and `assets/` before the symlink is swapped, so a truncated upload cannot replace a working site with a 404.

Rollback is now a symlink swap:

```bash
ssh -i <key> hotvds-deploy@<host> list
ssh -i <key> hotvds-deploy@<host> rollback
```

## Testing

Exercised against a throwaway tree on the host before installing: deploy, list, rollback, rotation past the 10-release cap, refusal of an empty upload and of one missing `assets/` (live release verified unchanged in both), a path-traversal attempt in the ref label, and arbitrary commands through the restricted key. All artifacts cleaned up.

## Before this can ship

Two repo secrets still need setting — `gh secret set` was not permitted in the session that prepared this. See the notes on the PR conversation.

author: menqstudio
body:
`.github/workflows/release.yml` pinned actions/setup-node to
0b93645e9fea7318ecaed2b359559ac225c90a2b, which is actions/setup-PYTHON's v5.3.0
commit. A commit exists in exactly one repository, so GitHub cannot resolve
actions/setup-node at that SHA:

    Unable to resolve action `actions/setup-node@0b93645e...`,
    repository or version not found

Every `v*` tag push therefore died at that step — before `npm ci`, before the bundle,
before the signing step — so this workflow has never produced an installer. The pin is
now the same actions/setup-node v4.1.0 commit the other five workflows already use, and
the trailing version comment names the action's real version again.

Fixing the line is not enough: a SHA pin is only wrong RELATIVE to other pins, so no
existing check could see it. tools/check_action_pins.py encodes that relation, stdlib
only and with no network:

  1. third-party `uses:` must be pinned to a 40-hex commit SHA, or be a DECLARED
     exception with a written reason (today: tauri-apps/tauri-action@v0, audit F-15,
     owner-gated because it holds the updater signing key);
  2. a SHA pin must carry a trailing `# <version>` comment — the human-auditable half;
  3. one action resolves to ONE (sha, version) across the dispatched workflows;
  4. one commit belongs to ONE action. This is the rule that catches this defect, and
     because it is a fact about git rather than about versions it also covers the
     vendored engine/ and apps/desktop/ workflow copies GitHub never dispatches (F-22),
     which carry their own independent pin history and are exempt from rules 1-3.

Wired as the `action-pins` job in supply-chain.yml. 11 self-tests, including a faithful
reconstruction of this exact defect, so the gate is proven to go RED on it rather than
merely to pass on today's tree. Verified: RED on the original line, GREEN after the fix;
coordination + capability gates GREEN.

This is independent-audit F-46, on `main` where it still bites. The same one-line fix
already exists on the PR #53 branch; the gate does not.

author: baozhoutao
body:
Fixes #5360

**comment-only, no runtime change, skip-changeset requested.**

## 问题

`packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/tenancy-service.ts` 里 `TenancyService.degraded` 的文档注释结尾仍写着:

> Only reachable for `isolated` — `group` is enforced by the open engine, so it has no missing dependency to degrade against.

这是 ADR-0105 D12 修正前那一版的残留(当时 `group` 确实自激活),与**同一个文件 120 行之后的实现相反**。

## 前提复核(origin/main@`1624f4a`)

逐点对着实现核过,issue 的事实全部成立:

- `tenancy-service.ts:196-207` `isolationActive()`:`requestedPosture === 'single'` 直接 `false`,其余**两种有墙 posture 一视同仁**地 `deps.probeIsolation()`,注释里自己写着「BOTH walled postures probe」;
- `tenancy-service.ts:224-226` `degraded` = `postureEnforcesWall(requestedPosture) && !isolationActive()` —— `group` 请求 + 无 `org-scoping` ⇒ `degraded === true`;
- `packages/cli/src/commands/serve.ts:1831` 的 D5 启动闸门是 `const multiTenant = tenancyPosture !== 'single'`,`group` 同样走 FATAL / `OS_ALLOW_DEGRADED_TENANCY` 分支 —— 所以注释前半句「Boot is refused unless ...」对两种 posture 都成立,保留不动。

更强的佐证是**既有测试已经把实现钉死**,即错的是注释而不是代码(`tenancy-service.test.ts`):

- `requested: 'group'` + `probeIsolation: () => false` ⇒ `expect(t.degraded).toBe(true)`;
- `requested: 'group'` + runtime 已装但 `probeEntitledPostures: () => ['isolated']` ⇒ `expect(t.degraded).toBe(true)`。

## 改法

**以实现为准**,而不是照抄 issue 的措辞 —— 实现里降级有**两个**触发条件,issue 只提了第一个:

1. 企业版 `org-scoping` runtime 缺席(`probeIsolation()` 为假);
2. runtime 已装,但用 `supportedPostures` 声明**不授权**所请求的 posture(ADR-0105 D12 的授权接缝,`isolationActive()` 第 200-202 行)。

新注释两条都写了。

另外,**同一 interface 上方 `posture` 的注释有同源的 D12 残留** —— 它只举 `isolated`(「an `isolated` request that cannot be」)、且把原因只归给「the enterprise package is absent」。它不像 `degraded` 那句是直接说反,但属于同一批过时收窄,且就在被修的那句上方 15 行;只改一处会让读者在上一段仍得到同样的错误印象。故一并按同一事实收敛为「a walled request that cannot be — `group` 或 `isolated` alike」。**落点仍是单文件、仅注释。**

## 验证

零行为改动,注释无断言面,故不新增测试;既有测试全绿即为验收标准。

- `pnpm --filter '@objectstack/plugin-auth' typecheck` —— `tsc --noEmit` 无输出(通过);
- `pnpm --filter '@objectstack/plugin-auth' test` —— **Test Files 34 passed (34) / Tests 786 passed (786)**;
- `node scripts/check-nul-bytes.mjs` —— OK(5678 个文件,无裸控制字节)。

## 不做 changeset

注释-only,发布不可见,不提交空 changeset(#4898:空 changeset 滞留发布)。需要 `skip-changeset` 标签。

author: rachelslurs
body:
Closes items 2c and 10 of #75.

## Why

The addon ships two surfaces and neither was covered by anything that runs the real thing.

`@storybook/addon-vitest` puts `**/*.mdx` into `test.exclude` unconditionally, so no Docs entry runs as a test at any configuration. Story tests execute inside the preview, so none of them reaches the manager. What was left was mocks on both sides: `stories/DocsBlock/DocsBlock.stories.tsx` hands the container a `resolveOf` written by hand, and the panel's unit tests mock `storybook/manager-api` outright. A fixture cannot disagree with the contract it is imitating, and `OversightDocsContainer` reads that contract inside a bare `catch {}`, so a Storybook release that changed it would drop the block from every consumer's Docs page with nothing logged anywhere.

## What this adds

`scripts/built-storybook-checks.js`, plain node in the same idiom as `prepublish-checks.js`. It serves `storybook-static` with `vite preview` and drives it with the Playwright chromium CI already installs, so the marginal CI cost is the run itself.

```
✔ built Storybook checks passed against …/storybook-static:
  · the Docs page mounts parameters.docs.container (data-display-card--docs)
  · the real DocsContext resolves Card's findings
  · the block heading outranks DocsContent, and paints the muted color
  · an unattached Docs page renders, without the block (overview--docs)
  · the manager boots and the addon registers its panel
  · the panel reports Card's findings in the manager
```

The unattached case asserts both halves, that `.sbdocs-content` is present and the block is not. That is not defensive writing: forcing `hasComponent` true makes `useOf` throw uncaught, Storybook replaces the whole page with its error screen, and the Oversight heading count goes to zero. A check written as absence alone passes the mutation it exists to catch.

A `compat` job pins the declared peer floor and a React 19 entry, prints what actually resolved before doing anything else, and runs the gate rather than only proving `pnpm install` succeeded. It has to boot the manager, because the crash `src/react-shim.ts` exists for happens in the manager bundle and is invisible from the preview.

`pnpm test` and `build.yml` both run the gate. It refuses when `storybook-static` is older than the addon's `dist`, since a build that fails partway leaves exactly that state and the run would otherwise grade the previous artifact and call it a pass.

## What the compat job found immediately

The peer range said `storybook@^10.3.0`. It was not true.

| storybook | `.sbdocs-content` | Oversight heading |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 10.3.0, 10.3.6 | 0 | 0 |
| 10.4.0, 10.4.6 | 0 | 0 |
| 10.5.0 | 1 | 1 |

Zero `.sbdocs-content` means addon-docs' own container never rendered, so the Docs page is gone, not merely missing the block. Removing only `container: OversightDocsContainer` from the demo's `preview.ts` makes the same 10.3.0 build render cleanly with no page errors, and pinning the same clone back to 10.5.0 with the container restored renders correctly, so this is the Storybook version rather than a poisoned checkout.

It was never true. `^10.3.0` was set in `cd451fe` (2026-07-15) and that same commit fails identically when built against 10.3.0, so no released version has worked there. The commit before the service API work fails the same way, so it is not a regression from that merge either. Nothing in CI installed anything other than what the lockfile resolved, so no job could have caught it.

The range correction itself is **#94**, kept separate so it can land on its own. **Merge #94 first**: the `storybook-floor` entry here pins 10.5.0, which is the floor only once #94 declares it. Root cause, and whether 10.3 and 10.4 can be made to work, is #93.

This PR changes no published package, so its changeset is empty.

## Two premises from #75 that did not survive

**`ThemedRoot`'s fallback is not observable here.** #75 expected this route to cover it. `storybook/theming` is not in `storybook/internal/preview/globals`, so a `storybook build` dedupes it to one module instance, the theme context resolves, and the inherited branch is what a Docs page takes. The block's own docstring already said the theme is inherited on a Docs page. The fallback stays guarded by the unit tests from #86.

**`match: ({ viewMode }) => viewMode === 'story'` in `manager.tsx` is inert.** The type says `match` decides the `active` prop, but for `types.PANEL` that prop tracks which tab is selected. Built as `'docs'`, with the change confirmed in the shipped bundle, the tab sits in the same place on a story and the findings stay just as visible. What keeps the panel off Docs pages is Storybook rendering no addon panel region there at all, not even Controls.

It is documented in place rather than deleted. The predicate states the intent correctly and is the value we would want if a release began honoring it, so removing it is the direction that carries risk. The only change to a published package in this PR is that comment, which is why the changeset stays empty.

## Mutation evidence

Two passes, each in a fresh context, rebuilding between every mutation and confirming the marker reached both `dist/` and the built bundle.

| Mutation | Checks that failed |
| --- | --- |
| `resolveOf` throws | container mounts, findings resolve, heading color |
| heading `color` deleted | heading color, alone, reporting `rgb(46, 51, 56)` against the expected `rgb(92, 101, 112)` |
| `hasComponent` forced true | unattached page, alone |
| `addons.add` removed | manager boots, panel findings |
| panel forced to an empty state | panel findings, alone |
| `Card.elevated` documented | Docs findings and panel findings, both on row content |

Two things the second pass found, both fixed here. `renderedText` looked for the block's `h2` on both surfaces; the manager has only a `div role="heading"`, so panel failures fell through to the whole document and printed Storybook's inline radix scrollbar CSS instead of the panel's message. It now scopes to the tabpanel and reads `innerText`, and re-running the mutation confirms it reports `No manifest entry for this component.` The false comment about `match:` is corrected above.

The manager assertions wait on visibility rather than presence. `AddonPanel` hides an inactive panel with the `hidden` attribute instead of unmounting it, so `attached` would pass for a panel nobody can see.

Two honest limits. No mutation breaks the heading while leaving findings intact, so the "container mounts" check is never isolated from "findings resolve"; it is a precondition rather than an independent claim. And nothing here can catch a wrong `match` predicate, because that predicate has no effect to catch.

author: subhankarmaiti
body:
### Changes

Marks the client-side Management API as deprecated so consumers get a migration runway before it is removed in v6. Nothing is removed and no behaviour changes — this is additive.

`auth0.users(token)` now carries a `@deprecated` JSDoc tag and logs a one-line warning when called. The tag is also applied to `IUsersClient` and its `getUser()` / `patchUser()` methods, `ManagementApiOrchestrator`, and the `GetUserParameters` / `PatchUserParameters` types, so editors show a strikethrough wherever any part of the surface is referenced.

The reason for the removal: calling the Management API from a client requires an access token with over-privileged scopes (`read:current_user`, `update:current_user_metadata`) that can't be kept secret in a mobile app or a browser. Auth0.swift and Auth0.Android have both already dropped their Management clients. The recommended path is a backend-for-frontend — your app sends its own access token, and the backend validates it and calls the Management API with its own credentials:

```diff
- const profile = await auth0.users(accessToken).getUser({ id: user.sub });
+ const res = await fetch('https://your-api.example.com/me', {
+   headers: { Authorization: `Bearer ${accessToken}` },
+ });
+ const profile = await res.json();
```

If you only used `getUser()` to read the signed-in user's profile, you don't need a backend at all — `auth0.auth.userInfo({ token })` works with a normal access token, and the `user` object from `useAuth0()` is decoded from the ID token. The migration guide has a new "Deprecated in v5.x — removed in v6" section covering this.

The runtime warning sits on `users()` rather than on `getUser()` / `patchUser()`, since that is the single entry point to the surface — it fires once per client acquisition instead of on every request.

The legacy MFA methods on the auth client are deprecated separately in #1625.

<!-- This is an auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->

## Summary by CodeRabbit

* **Documentation**
  * Added migration guidance for the deprecated Management API user operations, including their planned removal in v6.
  * Recommended routing Management API requests through a secure backend or BFF.
  * Documented `userInfo()` and current authentication profile data as alternatives for reading the signed-in user’s profile.
* **Bug Fixes**
  * Added runtime warnings to help identify continued use of the deprecated APIs.

author: pulbhaba
body:
## Summary

Part of pulbhaba/albedo-novels#23. Adds a third service `novels-api` to `docker-compose.yml` so a developer can run MySQL + auth-api + novels-api together with one command. The Dockerfile it consumes lives at `../backend/novels/Dockerfile` (added in pulbhaba/albedo-novels#26).

## Changes

- **docker-compose.yml**: new `novels-api` service.
  - `build.context: ../backend/novels`, `dockerfile: Dockerfile`, `image: albedo-novels-api:local`.
  - `ports: [${NOVELS_HOST_PORT:-8000}:${NOVELS_CONTAINER_PORT:-8000}]` — host and container ports independently overridable.
  - `environment` wires JWT verification to the in-stack auth-api: `AUTH_ISSUER=http://auth-api:8080`, `AUTH_AUDIENCE=albedo-novel-service`, `AUTH_JWKS_URL=http://auth-api:8080/oauth2/jwks`. `HOST=0.0.0.0` and `PORT=${NOVELS_CONTAINER_PORT:-8000}` for uvicorn.
  - `depends_on`: `mysql (service_healthy)` + `auth-api (service_started)`. The existing auth-api compose definition has no healthcheck, so `service_started` is used to avoid an unsatisfiable `service_healthy` wait.
  - `healthcheck` probes `http://127.0.0.1:8000/health` via an inline `python -c` urllib call. The local FastAPI server leaves /health unauthenticated, so the probe is reliable as soon as uvicorn is up. 15s `start_period` covers pip install on first build.
- **.env.example**: adds `NOVELS_HOST_PORT=8000`, `NOVELS_CONTAINER_PORT=8000`, and the three auth-wiring vars with sensible defaults that match the in-stack service names.

## Validation

- `docker-compose -f docker-compose.yml config` resolves cleanly with all three services, the depends_on graph, env interpolation, and the novels-api healthcheck.
- Local `pytest` for the novels service (separate repo) — 7 passed in `tests/test_local_app.py` + `tests/test_health_handler.py`. `/health` payload parity is asserted there.
- A full `docker compose up --build` end-to-end run was not executed in this sandbox (no Docker daemon); reviewers with a daemon should verify the /health probe flips to healthy and `curl http://localhost:8000/health` returns `{"status":"ok","service":"albedo-novel-service"}`.

## Notes

- The auth-api compose definition is unchanged; this PR does not modify authentication, OAuth, or database schema defaults.
- Workspace layout assumes `../backend/novels` exists, i.e. a full workspace checkout produced by `repo sync` against `albedo-manifest` (matches the assumption the infra README already documents for auth-api).
- Closes the shared-stack portion of pulbhaba/albedo-novels#23. The Dockerfile + README side of that issue is in pulbhaba/albedo-novels#26.

author: vaibhavsrv
body:
## Problem

In `ods/scripts/session-cleanup.sh`, inline Python cleanup logic rewrote `sessions.json` directly using `with open(sessions_file, 'w') as f: json.dump(data, f, indent=2)`. If process execution is interrupted during session pruning, the target `sessions.json` file can be left partially written or corrupted in place.

## Fix

1. Update inline Python session cleanup logic in `session-cleanup.sh` to write updated session states to a temporary file via `tempfile.mkstemp` inside `sessions_file.parent`.
2. Use `os.replace` for atomic replacement of destination `sessions.json` files.

## Verification

Verified syntax with `bash -n ods/scripts/session-cleanup.sh`. `git diff --check` passed cleanly with zero whitespace issues.

author: aarya-1424
body:
Free becomes the invited-tester allowance: one diagnosis a month (unmetered), 500 chat messages, and 7 planning actions a day. Built from measured per-operation costs rather than round numbers:

    diagnosis  18,900 in + 5,500 out = 24,400   unmetered, 1/month
    chat        2,000 in +   400 out =  2,400   x 500      = 1,200,000
    planning      800 in +   300 out =  1,100   x 7 x 30   =   231,000
                                                 total     = 1,431,000

1,431 credits at 1,000 tokens each, and exactly reachable: 40,000/day x 30 for chat, 7,700/day x 30 for planning. Roughly Rs 168 per tester per month.

Chat and planning meter SEPARATELY. daily_token_usage had one counter per founder per day, so every feature shared a ceiling and exhausting chat would have disabled planning. `source` joins the primary key; existing rows backfill to 'chat' because everything metered so far was chat.

Diagnosis is capped by COUNT, not tokens. It is unmetered on purpose -- nobody may hit a wall mid-assessment -- which leaves the number of runs as the only thing bounding its cost. The check sits after the resume path, so an in-progress diagnosis can always be continued, and fails OPEN: refusing someone their diagnosis because a lookup failed is worse than serving one extra. There was no limit of any kind before this; diagnosis_used exists in the ORM but nothing outside the admin panel ever read it.

Two bugs found while enabling the gate:

* enforcement_enabled() read only os.environ. pydantic-settings parses .env into Settings and never exports it, so PLAN_ENFORCEMENT_ENABLED=true in .env was read as absent -- the flag looked set and enforcement stayed silently off. Now reads the environment first, then settings.
* Free had a planning token budget but not the plan_your_day feature, so a tester promised 7 planning actions would have hit 403 on the first one.

TESTING-PHASE ANOMALIES, asserted in tests so they break on the way back out rather than surviving into launch:
* Free grants 1,431 credits -- ~8x Pro -- inverting the credit ladder. Harmless while only invited testers exist and no pricing page is visible; indefensible the moment either changes.
* plan_your_day moves from _PAID into Free. Must go back when Free is resized.

Free includes zero discovery calls (free_calls_per_month=0), which only became reachable now that the gate is live: invited testers cannot book one. Correct per the catalog and a real product consequence, so it is pinned by a test rather than left to be discovered.

Tests: the daily-limit ordering test pinned a literal 4,000 and would have silently stopped testing anything when the ceiling rose -- it now seeds from the catalog. The planning gate test asserted "free is refused", which would pass for the wrong reason once Free gained the feature; it now strips the feature from the resolved plan and proves the gate enforces regardless of catalog contents.

Verified live: planning 200 on Free, a second new diagnosis in the same month 429s with "available from 1 September", credits and ceilings tie out exactly (1,431,000 reachable == 1,431 credits x 1,000). Migration round-trips; the downgrade folds per-source rows back into one before narrowing the key, since collapsing it directly would violate uniqueness.

Suite green except test_message_latency_bounded, which is NOT caused by this: it fails identically with enforcement off (1,619ms vs 1,250ms on) and ranges 1,054-1,666ms against remote Supabase versus a 500ms bound described as "offline". Left failing rather than quietly raised.
