body:
Closes #152 (rescoped — see the correction comment on the issue; the original "no socket server" premise explains none of the symptoms).

## What was actually wrong

Two SSE endpoints, two unrelated reasons, both 404 in every deployment. Measured against the running E2E stack with a positive control, before and after:

| | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| `/api/v2/elitea_core/conversations/prompt_lib/1` (control) | 200 | 200 |
| `/api/v2/events/prompt_lib/1` | 404 | **200** `text/event-stream` |
| `/api/v2/notifications/events/prompt_lib/1` | 404 | **200** `text/event-stream` |
| `/api/v2/definitely_not_a_route/prompt_lib/1` (negative control) | 404 | 404 |

Both were driven end to end, not just status-checked: a `redis-cli publish` to `project:1:events` arrives as an `application.created` SSE event, and a row inserted into `centry.notifications` arrives as `notifications_notify` after the `notifications_ready` handshake.

### A. `/api/v2/events/prompt_lib/{projectID}` — the fallback pair with no arms

Wired `RedisClient`. **Why Redis and not `EventSource`:** every elitea-main deployment in the repo already runs Redis and already passes `REDIS_URL` (`deploy/docker-compose.yml`, `docker-compose.e2e-standalone.yml`, `helm/elitea-main/values-staging.yaml`); none is given a NATS endpoint. `deploy/helm/nats` is the LLM gateway's broker, and elitea-main's only NATS-shaped variable is `GATEWAY_NATS_URL`, which is the gateway *client*. Choosing `EventSource` would mount the route against a broker that is not deployed. No new env var. `redisOptionsFromEnv` had no production caller either — it does now.

A configured-but-unreachable Redis fails startup rather than silently leaving the field nil, because a nil field unregisters the route again, which is the whole defect.

### A′. `/api/v2/notifications/events/prompt_lib/{projectID}` — the one the client calls

The issue attributed this 404 to the same gate. It isn't: this route has its own, and had **two** closed. `NewRouter` returns `newPrototypeCompatibilityRouter` whenever any prototype field is set — always, in practice — and only `production_router.go` mounted this path; and it was composed only inside the `ELITEA_AUTH_CONFIG_FILE` branch, so OIDC-only deployments never built it at all. Mounted in the prototype router at the top level (the `/api/v2` group's shadow wrapper buffers the response and has no `Unwrap`, so a stream inside it could not flush) and given an OIDC-only composition path mirroring `CurrentProjectList`. Authorization is unchanged: `apimw.Auth` still rejects anonymous, `serve()` still requires a runtime principal, `authorize()` still resolves `models.notifications.notifications.list`.

### Two defects that only appeared once the routes existed

- **`ssewriter.New` asserted `w.(http.Flusher)` directly.** `OtelMiddleware`'s `statusRecorder` embeds the `http.ResponseWriter` *interface*, so only three methods are promoted and the assertion fails — even though it implements `Unwrap()` precisely so this would work. Observable: 500 `streaming not supported`. Now walks `Unwrap` through `http.ResponseController`, the way `notifications/current_events.go` already did. It still *refuses* a genuinely unflushable writer rather than accepting one and stalling the client.
- **`centry.notifications` is queried by three Go call sites and created by no migration.** The list endpoint hides it: it runs the query under `if err == nil` and returns 200 with an empty array on any failure, so a missing table is indistinguishable from "no notifications". The stream does not swallow, and answered 503. Added to `001_initial.sql` (dev/E2E bootstrap only — production schema is owned by elitea-migrate).

### B. The guard that missed it

`declaredAbsent` justified `EventSource` by `RedisClient` and `RedisClient` by `EventSource`. Circular: both nil satisfied the allowlist while the route they gate existed nowhere. Fallback chains are now read out of `router.go` and require at least one wired arm.

Worth recording: the first implementation used one `(?s)if cfg.A != nil { … } else if cfg.B != nil {` regex and **passed the both-nil mutation** — `.*?` is leftmost-first, so an unrelated earlier `if cfg.X != nil {` claimed the match and swallowed the real chain, reporting a pair that was never there. It now locates each `} else if` and walks back to the nearest preceding `if`. That is why the mutation test is in the record below rather than assumed.

### C. JRNY-026 — rescoped, not repointed

Its mechanism was retired for this surface, so the manifest entry is `waived` with a `replacesBehaviour` naming the SSE journey. The acceptance text is left **byte-for-byte alone**: `uictl` holds it immutable against the git baseline, and editing it in place to describe SSE is exactly the "old wording pointing at the new mechanism" the rescope exists to avoid. `uictl parity-manifest --validate` reports nothing new for JRNY-026 (its one complaint is the repo-wide missing elitea-ui baseline checkout, shared with 1228 other items).

The test became three, and the old `vite_socket_server: ""` precondition is inverted rather than deleted:

- **J26.1** — the stream is mounted, and a transport-level drop is recovered by the browser on its own. `route.abort()` (a connection failure, not an HTTP status — a status is terminal for `EventSource` and would assert the opposite while looking identical), then a real in-page `EventSource` against the real server, real cookie, real RBAC. Asserts a second request to the same URL and the `notifications_ready` handshake.
- **J26.2** — `test.fail()`. The sidebar's own subscription passes `personal_project_id`, and `app/session-store.ts:67` fills that with the **user id**, with a comment saying so, because `/forward-auth/info` returns only `authenticated`/`user_id`/`email`. So it asks about a project the user is not a member of and gets 403 — terminal, one console warning. Giving that endpoint a real personal project id is a separate product decision and is not attempted here.
- **J26.3** — the socket dot, kept and re-read: on a chat-only stack `Disconnected` is *correct* state, not a defect, and it is the tripwire for the day a socket server appears.

Driven through a test-owned `EventSource` rather than the sidebar's because the sidebar cannot connect at all today (J26.2) — stated in the file rather than worked around.

### D. Out of scope, untouched

JRNY-008's `stream tokens → stop` stays blocked on #126 (`ChatService`/`Predictor` nil, arbiter pickle vs indexersvc JSON). Sockets were not enabled to reach it. `VITE_SOCKET_SERVER: ""` is unchanged.

## Verification

Every number below was run, not inferred. Images rebuilt and image IDs confirmed changed each time (`1dea624d67d8` → `abace7a197f8` → `79e4092ece48` → mutant `c11a6e39ea10` → restored `42bf803407bd`).

- Go: `go build ./... && go vet ./... && go test ./...` — clean.
- Unit: `npx vitest run` — **1162 files, 10427 tests, all passing**.
- E2E full suite, both engines, against a **cold-started** stack (`down -v` → `up` → `seed`, so the new migration is exercised from empty volumes): chromium **66 passed**, webkit **66 passed**.

### Mutation tests

| mutation | expected | result |
|---|---|---|
| both fallback arms nil + both allowlisted (the exact pre-#152 state) | nil-gate test fails | ✅ fails, naming the pair |
| `RedisClient` unassigned in main.go | nil-gate test fails | ✅ |
| `else if cfg.RedisClient` gate disabled | router registration test fails | ✅ |
| `if cfg.CurrentNotificationEvents` gate disabled | router registration test fails | ✅ |
| same, rebuilt into the image | **J26.1 fails** | ✅ |
| `ssewriter` stops following `Unwrap` | ssewriter test fails | ✅ |
| `ssewriter` accepts unflushable writers | ssewriter test fails | ✅ |
| `REDIS_URL` absence gate removed | redis client test fails | ✅ |
| ping failure ignored | redis client test fails | ✅ |
| the seeded `models.notifications...list` permission revoked | J26.1 fails | ✅ |
| the drop

author: grimblaz
body:
Inserts **#1045** into `Documents/Planning/sequence.yaml` `umbrellas:` at **rank 5**, satisfying the `safe-operations` §2c obligation that a new umbrella be ranked or it stays invisible to the control tower.

## Why rank 5

Rank 5 is the slot held by **#986** — *"Project memory has no lifecycle: learnings accumulate privately, never become repo artifacts"* — which closed after #1015 delivered the store's retention machinery and #1019 shipped the first promotion tranche. #1045 is its direct successor, so it inherits the rank.

#986 is **left in the list** rather than removed: `recently_closed_days: 14` may intend closed umbrellas to keep rendering for a window, and dropping a line on that assumption is a separate maintainer call.

## Why not rank 1

The memory store's budget pressure reads more urgent than it is. The index is ~20.2k characters against a budget that is a *fraction* of an observed **24,978-character** truncation limit — so real headroom before anything is lost is several thousand characters, and the demotion outflow is proven working (77 exits drained in one pass on 2026-08-09).

The actual deadline is **2026-09-08**: all 93 critical entries took their first and only deferral on 2026-08-09, a critical entry may not be deferred twice, and that sweep must otherwise demote critical lessons to the cold archive to stay lawful. Thirty days accommodates a design phase and two chunks without displacing #970 (dated 2026-08-31 retirement), #761, or #848 — each of which has a harder constraint than a memory index sitting inside its own safety margin.

## Scope

One line. `sequence.yaml` is not a plugin entry point, so no version bump is triggered.

body:
## What changed

- replaces prefix commands with ten consistent Discord slash commands
- centralizes management and team-leader authorization using configured role IDs
- replaces mutable JSON writes with transactional SQLite storage and one-time legacy JSON import
- fixes draft picking so the selected player is recorded and added to the picking team atomically
- protects team membership, leadership, roster capacity, match uniqueness, and score invariants
- adds strict environment validation, startup/deployment scripts, graceful shutdown, and safe error replies
- adds a multi-stage non-root Docker image, heartbeat health check, and `/data` persistent-volume contract for Coolify
- documents local setup, command registration, configuration, SQLite backups, and Coolify deployment
- adds GitHub Actions plus tests for configuration, permissions, slash-command definitions, teams, drafts, and matches

## Why

The imported prototype had a guaranteed crash in `/draft pick`, allowed any server member to change tournament matches, advertised commands that were not registered, depended on privileged gateway intents, and stored live state in JSON files that could be corrupted or lost during a Coolify redeploy.

## User and operator impact

- users interact through discoverable slash commands, including names containing spaces
- management-only actions now enforce the configured management role at execution time
- the bot needs only the non-privileged `Guilds` gateway intent
- Coolify must mount persistent storage at `/data`
- run `npm run deploy:commands` once after deployment or whenever command definitions change
- the first startup imports the tracked legacy JSON data into an empty SQLite database

## Validation

- 11 Node test-runner tests pass inside the Linux Node 22 Docker test stage
- production Docker image builds successfully on the target OVH VPS
- legacy migration smoke test imports 3 teams and active Week 2
- final image verified as user `node`, with a `/data` volume and heartbeat health check
- all JavaScript files pass `node --check`
- `npm audit --omit=dev` reports zero known vulnerabilities
- staged secret scan is clean; `.env`, `node_modules`, and the source archive were never committed

author: steffenmaas
body:
Rückmeldung aus **steffenmaas/vitacoach** (Healthy Crew), das dieses Modul produktiv fährt.

## Der Defekt

`autonomous-loop.md` hat die Regel **„Watchdog, always"** — die deckt jeden *Dispatch* ab: kein Heartbeat, Prozess wird gekillt und geborgen. Den *Loop selbst* deckt nichts ab.

Der Einstieg sagt: *„a standing orchestrator session on a ~15-minute rhythm. **It re-arms itself**"*. Das ist der einzige genannte Mechanismus. Wer das umsetzt, baut eine Kette von Einmal-Weckern, bei der jeder Zyklus den nächsten legt — mit einem Single Point of Failure, auf dem kein Alarm liegt.

## Was passiert ist

```
09:30 → 10:05 → 10:47 → 13:18 → 14:28 → (nichts)
```

Um 14:28 hat der Agent das Nachlegen angekündigt und nicht getan. **Vier Stunden Entwicklung verloren.**

Das Perfide: **jedes Gesundheitssignal blieb grün.** Jeder Wecker der Kette war erfolgreich abgelaufen (`ended_reason: run_once_fired`), es gab keinen Fehlschlag zu melden. Der Ausfall war die *Abwesenheit* eines nächsten Ticks — und Abwesenheit löst nichts aus. Aufgefallen ist es dem Founder, weil vier Stunden lang keine Commits kamen.

Im selben Environment lief parallel ein Loop mit einem **wiederkehrenden** Cron (`40 */6 * * *`) tagelang ununterbrochen weiter. Derselbe Agent, dieselbe Infrastruktur — der Unterschied war allein der Auslösemechanismus.

Bemerkenswert: Schritt 1 verlangt bereits *„watchdog armed"*. Der Begriff bezieht sich aber auf die Stall-Watchdogs der Dispatches, und ein Watchdog für den Loop wird nirgends definiert. Die Lücke ist also schon halb benannt, nur nicht geschlossen.

## Die Änderung

| Stelle | Vorher | Nachher |
|---|---|---|
| Entry | „It re-arms itself" | wiederkehrender geplanter Auslöser als Rückgrat; Selbst-Nachlegen als schneller Pfad darüber |
| Loop rules | nur Dispatch-Watchdog | neue Regel **„The loop needs a watchdog too"** mit dem Fehlerfall |
| Schritt 1 HEALTH | „watchdog armed" | zusätzlich: wiederkehrender Auslöser vorhanden und innerhalb eines Intervalls gefeuert |
| Schritt 9 Gate | „never ends without re-arming" | Nachlegen wird **geprüft**, nicht angenommen, und ersetzt den Auslöser nie |

Der feine Takt bleibt möglich: Scheduler haben oft eine Stundenuntergrenze, der Loop will ~15 Minuten. Selbst-Nachlegen behält also seinen Platz — es ist nur nicht mehr tragend. Klappt es, findet der wiederkehrende Tick die Arbeit schon erledigt und beendet sich still. Klappt es nicht, nimmt er den Loop wieder auf statt gar nichts.

Der Fehlerfall steht ausformuliert im Dokument, nicht nur die Regel — sonst rekonstruiert die nächste Person das „warum eigentlich zwei Mechanismen" nicht und vereinfacht es wieder weg.

## Im Ursprungsprojekt bereits umgesetzt

Ein stündlicher Cron ist dort angelegt und aktiv. Ich habe ihn allerdings **noch nicht laufen sehen** — der erste Lauf steht aus, und das Werkzeug hat gewarnt, dass die gefeuerte Sitzung möglicherweise ohne MCP-Connectors startet. Das prüfe ich beim ersten Tick nach; falls es zutrifft, ist das eine zweite, davon unabhängige Meldung wert.

body:
## Summary
Consolida uma sessão longa de divagação (2026-08-07/08) sobre o ADR-021 (Convergia Mobile: Ronda Fotográfica) num documento único, para não depender de segurar tudo de cabeça numa conversa só. Registrado como extensão separada (`ADR/ADR-021-Extensao-Questionario-Painel-Gestao.md`), mesma convenção já usada por `ADR-011` (emenda ao `ADR-010`) e `ADR-014-Emenda-1` (emenda ao `ADR-014`) — não edita o corpo do ADR-021 original.

- **Decisão 1** — o questionário de ronda deixa de ser fluxo fixo por categoria de risco e passa a ser montado a partir de um catálogo extensível de modelos (3 iniciais: Riscos Críticos, Procedimentos, 5S) + dado real do banco já populado + sugestão da IA, sempre com confirmação humana antes de salvar. Descarta tanto o fluxo fixo atual quanto construção 100% livre no chat (bloqueada por falta de tool-calling no `runCognitiveEngine`, já ligado a `ENG-038`/`FORGE-WORKSPACE-001`).
- **Decisão 2** — registra a necessidade de um painel de gestão (dashboard agregado, lista filtrável, achados como itens rastreáveis tipo Plano de Ação), ainda sem código nem ID de roadmap formal.
- **Decisão 3** — especifica os templates multi-página que a Fase 2 (`CONV-014`, geração de relatório) vai aceitar por upload (PPT/docx/PDF via conversão para imagem; XLS como exportação de dado, não layout; Power BI resolvido via CSV/XLS, sem gerar `.pbix`), fallback para o padrão Midnight Executive, e a nota de auditoria "Editado em [data]" quando o relatório for gerado a partir de ronda editada.
- **Pendências (P1-P3)** ficam registradas em aberto — escopo de PT (sinalizar vs. gerenciar), qual das três interpretações de "passivo trabalhista" perseguir, e sequenciamento frente ao que já está pronto pra Builder (Ctrl+V, cores de classificação, tema claro/escuro). Sem resposta a essas três, nenhuma instrução de Builder é preparada para esta extensão.

Também atualiza `INDEX.md` para apontar o novo documento.

author: duane-eldridge
body:
## Summary

Prevent compute-response dispatch from crashing the Grafana plugin when Nominal returns a response variant the plugin cannot render, and contain unexpected batch panics as query errors.

## What changed

- Replaced nil `ComputeNodeResponse` union handlers with typed handlers that return descriptive errors.
- Moved the `arrowNumeric` arm onto the shared unsupported-response handler, and removed its standalone test because the table test now covers that arm.
- Reject unknown future response variants instead of silently producing an empty result.
- Added a recovery boundary around each batch partition so an unexpected panic becomes a generic per-query error instead of terminating the plugin process.
- Added test coverage for:
  - Response variants the plugin does not currently support.
  - Unknown response variants.
  - Isolation between unsupported responses and successful sibling queries.
  - Panic recovery for batch partitions.

## User-facing behavior

Response variants the plugin cannot render now return query errors while the plugin remains available. Successful sibling queries continue to render.

If an unexpected panic occurs during batch execution, every query in that partition receives:

`Internal error while executing query batch`

## Testing

Passed:

- `go vet ./pkg/...`
- `go test -count=1 ./pkg/...`
- `go test -race -count=1 ./pkg/...`
- `go test -count=2 ./pkg/plugin`
- `gofmt -l pkg`
- `git diff --check main`

Focused regression tests cover all changed behavior.

## Residual risk

The recovery boundary operates at the batch-partition level. An unexpected panic therefore errors every query in that partition for the current refresh, including partial results produced before the panic. Per-query recovery was intentionally avoided to keep the backstop small and prevent repeated stack logging for a systematic failure.

author: keithfawcett
body:
Closes #8 from `docs/audit-remaining-work.md`. Not money-risky, but it's the one architectural promise the repo makes on its front page.

## What wasn't true

CLAUDE.md principle #2 and the README promise **every table exports to CSV + JSON + SQL, and a hosted export re-imports into self-host.** Three gaps:

1. **The exported set omitted `PartnerProgram`, `PartnerCommission` and `Coupon`.** A restored instance had the partner roster but no program grants, no record of what any partnership was *agreed at*, and no coupon → (partner, program) mapping — so coupon-driven conversions couldn't be re-attributed.
2. **No SQL dump existed**, though the contract names it as one of the three formats.
3. **Import hardcoded `id` as the conflict target**, but `PartnerCommission` is keyed on `partnerId` — adding it naively would have thrown on every re-import.

Each table now carries its real primary key in `EXPORT_TABLES`, and that list doubles as the FK-safe import order.

## Two more the round-trip test caught (both live bugs)

- A JS array coming out of `select *` is **ambiguous**: `Program.commissionRule` is a `jsonb` array, `Program.categories` is a `text[]`. The driver renders a bare array as a Postgres array literal, so importing **any program with compound commission rules** failed with `invalid input syntax for type json`. Both the import and the dump now read the live column types and render each correctly (`'[{"type":"percent"}]'` vs `'{"saas","devtools"}'`).
- Same ambiguity in the dump: a `text[]` column was being emitted with `::jsonb`.

## The SQL dump

`GET /export.sql` (full bundle) and `GET /export/<Table>.sql`. Portable by default — rows are written under a psql variable, so one file restores into any instance:

```bash
psql "$DATABASE_URL" -v tenant_id=default -f openpartner-export.sql
```

It opens a transaction, `set_config('app.tenant_id', …)` so it works on the RLS-scoped app role as well as the privileged one, emits tables in import order, and every statement is `ON CONFLICT (pk) DO NOTHING` — idempotent and resumable, same guarantee as the JSON path. `?tenantId=<id>` bakes a literal instead, for clients that don't run psql meta-commands.

## Versioning

`schemaVersion` 1 → 2. `POST /import` still accepts **v1** bundles — an export sitting on someone's disk must not become worthless because we added tables. `SUPPORTED_IMPORT_VERSIONS` only ever grows.

## Tests

`export-roundtrip.test.ts` (11): seed one row in **every** exportable table with the FK chain intact → export → wipe → restore → compare. Once through JSON, once through the SQL dump **actually executed against Postgres**, and once through the portable dump put through psql's own substitution. Plus idempotency on both paths (the case that used to throw on `PartnerCommission`), v1 acceptance, PK/order invariants, and escaping of apostrophes, jsonb arrays, `text[]` and nulls.

Full suite: 274 passing. `pnpm typecheck` + `pnpm lint` clean. No migration.

## Also

The portal export page listed 9 of the 14 tables and offered no SQL — now complete, with a SQL column and a SQL bundle button. `docs/data-portability.md` is the format contract: bundle shape, the table list with its keys, both restore procedures, the type-fidelity note, and the checklist for adding a table.

Slice D of the Starlight full-theming handoff. **Stacked on #91** (extends `site-starlight.css`) — retarget after it merges.

## 3.6 — mobile drawer

- New `StarlightSidebar` override (registered in `astro.config.mjs` `components:`) prepends the **site nav** to the sidebar pane: flattened `visibleHeader` manifest (same derivation as the docnav — no hardcoded links) + GitHub/Discord icon row, styled to the comp's `.drawer` idiom (mono 15px rows, `--line-soft` separators, active row = amber + 2px inset rail + `--accent-soft` fill; `.foot` icon row).

## 3.7 — theme unification

- Marketing pages read the persisted Starlight preference (`localStorage['starlight-theme']`) via a pre-paint inline script in `MarketingLayout` head — no flash; static `data-theme="dark"` remains the no-JS / first-visit default; `auto`/unset follows `prefers-color-scheme`, mirroring Starlight's own resolution.

The handoff's own 3.7 QA list includes "a KB page" in both themes, so this is the item working as specified; all KB **articles** remain byte-identical. body: ## Resumo Adiciona o agente **WhatsApp** para responder mensagens pessoais e profissionais em modo automático, usando Gemini/OpenAI, histórico local por chat e três níveis de risco (`routine`, `ambiguous`, `legal_high`). Assuntos com risco jurídico recebem resposta segura (sem orientação legal), não ficam sem resposta. Conexão via **Neonize** (sessão do seu número; API não oficial — ver avisos abaixo). ## Como usar ```bash pip install -e ".[dev,whatsapp]" export GEMINI_API_KEY=... # e/ou OPENAI_API_KEY # Testar resposta sem WhatsApp whatsapp preview --chat-id 5511999999999@s.whatsapp.net --text "Podemos falar amanhã?" # Subir o bot (QR no terminal na 1ª vez) whatsapp run # whatsapp run --dry-run # não envia, só processa ``` Opcional: `WHATSAPP_OWNER_NAME`, `WHATSAPP_PERSONA`, `--include-groups`. ## Validação - `ruff check src tests` — OK - `pytest tests/test_whatsapp_*.py` — OK (8 testes) - `pytest` completo: 3 falhas pré-existentes em `test_interaction_pipeline` / `test_pa_standalone_registry` por `invalid_scope` ao refrescar token Gmail no ambiente cloud (não relacionadas a este PR) ## QA Validation Guide ### Risk Assessment **Critical (integração + efeitos externos)** — o bot envia mensagens reais em seu nome; API não oficial do WhatsApp pode violar ToS e levar a banimento. ### Affected Pages & Features | Área | Impacto | |------|---------| | CLI `whatsapp` | Direto | | `data/whatsapp-*` (sessão/estado) | Direto — não commitar | | Procon / Questor / Contratos | Nenhum | ### Manual Validation Steps 1. author: chemaclass
body:
## 🤔 Background

Related #1009

Selection by name was one-directional — `--filter` includes, with no way to exclude. Tags had both `--tag` and `--exclude-tag`; names had only the positive form, so dropping a handful of tests meant tagging them first.

## 💡 Changes

- `--exclude-filter <name>` skips tests whose name matches, with semantics identical to `--filter` (including the leading `test_` strip), so the two are symmetric
- Repeatable and OR'd; exclusion wins when a name matches both, mirroring `--exclude-tag` over `--tag`
- Excluded tests are never selected — not reported as skipped, and not counted in the header
- Works alongside `--filter`, `--tag`, `--shard` and `file::fn` targeting

## Design note

The value is read from `BASHUNIT_EXCLUDE_FILTER` inside `get_functions_to_run` rather than threaded through as a new argument. That function is reached from two places — the header count (inside a subshell) and the runner (main shell) — and passing the filter to only one of them would print a count the run then contradicts. One source, both callers.

`export -n` per #839, verified: the flag does not leak into nested `./bashunit` runs.

## Verification

Mutation-tested: disabling the exclusion branch fails 11 tests. Green on the Bash 3.2 floor. Selection asserted through `--list` (#1007).

**SQL must be applied manually in the Supabase SQL Editor after merge** (migration 196).

## The fix

`calculate_period_settlement` computed `round(pm.km * (t.total_paid / t.total_km), 2)` — divide first. Postgres numeric division truncates the repeating quotient to 16 fractional digits, dropping an exact half-øre tie just below the half, so the server rounded 45 × 221,43 / 90 to 110,71 kr while the client's double arithmetic rounds the same tie to 110,72 (GV-471-F2, found by the Phase A client-parity oracle). Migration 196 re-declares the function **completely off 194** (provenance chain verified: 054→055→068→070→107→108→112→114→157→194, nothing later touches it) and changes exactly two expressions — the printed `tripCost` and the copy `net` recomputes inline, which must move together or `net` disagrees with its own components by an øre. `fuelRate` (a genuinely different quantity) and the zero-km/deferredFuel branches are deliberately untouched.

## Riders

- **`KNOWN_FINDINGS` is empty again** — GV-471-F2 removed in the same PR, its README section moved to the Fixed pattern with the historical repro.

Sub-batch 1 of THR-929. **Not a closing PR** — 9 of the 30 templates remain, deferred by a live mutex, so no close keyword rides this one.

## What changed

THR-899 split the vagueness lexicon by intent and scoped enforcement by field class, which enforced `thing` / `way` / `ways` / `nothing` / `anything` / `whatever` in **outcome prose** for the first time — `countVagueness()` had never matched them — so 30 shipped templates went from clean to failing without anyone writing a word.

21 of them are rewritten here. Every one now reads `vaguenessByClass.outcome === 0`. Outcome-side only: afterimages, band fragments, and `narrativeTemplates.success`/`.failure`.

Three that carry the shape of it:

| template | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| `loc.awaken_spirit` | "**someone** answers … here in a **way** that can be seen" | "the spirit of the place answers … here in a shape that can be seen" |
| `ac.senior.planar_probe` | "**something** on the other side has taken note" (×4 slots, inconsistent) | "the watcher on the other side has taken note" (consistent across all four) |
| `tavern.overheard_rumor` | "**Nothing** usable surfaced tonight" | "No name, no route, no date surfaced tonight" |

**Scene prose is untouched everywhere**, per the ticket's explicit prohibition — re-tightening it is what produced the "asking the room for them by name" contortions THR-899 removed, so every remaining `s`-column hit is a natural indefinite doing ordinary work.

## Why nine templates are missing

`src/data/encounter-content.ts` is deliberately not in this diff. THR-860's PR #1114 holds that exact file open (held behind THR-883, `mergeStateStatus: DIRTY`), and the mutex's stated reason names it. Per THR-688 rule B the reason is verifiably *applicable*, so this serializes on the surface the reason names rather than bouncing a ticket it can deliver 21/30 of. Those nine ride a later sub-batch, which carries the close keyword.

## Cleared as collateral (not targeted)

- `social.intimidate` fell to one not-X-but-Y once *"the dynamic is less favorable than expected"* — a single outcome line tripping two detectors at once — was rewritten.
- `npc_bribe` fell to one second-person once *"You have bought nothing but suspicion"* became *"The coin goes back in the purse; the suspicion stays."*

## What is deliberately not claimed

**`audit:nudge-batch` still exits 1 on this set.** Three templates still fail — `npc_eavesdrop` and `ag.senior.deep_expedition` on abstraction **and** second-person, `social.spy_on` on abstraction. All on detectors THR-899 never touched, all predating it, none reachable from this ticket's scope: both second-person counts stay ≥ 2 with every outcome-side `you` removed because the rest sit in scene prose, and the abstract-noun proxy fires on `expedition`, `surveillance` and `fragment` — the templates' own subject nouns, which `nudgeAuditDetectors.ts` itself documents as *"a **ranking** signal, not a verdict on any single line"*.

Filed as [THR-1066](https://linear.app/threadbare/issue/THR-1066/three-templates-in-the-thr-929-set-fail-abstractionsecond-person-on) with the content-defect-versus-detector-false-positive fork stated, rather than gamed by editing out-of-scope prose. Impediment #517 records the harness gap: it gates on every detector while a scoped ticket owns one, so the per-template `o/s/i` column is the honest evidence and the CLEAN verdict is not.

author: alexrbrowne
body:
**Dispatching has been silently doing nothing.**

Every dispatch materialises a brand-new worktree directory, and Claude Code asks *"do you trust this folder?"* the first time it starts in one. Nothing answers it — the session is unattended by design — so `claude` sits on the prompt forever. The prompt is never read, no work happens, and the record still reports `working · processing your prompt`, because the lifecycle hook fired on session start.

Caught it by looking inside a stuck session:

```
 ❯ 1. Yes, I trust this folder
   2. No, exit
```

and confirming the sessions were alive but running `zsh`, not `claude`.

## The fix

The worktree inherits the repo's own entry from `~/.claude.json`. **Trust is inherited, never invented** — if the repo is not already trusted, neither is the worktree, and you answer once as you would anywhere else.

Cloning the *whole* entry rather than writing `hasTrustDialogAccepted` alone was found the hard way: a half-populated entry is ignored and Claude Code asks regardless. It also means the worktree runs with the repo's allowed tools and MCP servers, which is right — it is the same codebase in a different directory.

The config belongs to Claude Code, so it is round-tripped whole: unknown keys survive, the write is atomic (temp + rename), and every failure path is quiet. A dispatch that shows a trust prompt is worse than one that does not; a dispatch that does not happen at all is worse than both.

## Verification

Tests cover inheriting from a trusted repo, refusing an untrusted or unknown one, preserving unrelated config, degrading quietly on a missing or corrupt file, and idempotency on re-dispatch.

Verified end to end against a real trusted repo and a fresh directory: **claude starts with no trust prompt**. The probe entry was removed afterwards and the config left exactly as found.

## Release

No label — a bug fix, so this cuts a patch.

body:
Summary
This PR introduces the Category model and implements comprehensive search, filtering, and sorting functionality for the events API, alongside query optimization and database seeding capabilities.

Key Changes
1. Models & Database
Category Model: Added a new Category model with name and unique slug fields.
Event Model Update: Linked Event to Category via Foreign Key (category = models.ForeignKey(..., null=True, blank=True)).
Migrations: Generated and applied database migrations (0003_category_event_category.py).

2. Search, Filter & Sorting (Django REST Framework)
Search (EMP-182, EMP-183, EMP-184): Integrated filters.SearchFilter allowing case-insensitive search by title and description.
Filtering (EMP-198, EMP-199, EMP-200):
Implemented EventFilter class using DjangoFilterBackend.
Supported filtering by category slug (?category=classical-jazz) and category ID (?category_id=1).
Handled validation: requests with non-existent categories gracefully return a 400 Bad Request.
Sorting (EMP-214, EMP-215, EMP-216):
Integrated filters.OrderingFilter for sorting events by date, title, created_at, and price.
Handled invalid sorting parameters gracefully without crashing the server (200 OK fallback).

3. Performance Optimization (EMP-185, EMP-201, EMP-217)Added .select_related("organizer", "category") to event querysets to eliminate N+1 database query performance issues.

4. Developer & QA Utilities
Added a custom management command (python manage.py seed_data) to quickly seed the database with initial categories and test events.

Verify API Endpoints:
List categories: GET /api/events/categories/
Filter by category: GET /api/events/?category=classical-jazz
Search events: GET /api/events/?search=Rock
Sort events: GET /api/events/?ordering=-price
Validation check: GET /api/events/?category=invalid-slug (Returns 400 Bad Request)

author: kasai32
body:
Stacked on #6 — base is `feat/close-case-ui`, not `main`, because `DECISIONS.md` #52–#57 append directly after #51, which only exists on that branch. GitHub will retarget this to `main` automatically once #6 merges. Review this diff alone; it is one commit.

## Four defects, each verified rather than argued

**Audit integrity.** `POST /resolution-queue/:id/undo` fired an unconditional `UPDATE` and reported success regardless. RLS enforces clearance on an UPDATE by matching zero rows, not by raising — the behaviour #30 already addressed on the *merge* path. An under-cleared reviewer got `{ok: true}` and an audit entry stating the merge was undone while `canonical_of` never changed. The chain stayed tamper-evident and attested to something that never happened, which is worse than a missing entry. Now checks `rowCount`, and scopes the statement with `canonical_of = $2` so undoing an old queue row cannot wipe a newer merge of the same object.

**Existence inference, three routes.** RLS filters rows by classification; it does not mask references a permitted row carries to a forbidden one.

- `GET /objects/:id` returned `canonical_of` raw and joined neighbours only to `relationship_types`, so an edge classified below its endpoints handed an under-cleared reader the far end's uuid.
- `/graph/expand` emitted edges referencing nodes absent from its own node list.
- `/graph/path` returned the unreadable uuid **verbatim in its `path` array** — the plainest disclosure of the three.

No field values crossed the boundary. In an AML context an entity uuid is enough to cross-reference against another source. All four reads now resolve references through RLS-subject queries, and both graph routes seed from `objects` so an unreadable root cannot serve as an existence oracle.

**Planner regression.** Entity resolution bound the JSON key as a parameter (`properties->>$1`) against an expression index on the literal `(properties->>'name')`. Expression indexes match structurally, so this reached the index only under a custom plan — a prepared-statement layer or plan-cache promotion would have silently reverted #32 at one sequential scan per ingested row, with nothing at runtime reporting it. #32's `EXPLAIN` evidence was taken against `bench.sql`, which writes the key as a literal, so it never covered the shape production ran.

## Verification

`api/scripts/test-rls-http.sh` gained five graph assertions, **confirmed to fail against the unfixed code and pass against the fixed one**:

```
FAIL: /graph/expand returned edge endpoints absent from nodes: ...000021
FAIL: /graph/expand response contains the SENSITIVE account uuid anywhere
FAIL: expanding from an unreadable node returned 2 node(s)/3 edge(s), expected 0/0
FAIL: /graph/path returned path entries absent from nodes: ...000021
FAIL: /graph/path response contains the SENSITIVE account uuid
```

Getting there needed two fixes to the tests themselves: a seed edge (#57), because no unreadable node sat between two readable edges; and a different probe node, because the first one's only edge was RESTRICTED, making that assertion unable to fail.

`db/scripts/test-rls.sh` now splits hard invariants from reported exposures — the seed deliberately contains an edge classified below its endpoints, so failing on it was wrong.

Full run on a rebuilt database (all 14 migrations clean, 16 objects / 12 edges, zero duplicates): `test-rls.sh` pass, `test-rls-http.sh` ALL CHECKS PASSED, `test-audit-chain.sh` pass, both typechecks clean.

## Reviewer focus, if you have 15 minutes

1. `api/src/routes/resolutionQueue.ts:159-178` — the only defect that put a false statement into a tamper-evident log. Confirm the early return precedes `writeAudit` at :185.
2. `api/src/routes/graph.ts:230-266` — `expandFrontier`. Question why it is a `LEFT JOIN` plus a flag rather than an inner join: an inner join applies `LIMIT $2` after filtering, letting a session scan far past `MAX_PATH_EDGES_EXAMINED` while consuming almost no budget. That is the non-obvious decision here.
3. `api/src/routes/ingestion.ts:107-124` and `:243-253` — the only place in the codebase that deliberately interpolates into SQL text. Verify the identifier regex *and* the `property_schema` membership check both run before the value reaches the query string.

## Known and deliberately not done

- #31's 49,754-degree hub timing predates the fan-out cap now counting *visible* neighbours, and has not been re-measured. Needs `loadtest-generate.sh` at 1M/5M first.
- `explain-trgm-plan-modes.sh` is included but proves nothing at seed scale — it warns below 100k rows.
- No `CHECK` or trigger yet forbids an edge classified below its endpoints, or a `canonical_of` chain. `test-rls.sh` detects both; constraining them at write time is the stronger fix and is not in this pass.
- `test-audit-chain.sh` tampers a row and never restores it, so it must run last. Noted in `SECURITY_GAP_ASSESSMENT.md` A.8.29 rather than reordering CI, since nothing is currently broken.

Also records #52 (tenant isolation is the database boundary — the policies would fail *open*, not closed, across co-located tenants) and refreshes `SECURITY_GAP_ASSESSMENT.md`, which was scoped to Phases 0–5: twelve rows moved, three prioritised gaps closed by #42/#43/#48, and A.8.12's "RLS prevents cross-clearance leakage by construction" corrected to the claim that actually holds.

body:
Perder um combate passa a **custar**. Cada monstro declara o que faz com quem ele derrota; o **Ogro** (o de 3 tesouros) **evacua** — mão, mochila e os cinco encaixes vão aos cemitérios — e quem evacuou **recomeça no turno seguinte com 4 Portas + 4 Tesouros em `recompor`**.

É a fatia **2a**, a primeira das quatro em que o bloco 2 foi decomposto (decisão #110). Decisões **#112–#126** do bible.

**693 → 737 testes**, typecheck 7/7, lint limpo.

## O que entrou

- **`MonstroCarta.badStuff`**, obrigatório e **lista**. Dois verbos: `evacuacao` e `perdeSlot(família)`. A escala é regra, não dial: **só o de 3 tesouros evacua**.
- **`BadStuff` virou a quarta união gêmea do repo**, travada por **`_CoberturaBadStuff`** em `shared`. Sem ele, verbo novo em `cartas` sem o `partida` deixa o typecheck **7/7 limpo**.
- **O interpretador puro** `aplicarBadStuff` (`partida/src/badStuff.ts`), `switch` fechado por `never`. Ele **devolve os eventos** porque só ele sabe qual efeito produziu o quê — reconstruir isso no `mesa.ts` instalaria um segundo interpretador da união.
- **`perdeSlot('mao')` limpa os DOIS encaixes** e deduplica por id: o Montante é uma carta em duas vagas, e limpar uma só o deixaria vivo dando stats cheios.
- **O item arrancado vai direto ao cemitério** — assimetria deliberada com `destinoDoDesequipado`, que prefere a mochila. Se fosse à mochila, o item voltaria ao corpo no mesmo turno (a punição vira nada) **e** devolveria zero carta ao baralho (a economia vira nada).
- **O Bad Stuff aparece escrito na carta do monstro** (#119), em duas superfícies: o painel de combate e a carta na mão, ao lado do "Procurar encrenca" — que é onde a escolha acontece.

## Os números (soak, N=240 partidas por braço)

Controle interno: **o Ogro em duas versões**, mesmo build, mesma sessão, uma variável. Não há braço "desligado" — a #118 recusou o variante `nenhum` pelo lado do jogo.

| Medida | Resultado |
|---|---|
| Margem da evacuação sobre punição leve | **+13,57 cartas/partida** aos cemitérios |
| Evacuações por jogador | **0,364** (previsão do spec: ~0,3, declaradamente enviesada para baixo) |
| Censo de conservação · `AcaoInvalida` · `Error` cru · teto de ações | **zero** em cada braço |

⚠️ Isto mede a **margem** da evacuação sobre uma punição leve — **não** o valor do Bad Stuff contra zero.

🔴 **A resposta honesta à pergunta da fatia: a evacuação NÃO conserta a economia sozinha.** ~90% das partidas ainda esgotam Tesouros. O spec previu isso por escrito — a **#40** segue sendo a resposta estrutural, e os consumíveis do **2b** seguem com trabalho.

## O que a execução pegou, e vale mais que os números

🔑 **O soak achou dois bugs reais que 730 testes e sete revisões não pegaram**, os dois nascidos nesta fatia, em `comprarMaoInicial`:

1. **Perda de carta.** A mão era *substituída*, e quem evacua mantém a patente — logo continua alvo legítimo de caridade enquanto espera a vez. A carta doada nesse intervalo sumia de todas as zonas, sem cemitério, sem evento, sem log. **35 de 240 partidas, 81 cartas.** Pego pelo **censo de conservação**.
2. **500 em produção.** O recomeço não tratava Tesouros esgotado, enquanto o `sacarTesouros` trata. Com 90–97% das partidas esgotando, a conjunção é caminho real: **1 em 240**.

Consertados e re-medidos: censo **0/240**, `Error` cru **0/240**.

🔑 **A revisão ampla do branch achou o que as 10 revisões por task não podiam** — terceira fatia seguida. Apagar `eventos.push(...efeito.eventos)` deixava **732/732 verdes**: o jogador perdia tudo, o censo ficava verde, e **o log não dizia uma palavra**. As duas pontas provadas, o fio no meio não.

## Documentação

O `CLAUDE.md` raiz foi refatorado nesta branch: **2.396 linhas / 193 KB → 290 / 19 KB**. O diário foi para `docs/historico/` (verbatim), e nasceram `docs/licoes-aprendidas.md`, `docs/divida-tecnica.md` e um `CLAUDE.md` por pacote.

⚠️ **A branch carrega 40 commits**, não só os 26 da fatia — vêm junto as decisões da esquiva (#105–#109), a decomposição do bloco 2 (#110–#113), o spec e o plano. **Tudo docs; zero código fora da fatia.**

## 🔴 O gate ocular está PENDENTE

Nenhum item conferido. O roteiro tem 6 itens em `docs/historico/2026-08-09-bad-stuff-e-evacuacao.md`, com a frequência esperada em cada linha e dois marcados **de sonda, não de olho**.

✅ **Exercitado por e2e em processo** (Fastify real via HTTP): catálogo com `badStuff` → equipar/guardar → porta → Ogro → derrota → `evacuou` com `daMao` como número → recompra 4+4 em `recompor` com a patente mantida.

## 1. The "black border" was the browser's, not ours

`TypePicker`'s four group headers (เบิกได้บ่อย / เหตุการณ์สำคัญ / เครื่องแต่งกาย / อื่นๆ) are bare `<button>`s, and this project ships **no Tailwind preflight** — so they kept the UA's own button chrome. Measured before the fix:

An actual black bevel around every group. ## 2. Renamed คำขอ → คำขอเงินพิเศษ

Both tabs are claims for extra pay (OT hours, welfare/special money), so the bare "คำขอ" didn't distinguish this page from `/leave` or the ขอแก้ไขเวลา flow — which are also คำขอ.

That's three restatements of the same facts in one card. Fixing it properly means deciding what the expanded row is *for* — I'd argue it should carry only what the collapsed row can't (the rejection reason, the evidence, the payout period) and drop the rest — but that's a content decision I shouldn't make unilaterally at 05:40.

**OT mobile card structure.** Also real: the `×` button floats mid-card against a block of empty space, `เวลาจริง / จ่ายได้` prints `0 นาที` twice, and the layout doesn't match the welfare card's. Same reason.

Every top-level declaration in a `.d.ts` file is implicitly ambient, so a variable initializer there is an ambient-initializer grammar error even without an explicit `declare` keyword: **when a `.d.ts` file has a top-level variable declaration with an initializer, tsc reports TS1039 (or TS1254 for a bare `const` with a non-literal initializer); tsz now does the same through `CheckerState::is_ambient_declaration` in `state/variable_checking/core.rs`.**

`variable_checking/core.rs` previously gated the TS1039/TS1254 check on `arena.is_in_ambient_context`, which only checks for an explicit `declare`-keyword ancestor. Its own comment claimed *"TSC does not emit TS1039 for variable initializers in .d.ts files"* — false per the pinned oracle, and exactly the false-negative filed in #17086 with a repro table. The fix swaps in `self.is_ambient_declaration(decl_idx)` (`CheckerState`, resolving to `CheckerContext::is_ambient_declaration` = `is_declaration_file() || arena.is_in_ambient_context`), the same helper the adjacent TS1155 check two call sites up in this file already uses — no new logic, just the correct existing gate.

Owner layer: checker only (`state/variable_checking/core.rs`), no parser/emitter changes.

Closes #17086.
